steps.text: In a sauté pan over medium-high heat, brown each side of the chicken in oil — 2–3 minutes per side — then lift it onto a plate. Toss the onion, garlic, oregano, chilli powder, cumin, coriander, salt, and cayenne into the same pan and cook for 2–3 minutes until the air smells peppery.

steps.title: Slow cook
steps.text: Tip the tomatoes and their juice into a slow cooker with the chicken and any pan drippings. Cover and cook on high for 3–4 hours or low for 6–7 hours, until the chicken falls apart. Let it rest 5 minutes, then shred into strips.

steps.title: Thicken sauce
steps.text: Purée the tomato mixture in the slow cooker with a handheld blender — this gives the sauce body. Stir in lime juice and adjust seasoning with salt. Reserve 1 cup sauce separately; toss the shredded chicken with the rest.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Warm the tortillas and pile each with chicken, a spoonful of the reserved sauce, guacamole, and sour cream.

steps.title: Build base
steps.text: Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high. Cook onion until just soft, 2–3 minutes. Stir in garlic, oregano, thyme, red pepper flakes, and bay leaf; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.

steps.title: Slow cook broth
steps.text: Pour the canned tomatoes, clam juice, tomato paste, and white wine into a slow cooker. Add the onion mixture and stir. Cover and cook on low for 4 hours to meld the flavours.

steps.title: Add seafood
steps.text: Gently stir in the grouper, shrimp, and scallops, so they stay whole. Cook on high until the fish is opaque and shrimp are pink, 15–20 minutes.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Off heat, stir in basil and lemon juice. Season. Ladle into bowls and give each a squeeze more lemon if it needs it.

steps.title: Toast rice
steps.text: Sauté diced onion in oil in a saucepan over medium-high heat until softened, then stir in the rice and cook, stirring, until fragrant, 1–2 minutes.

steps.title: Simmer
steps.text: Add broth, coconut milk, sugar, and salt; bring to a boil. Cover, drop the heat to low, and simmer until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed, 15–20 minutes.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Remove from heat and leave it 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork. Stir through the cilantro and lime juice just before serving.

steps.title: Crisp bacon
steps.text: Preheat oven to 325°. Cook the bacon in a Dutch oven until crisp, then lift it onto a paper towel; reserve the fat in the pot.

steps.title: Brown chicken and build sauce
steps.text: Brown the seasoned chicken in 1 tablespoon of the bacon fat, about 8 minutes, and set aside. In the same pot, cook onion, celery, and carrot in 1 tablespoon fat until softened, 3–5 minutes. Stir in tomato paste, thyme, rosemary, and garlic; cook until fragrant, about 1 minute. Dust with flour and cook 1 minute more.

steps.title: Braise chicken
steps.text: Pour in the wine and let it bubble, scraping up the bits on the bottom; reduce to about 2 cups over 10–15 minutes. Return the chicken to the pot, add 2 cups broth and the bay leaf, and bring to a boil. Cover and transfer to the oven for 45 minutes until the chicken is nearly tender.

steps.title: Brown mushrooms
steps.text: While the chicken braises, brown the mushrooms in two batches in 2 tablespoons butter per batch over medium heat, about 10 minutes each. Dust with flour, cook 1 minute, then deglaze with brandy and scrape everything into a saucepan. Add the remaining broth and pearl onions; transfer all to the Dutch oven and return to the oven for 15 minutes more.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Transfer chicken, mushrooms, and onions to a plate. Reduce the sauce in the pot over medium until thickened, 5 minutes. When cool enough, debone the chicken if you like, then return it with the vegetables to the sauce. Top with bacon crumbles and parsley.

steps.title: Crisp crowns
steps.text: Preheat oven to 425°. Cook the Crispy Crowns according to the packet, then season with salt and pepper. Whisk together mayonnaise, hot sauce, and garlic; pour into a squeeze bottle for easy drizzling.

steps.title: Cook fillings
steps.text: Heat oil in a sauté pan over high and brown the ham until it begins to colour, 3–4 minutes; transfer to a paper towel. Add mushrooms, bell pepper, and onion to the same pan; cook until tender and the moisture evaporates, 5 minutes. Stir in the ham and season with salt and pepper.

steps.title: Scramble eggs
steps.text: Season eggs and milk together, then whisk until combined. While butter foams in a nonstick skillet over medium heat, pour in the eggs and scramble them gently, never stopping the motion of the spoon, until they are nearly set. Slide them into a bowl.

steps.title: Assemble and bake
steps.text: Layer half the Crispy Crowns into an ovenproof dish, then drizzle with one third of the sauce. Top with half each of the ham mixture, eggs, and cheese. Bake for 3 minutes until the cheese melts. Add the remaining Crispy Crowns, drizzle with another third of sauce, and top with the remaining ham mixture, eggs, and cheese. Bake until this layer melts and bubbles, 3 minutes. Finish with the last of the sauce and sliced scallions.

steps.title: Make sauce
steps.text: Oven to 450°. Pour oil into a 12-inch ovenproof skillet on medium heat. Once it gets hot, add the Anaheim chiles and onion; let them soften over 5 minutes. Stir in garlic, oregano, cumin, paprika, and salt and cook for 1 minute. Follow with all the tomatoes, beans, tomato sauce, and hot sauce. Let it simmer gently until thickened and reduced, 8–10 minutes.

steps.title: Simmer and bake
steps.text: Make six wells in the sauce by pushing it aside, then crack an egg into each well. Sprinkle cheese around the eggs rather than over them, so it melts into the sauce. Bake until the whites set and the yolks stay soft, 10–12 minutes, or longer if you like them firmer.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Top with fresh cilantro leaves and thin slices of serrano chile.

steps.title: Make paste
steps.text: Pulse scallions, garlic, and ginger in a food processor until minced. Whisk together soy sauce, chilli paste, vinegar, brown sugar, and the minced mixture. Reserve half this paste.

steps.title: Slow cook pork
steps.text: Trim any excess fat from the pork shoulder and cut it into 4–5 equal pieces. Transfer to a slow cooker, pour over half the soy paste and the water, cover, and cook on high for 3–4 hours until the pork falls apart at a fork.

steps.title: Shred and reduce
steps.text: Pull the pork from the cooker onto a plate and shred it with two forks. Strain the cooking liquid, leaving the fat behind, then pour it into a saucepan. Over medium-high heat, let it bubble down until only 1 cup remains, about 10 minutes. Stir the reserved paste into this reduced liquid and heat through, then coat the shredded pork with the sauce.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Pile the pork onto warm tostada shells with pickled vegetables of your choice.

steps.title: Make sauce
steps.text: Work the sausage in a food processor to a loose purée and scrape into a bowl. Now mince the onion and garlic in that same processor. Warm oil in a large skillet over medium-high, add the minced vegetables and Italian herbs, and cook until soft, 2–3 minutes. Stir the tomato paste into this base and cook 2 minutes more. Crumble in the puréed sausage, letting it brown as you break it up, then follow with both tomatoes. Lower the heat to medium-low and let it bubble gently for 15 minutes, crushing any remaining lumps with a potato masher. Taste and adjust seasoning.

steps.title: Cook pasta
steps.text: Preheat oven to 350°. Spread 1 cup sauce over the bottom of a 9×13-inch baking dish. Cook the lasagna sheets in boiling salted water for 5 minutes to soften them; drain and lay them on oiled baking sheets to cool.

steps.title: Fill and roll
steps.text: Pulse the provolone, ricotta, and Parmesan in the food processor until spreadable. Spread ¼ cup of this mixture onto each cooled lasagna sheet. Top each with 5 slices of pepperoni, 1 tablespoon diced bell pepper, 1 teaspoon olives, and 2 tablespoons sauce. Roll up tightly and lay seam-side down in the prepared dish.

steps.title: Bake and finish
steps.text: Top the rolls with the remaining sauce, cover with foil, and bake for 1 hour until bubbling. Remove the foil, scatter additional shredded provolone over the top, and bake for 5 minutes more to melt. Let it rest 15 minutes before serving.

steps.title: Heat and dress
steps.text: Preheat oven to 450° with racks in the top and bottom thirds. Set two baking sheets in the oven to heat. Whisk together sesame oil, tamari, and rice vinegar.

steps.title: Roast vegetables
steps.text: Toss the broccoli florets and mushrooms with ⅓ cup of the dressing and spread on one hot baking sheet. Roast for 10 minutes, stir, then roast until the broccoli is fork-tender, another 10 minutes.

steps.title: Roast shrimp
steps.text: Toss the shrimp with the remaining dressing, salt, and pepper, and spread on the second hot baking sheet. Roast until the shrimp are firm, bright pink, and opaque, about 10 minutes. Combine the shrimp with the vegetables and serve.

steps.title: Pound cutlets
steps.text: Pound the pork pieces with a meat mallet to ½ inch thick and season with salt and pepper. Combine panko and sesame seeds in one shallow dish, whisk eggs in a second, and place flour in a third, all seasoned with salt and pepper.

steps.title: Bread pork
steps.text: Flour each piece and shake it well, then egg, letting it drain, then press it hard into the panko — a slack hand here and the crust comes off in the pan.

steps.title: Make caramel
steps.text: Heat sugar in a skillet over medium until it turns the colour of iced tea, 7–10 minutes — watch it closely. Combine vinegar, lemon juice, soy sauce, and fish sauce in a small bowl, then carefully pour this into the hot caramel, whisking until smooth.

steps.title: Finish sauce
steps.text: Scatter the shallots, garlic, ginger, and serrano into the pan and raise the heat to medium-high. Simmer until the sauce thickens and has lost half its volume, about 5 minutes. Pass it through a fine-mesh sieve to strain out the solids, return it to the skillet, and hold it warm over low heat.

steps.title: Sauté cutlets
steps.text: In a sauté pan over medium-high, warm the oil until it shimmers. Cook the breaded pork, turning once, until both sides are golden and a thermometer inserted in the middle reads 145°, 5–6 minutes altogether. Plate and drizzle with the warm caramel sauce.

steps.title: Start grits
steps.text: Heat milk, broth, and 1 teaspoon salt in a saucepan to a boil over high. Whisk in the grits in a steady stream, stirring constantly to avoid lumps. Reduce heat to medium-low and cook according to package directions. Stir in corn, bell peppers, and jalapeño; cook 3 minutes more. Season with salt and pepper and reduce heat to low. Meanwhile, bring water and vinegar to a gentle simmer in another pan for poaching the eggs.

steps.title: Cook ham and tomatoes
steps.text: Heat oil in a skillet over medium-high. Add the tomatoes and ham; sauté until the ham begins to brown, 2 minutes. Off the heat, stir in the cilantro and season with salt and pepper.

steps.title: Poach eggs
steps.text: Slide each egg gently from its ramekin into the simmering water, working one at a time. Poach until the whites are just set and the yolks are still soft, 3–5 minutes depending on how you like them.

steps.title: Assemble
steps.text: Spoon the grits across four plates, then crown each mound with a poached egg, a quarter of the tomato mixture, and a scatter of feta crumbles.

steps.title: Toast fideos
steps.text: Preheat oven to 375° and coat a baking sheet with nonstick spray. Spread the fideos on the sheet and toast until golden brown, 4–5 minutes.

steps.title: Build soup
steps.text: Sauté the onions and garlic in oil in a large pot over medium-high heat until softened, 2–3 minutes. Add broth and fire-roasted tomatoes; bring to a boil. Stir in the shredded turkey meat, tomato sauce, chipotle in adobo, oregano, coriander, and toasted fideos. Simmer until the pasta is tender, about 5 minutes. Taste and season with salt and pepper.

steps.title: Make relish
steps.text: Pulse the bell peppers, onion, cilantro, jalapeño, and garlic in a food processor until minced, scraping the bowl down as needed.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Ladle the soup into bowls and top each with a spoonful of relish, a handful of pepper Jack cheese, a dollop of sour cream, and a lime wedge.

steps.title: Form meatballs
steps.text: Oven to 400°. Mix onion, half-and-half, cornstarch, egg, salt, nutmeg, allspice, and pepper with the meatloaf mix. Shape 30 balls (1½ inches each) on a parchment-lined baking sheet.

steps.title: Brown in batches
steps.text: Heat butter and oil in a skillet over medium. Add meatballs in two batches, browning about 2 minutes per side — don't cook them through, they finish in the oven. Transfer to a Dutch oven.

steps.title: Deglaze and simmer
steps.text: Deglaze the skillet with 3½ cups broth, scraping up brown bits. Stir in beef base and bring to a simmer.

steps.title: Thicken the gravy
steps.text: Whisk flour and Kitchen Bouquet smooth with the remaining ½ cup broth. Stir into the gravy, stirring constantly, and simmer 5 minutes until thickened. Season with salt and pepper.

steps.title: Braise until done
steps.text: Pour the gravy over the meatballs, cover the Dutch oven, and transfer to the oven. Braise for 35–40 minutes until cooked through.

steps.title: Oven and season steaks
steps.text: Oven to 375°. Arrange cauliflower steaks on a baking sheet, drizzle with oil, and season with salt.

steps.title: Roast cauliflower
steps.text: Roast for about 25 minutes until fork-tender.

steps.title: Build caponata
steps.text: Sweat currants, garlic, pepper flakes, and anchovy paste in oil in a pan over medium-low heat until the currants soften, about 2 minutes. Stir in roasted peppers, vinegar, and capers; simmer 4 minutes.

steps.title: Finish and serve
steps.text: Stir in pine nuts and season with salt. Serve the caponata over the cauliflower steaks and garnish with fresh mint.

steps.title: Render bacon
steps.text: Render bacon in a skillet until crisp; transfer to a paper-towel-lined plate.

steps.title: Sear brisket
steps.text: Sear the brisket in the bacon fat over high heat until browned, 5–7 minutes per side. Set aside.

steps.title: Build the braise
steps.text: In the same skillet over medium-high, cook onion, celery, garlic, and tomato paste for 2 minutes. Deglaze with apple juice and reduce by half (3 minutes). Transfer to a 6- to 8-qt. slow cooker and add cider and maple syrup.

steps.title: Cook on high
steps.text: Place the brisket in the slow cooker, cover, and cook on high for 4½ hours. Add parsnips, apples, and potato; cook 1 hour more until fork-tender.

steps.title: Make mash
steps.text: Set the brisket aside under foil. Put the cooked parsnips, apples, and potato (discard the remaining solids) into a food processor and add butter, thyme, and rosemary. Pulse until smooth, then season with salt and pepper.

steps.title: Reduce, thicken, serve
steps.text: Strain the braising liquid into a saucepan and reduce to 2 cups (11–12 minutes). Whisk cornstarch, vinegar, and water together, then stir into the sauce. Boil 1 minute, season with salt and pepper. Top the mash with bacon and serve with the sauce.

steps.title: Layer and season
steps.text: Put the onions and bay leaf in the bottom of a 4- to 6-qt. slow cooker, then add thyme, salt, and pepper.

steps.title: Build the soup
steps.text: Pour the beef stock, brandy, and melted butter over the onions. Cover and cook on high for 5–6 hours or low for 6–7 hours until the onions are very tender.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Season with salt and pepper before serving.

steps.title: Brown the meat
steps.text: Brown the ground sirloin in a large skillet over medium-high heat until cooked through.

steps.title: Cook vegetables
steps.text: Stir in onion, bell pepper, and celery; cook until soft, about 10 minutes. Drain in a colander.

steps.title: Slow-cook the filling
steps.text: Transfer to a 4- to 6-qt. slow cooker and add ketchup, relish, Worcestershire, and tomato paste. Stir to combine, cover, and cook on high for 2–3 hours or low for 4–5 hours.

steps.title: Season and serve
steps.text: Season with salt and pepper. Serve on ciabatta bread.

steps.title: Cook potatoes and eggs
steps.text: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil, then add the potatoes and eggs. Cook for 12–15 minutes until the potatoes are fork-tender.

steps.title: Prep ingredients
steps.text: Drain the potatoes and let them cool for 15 minutes — they absorb the vinegar better slightly warm. Toss with vinegar, then peel and quarter the eggs.

steps.title: Combine salad
steps.text: Whisk mayonnaise and Dijon together. Add to the potatoes along with the eggs, celery, and scallions; mix gently. Season with salt and pepper and chill until ready to serve.

steps.title: Make the rub
steps.text: Combine sugar, salt, paprika, five-spice powder, black pepper, and cayenne in a small bowl.

steps.title: Season and slow-cook
steps.text: Cut the rib rack in half. Rub the spice mixture all over the ribs. Pour ½ cup soy sauce into a 4- to 6-qt. slow cooker, arrange the ribs inside. Cover and cook on high 1 hour to build flavour, then reduce to low and cook 2 more hours until the meat shrinks about ½ inch from the bones.

steps.title: Make the glaze
steps.text: Whisk together sugar, the remaining ¼ cup soy sauce, ketchup, vinegar, chili garlic sauce, ginger, and five-spice powder in a saucepan over medium-high heat. Simmer 5 minutes to dissolve the sugar, then reserve ⅓ cup for dipping.

steps.title: Broil ribs
steps.text: Get the broiler to high, 6 inches from the element. Oil a broiler pan and lay the ribs on it, meaty side up. Glaze and broil 3 minutes, then repeat the glaze-and-broil twice more, until the ribs begin to brown in spots.

steps.title: Rest and serve
steps.text: Cool the ribs to room temperature (at least 5 minutes). Slice vertically between the bones to separate individual ribs, then serve alongside the reserved glaze.

steps.title: Oven and prep bacon
steps.text: Get the oven to 400°. Render the bacon in a 10-inch ovenproof nonstick skillet until it's crisp, then transfer it to paper towels but save 1 Tbsp. of the fat in the pan.

steps.title: Mix egg filling
steps.text: Whisk together eggs, cream, cream cheese, ½ cup each of Emmental and Cheddar, Parmesan, scallions, salt, cayenne, and black pepper. Stir in spinach and bacon.

steps.title: Build the base
steps.text: Combine the butter with the drippings and melt over medium-high heat. Add the hash browns, press them up the sides, and season with salt and pepper. Lower the heat to medium and cook until the edges crisp, about 10 minutes.

steps.title: Add egg and cheese
steps.text: Sprinkle the remaining cheeses over the hash browns, then pour the egg mixture over top.

steps.title: Bake and finish
steps.text: Bake for 30–35 minutes until the filling is set and a knife tip comes out clean when inserted near the center. Rest 5 minutes, loosen the edges with a spatula, flip it onto a plate, then flip it once more onto the serving dish.

steps.title: Cook and glaze bacon
steps.text: Cook bacon in a nonstick skillet until crisp; transfer to a paper-towel-lined plate. Stir brown sugar, chipotle, and vinegar into the skillet and simmer 1 minute. Return bacon to the skillet to coat in the glaze.

steps.title: Make salsa
steps.text: Combine tomatoes, avocado, scallions, cilantro, mayonnaise, and lime juice in a bowl; season with salt and pepper.

steps.title: Assemble sandwiches
steps.text: In the same skillet or a clean one, cook eggs in butter over medium until the whites are set; season with salt and pepper. Break the yolks, flip, and cook 1 minute more. Top with Pepper Jack cheese, cover, and let melt 1 minute. Assemble the bacon, eggs, and salsa on toasted kaiser rolls.

steps.title: Build the base
steps.text: Simmer the broth, potatoes, onion, carrot, salt, pepper, and nutmeg in a pot for 15 minutes.

steps.title: Make roux
steps.text: Over low heat in a saucepan, melt the butter and whisk the flour into it until smooth — this thickens without lumps.

steps.title: Add milk
steps.text: Whisk milk into the butter mixture, stirring to prevent lumps; cook 2 minutes. Stir this into the soup base.

steps.title: Add greens and shrimp
steps.text: Add spinach and shrimp; simmer until the spinach wilts and the shrimp cooks through, about 3 minutes.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Off the heat, stir in cream and lemon zest. Season with Tabasco and salt.

steps.title: Prepare noodles
steps.text: Cover the ramen with boiling water and soak, covered, for 2 minutes. Drain and dry in a salad spinner, then chill on a baking sheet — cold noodles fry better.

steps.title: Make sauce
steps.text: Whisk together soy sauce, oyster sauce, and white pepper in a bowl.

steps.title: Build aromatics
steps.text: In a wok or large nonstick skillet, soften the scallion whites, ginger, garlic, and jalapeño in 3 tsp. oil over medium-low heat for 3 minutes; they should look translucent. Move them to a bowl.

steps.title: Cook eggs and mushrooms
steps.text: Scramble the eggs gently in 2 tsp. oil until just set (1 minute), then move to a plate and chop once they're cool. Clean the wok, add 3 tsp. oil on high heat, and brown the shiitakes (about 3 minutes). Combine them with the aromatics in the bowl.

steps.title: Fry the noodles
steps.text: Wipe the wok, add the remaining 3 tsp. oil and heat until shimmering. Add the ramen and stir-fry until lightly browned, 2–3 minutes.

steps.title: Toss to finish
steps.text: Add peas, the aromatic-mushroom mixture, and eggs; toss to heat through. Off heat, add the sauce and scallion greens, toss to coat.

steps.title: Season the brisket
steps.text: Make a rub: combine Italian seasoning, salt, oregano, garlic, thyme, and pepper in a small bowl. Coat both sides of the brisket evenly.

steps.title: Sear and transfer
steps.text: Heat oil in a skillet over medium-high. Sear the brisket 5 minutes per side, then transfer to a 4- to 6-qt. slow cooker. Add pepperoncini and juice, ale, broth, and Worcestershire.

steps.title: Slow-cook
steps.text: Cover and cook on high for 4–5 hours or low for 8–9 hours — the long braise makes the brisket tender. Remove the meat and shred it.

steps.title: Strain and reserve
steps.text: Strain the liquid into a bowl and reserve the pepperoncini for serving.

steps.title: Assemble sandwiches
steps.text: Divide the shredded meat among the toasted kaiser rolls and top with pepperoncini and provolone. Use the reserved liquid as a dipping sauce.

steps.title: Brine the chops
steps.text: Submerge pork chops in pickle brine, cover, and refrigerate 4 hours or overnight, turning occasionally — the brine keeps the meat moist and seasoned through.

steps.title: Prepare the relish
steps.text: Grill a whole garlic bulb in foil until soft, 15–20 minutes. Grill an Anaheim chile covered until charred, 5–7 minutes; let steam 5 minutes under plastic wrap, then peel and chop. Grill red onion slices 3–5 minutes per side. Mince 1 Tbsp. of the roasted garlic and whisk it with mustard, honey, and dill. Fold in the chopped chile, onion, and tomatoes; season with salt and pepper.

steps.title: Grill to temperature
steps.text: Pat chops dry and season with pepper. Grill over medium-high heat until an instant-read thermometer at the bone reads 145°, about 3–4 minutes per side.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Serve chops topped with the relish.

steps.title: Make the dough
steps.text: Heat milk, sugar, and salt until the sugar dissolves; cool to 100°. Mix flour and yeast in a stand mixer's bowl, then add egg, yolk, and milk. Knead on medium-low with the dough hook until springs back when pressed, about 4–5 minutes. Add softened butter 1 Tbsp. at a time, scraping the bowl between each addition. Cover and let rise in a warm place until doubled, about 2 hours. Chill overnight — this keeps the dough stable for braiding.

steps.title: Make the filling
steps.text: Mince dried cherries in a food processor, then add the thawed cherries and pulse until roughly chopped. Transfer to a pan, add sugar, cornstarch, and vanilla bean paste, and simmer over medium heat until thick, about 1 minute. Chill completely.

steps.title: Shape and braid
steps.text: Lightly flour a sheet of parchment and roll your dough to 12×16 inches. Using a knife, cut ½-inch strips from the outer thirds at a 45-degree angle. Down the middle, lay the Brie slices with 2 inches of bare dough at top and bottom; spread the chilled filling on top. Fold the flaps over the ends, then weave the strips across in a braid. Let it rise covered until puffy, about 2 hours.

steps.title: Bake and glaze
steps.text: Heat oven to 350°. Brush braid with egg wash, sprinkle with almonds, and bake until golden, about 30 minutes. Whisk powdered sugar and milk; drizzle over the braid after cooling 10 minutes. Cool 30 minutes more before serving.

steps.title: Prepare the chorizo sauce
steps.text: Work the ground pork through a food processor until it breaks into paste — this texture takes on the spices better. In a hot pan with oil, add the pork and all spices — paprika, garlic, oregano, coriander, cumin — crushing it with a potato masher as it cooks through, 3–5 minutes. Purée salsa with chipotle and broth, stir it in, and simmer until thick, roughly 15 minutes. Fold in drained beans and cilantro; season with salt and pepper.

steps.title: Assemble and bake
steps.text: Set oven to 350°. In a 2-quart casserole, layer—starting with one-third of the tortilla chips, then one-third of the cheese mixture, then repeat twice more, ending with cheese. Bake until the cheese melts and everything is hot, roughly 15 minutes.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Top with sliced radishes and cilantro sprigs.

steps.title: Season the pork
steps.text: Mash garlic with salt to a paste — it won't burn like raw garlic would — then work in brown sugar, rum, orange zest, cumin, and coriander. Rub this paste all over a 1¼ lb pork tenderloin that you have already seasoned with salt and pepper.

steps.title: Prepare vegetables
steps.text: Combine olive oil, rum, orange juice, salt, pepper, and cumin; toss with cubed sweet potatoes and red onion wedges.

steps.title: Sear and roast
steps.text: In a hot 10-inch cast-iron skillet over medium-high, sear the seasoned pork on one side until golden, then flip. Arrange the dressed potatoes and onion around it. Roast in a 475° oven until an instant-read thermometer at the thickest part reaches 145–150°, with the vegetables fork-tender — 12–15 minutes all told. Let rest 5 minutes, then slice and serve.

steps.title: Prepare tofu
steps.text: Blot a 14 oz. block of firm tofu dry and cut into 1×2-inch strips. Toss with 1 Tbsp. cornstarch, salt, and pepper.

steps.title: Cook tofu and vegetables
steps.text: Set a wok over high heat with 1 Tbsp. sesame oil. Fry tofu in batches until golden on both sides, about 2 minutes per side — batches keep the oil hot enough to crisp the surface — drain on paper towels. In the same wok, stir-fry roll-cut carrots and onion wedges for 3 minutes. Add broccolini florets and stir-fry 3 minutes. Toss in scallion whites, minced garlic, and ginger; stir-fry 2 minutes.

steps.title: Finish with sauce
steps.text: Whisk vegetable broth, soy sauce, lemon juice, sambal oelek, and 1 Tbsp. cornstarch together. Return tofu to the wok, add the broth mixture, and stir to coat. Add scallion greens and cilantro. Serve over jasmine rice.

steps.title: Pickle onions and jalapeños
steps.text: Whisk ⅓ cup lime juice with sugar and salt; heat in a microwave 20 seconds until sugar dissolves. Add thinly sliced red onion and jalapeño; let stand 30 minutes, stirring occasionally.

steps.title: Marinate chicken
steps.text: Purée fresh orange juice, ⅓ cup lime juice, achiote paste, minced garlic, and honey. Add chicken breasts, cover, and marinate in the refrigerator 20 minutes — achiote is potent, so brief is enough.

steps.title: Sear and reduce
steps.text: Remove chicken from marinade and reserve the marinade. Pat chicken dry, season with salt and pepper, and sauté in olive oil over medium-high until cooked through, about 5 minutes per side. Transfer to a plate. Add the reserved marinade to the pan, bring to a boil, then reduce heat to medium-low and simmer until slightly thick, about 3 minutes. Season the sauce with salt and pepper.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Plate the chicken with sauce and the pickled onions and jalapeños.

steps.title: Prepare bacon
steps.text: Preheat to 450°. Arrange bacon strips to line the bottom and up the sides of an 8-inch cast-iron skillet, leaving about a third of each strip overhanging the rim. Scatter the minced fresh thyme over the bacon.

steps.title: Layer vegetables and cheese
steps.text: Layer half the thinly sliced potatoes on the bacon, then sprinkle ¼ cup shaved Gruyère and season with salt and pepper. Add the shredded chicken and another ¼ cup Gruyère. Continue with the sliced leeks, minced garlic, the remaining potato slices, salt, pepper, and the last ¼ cup Gruyère — potatoes go on the edges so they get more heat.

steps.title: Cook and roast
steps.text: Fold the overhanging bacon to the centre, creating a top seal. Set the skillet on a stovetop over medium and cook 10 minutes. Cover with foil, transfer to the oven, and roast 30 minutes. Uncover and roast until the bacon crisps and potatoes are tender, another 30 minutes. Let rest 10 minutes; pour off drippings and loosen the edges before serving.

steps.title: Prepare ingredients
steps.text: Thaw two 10 oz. packages of frozen chopped spinach and squeeze out excess moisture — dry spinach keeps the dip from becoming watery. Have ready toasted pine nuts, kalamata olives, fresh thyme, and roast red pepper pieces.

steps.title: Mix and heat
steps.text: Whisk together half-and-half, garlic cooking cream, grated onion, crumbled feta, toasted pine nuts, fresh lemon juice, salt, dill, black pepper, nutmeg, and cayenne in a large bowl. Stir in the thawed spinach. Transfer to a 1.5 qt. slow cooker and cover.

steps.title: Cook and serve
steps.text: Cook in a slow cooker on high for 1½ hours. Transfer to phyllo shells or serve alongside pita chips. Finish with scattered olives, pine nuts, thyme, and roast pepper pieces.

steps.title: Crisp the bacon
steps.text: Cook diced thick-sliced bacon in a pan until it's crisp; transfer to a paper-towel-lined plate and keep the drippings in the pan.

steps.title: Make the sauce
steps.text: Heat the same pan over medium-high. Whisk salsa with adobo sauce and cumin, scraping up any browned bits — they carry all the flavour from the bacon. While that happens, set a baking sheet with two 6-inch cast-iron skillets into a 350° oven to preheat.

steps.title: Bake with toppings
steps.text: Grease the hot skillets generously with the bacon drippings. Divide diced avocado and the salsa mixture between them; crack two eggs into each and bake until the whites just set, 15–20 minutes. Top with the cooked bacon and cilantro.

steps.title: Make béchamel
steps.text: In a large pan over medium, melt the butter, then work in the flour and cook for 2 minutes. Add the milk and nutmeg in a slow stream while whisking, bring to a simmer, and cook 2 minutes more. Off heat, stir in ½ cup pesto — heat dulls basil — and season with salt and pepper.

steps.title: Make ricotta mixture
steps.text: Stir ricotta, Parmesan, and ½ cup pesto together; season with salt and pepper.

steps.title: Layer and bake
steps.text: Into a 9×13-inch baking dish, spread ⅔ cup béchamel. Lay 3 no-boil sheets across it. Top with ½ cup ricotta mixture, ¾ cup chicken, ⅔ cup béchamel, and ¾ cup mozzarella. Repeat this sequence three more times, finishing the final layer with 1½ cups mozzarella. Cover with foil and bake at 350° until bubbly, 45 minutes. Uncover, bake 15 minutes more, then broil until golden, 2–3 minutes. Rest 15 minutes before serving.

steps.title: Build the bed
steps.text: Set oven to 350° with the rack in the lower third. Chop onions, carrots, and celery, then scatter them in the bottom of a Dutch oven with bay leaves.

steps.title: Truss the bird
steps.text: Inside the chicken cavity, pack parsley and dill sprigs. Tie the legs together with kitchen string, then season the whole bird inside and out with salt and pepper.

steps.title: Into the pot
steps.text: Set the trimmed chicken fat and neck alongside the bird in the pot. Brush the top with butter, cover, and roast for an hour, basting twice from the liquid below. Uncover and continue roasting until the thigh reaches 165° on a thermometer — the skin should be golden, another 50 minutes or so.

steps.title: Rest and portion
steps.text: Pull the chicken from the pot to a plate and let it rest under foil. Fish out herb sprigs from the pot and discard them. Cut the cooled bird into eight pieces.

steps.title: Sauce from drippings
steps.text: Pour the drippings into the pot, then boil over high heat until reduced by half, about 5 to 6 minutes. Add Madeira and reduce by half again. Pour in broth and reduce until you have about 1 cup of strained drippings — strain to remove solids. Degrease the liquid, then whisk together with enough broth to make 1½ cups and cornstarch in a saucepan over medium heat until thickened. Whisk in minced dill and red wine vinegar, season with salt, and serve with the chicken.

steps.title: Start with bacon
steps.text: Set the oven to 425°. Cut bacon into strips and cook them in a large cast-iron skillet until they turn crisp. Move to a paper towel and pour off all but 2 Tbsp. of the fat from the pan.

steps.title: Vegetables in the pan
steps.text: Halve the Brussels sprouts and dice the butternut squash and red onion. Toss all three with the bacon fat you left behind, season with salt and pepper, lay them flat in the skillet, and transfer to the oven. Roast until they give way to a fork, roughly 20 minutes — stir halfway through.

steps.title: Pasta water matters
steps.text: Get salted water boiling in a pot and follow the package timing for the orecchiette. Scoop out and reserve 1 cup of the cooking liquid, then drain the pasta.

steps.title: Toss and taste
steps.text: Combine the drained pasta, bacon pieces, Parmesan, and fresh sage with the roasted vegetables in the skillet. Use some of the reserved pasta water to loosen it to your liking. Adjust the seasoning, then drizzle with balsamic vinegar and olive oil, and finish with more Parmesan.

steps.title: Toast and spread
steps.text: Heat the oven to 400°. Split the ciabatta horizontally, brush the cut sides with 2 Tbsp. melted butter, sprinkle with salt and pepper, and toast them on a baking sheet, cut side up, until they are golden — about 10 minutes. While they toast, mix softened goat cheese with lemon juice and zest.

steps.title: Cook the proteins
steps.text: Sear the Canadian bacon in a nonstick skillet with oil over medium heat until the edges curl, 1 to 2 minutes per side (3 to 4 if the slices are thick). Set aside on a plate. In the same skillet, boil ½ cup water, add asparagus, and simmer until the water disappears, 3 to 5 minutes.

steps.title: Eggs go in next
steps.text: Whisk 8 eggs with ¼ cup half-and-half and season with salt and pepper. Melt the remaining 2 Tbsp. butter in the skillet and scramble the eggs over medium heat until they are nearly set.

steps.title: Layer and finish
steps.text: Spread the goat cheese mixture on the toasted ciabatta. Layer eggs, two slices of bacon, asparagus, and fresh thyme on each half. Put the sandwiches in the oven for 5 minutes, then slice diagonally and serve.

steps.title: Combine the pasta
steps.text: Boil the pasta in salted water according to package directions, then drain. Combine with the tuna, pesto, chopped sun-dried tomatoes, pepper flakes, lemon zest, and lemon juice. Season with salt and pepper.

steps.title: Cook the roux
steps.text: Melt butter over medium-high heat in a saucepan. Add minced onion and cook until soft, about 3 minutes. Whisk in flour and cook 1 minute.

steps.title: Build the cream
steps.text: Pour in milk gradually while whisking constantly, simmer until the sauce is thick and smooth, 3 to 5 minutes. Add shredded Asiago and ¼ cup Parmesan and let them melt, stirring to combine. Stir in spinach and toasted almonds and cook until the spinach wilts. Season with nutmeg, salt, and pepper.

steps.title: Bake and broil
steps.text: Heat oven to 375° and coat a 2 qt. baking dish with nonstick spray. Spread the tuna mixture in the dish, pour the cream sauce over it, and sprinkle with the remaining ¼ cup Parmesan. Bake until the top bubbles, about 15 minutes. Switch on the broiler to high with the rack 6 inches away and broil until the top browns, 3 to 4 minutes.

steps.title: Make the marinade
steps.text: Dissolve ½ cup kosher salt in 2 cups boiling water, then add tequila, Triple Sec, ½ cup lime juice, and ice. Pour this brine into a resealable bag with the trimmed wings and chill for at least 3 hours or overnight.

steps.title: Lime crema
steps.text: Whisk together crema or sour cream with 1 Tbsp. lime juice, minced cilantro, jalapeño, scallions, and lime zest. Season with salt and refrigerate until needed.

steps.title: Warm the sauce
steps.text: Melt butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Stir in hot sauce, agave nectar, and 1½ tsp. lime juice. Season with salt and maintain over low heat.

steps.title: Fry until done
steps.text: Set oven to 300° and line a baking sheet with foil. Get oil to 360° in a cast-iron skillet over medium-high. From the brine, remove and dry the wings thoroughly. Fry in batches of about 10 until golden brown, 4 to 5 minutes per batch. Toss each batch in the warm sauce, then set on the baking sheet to keep warm in the oven until all are done. Serve alongside the lime crema.

steps.title: Prep poblanos and jerky
steps.text: Set oven to 350°. Char poblano chiles directly over a gas flame or under the broiler until blackened all over. Transfer to a bowl, cover with plastic wrap to steam, then peel, seed, and chop once they are cool. Spread jerky on a baking sheet and roast until darkened and flexible, about 5 minutes. Pulse in a food processor until minced.

steps.title: Sauté the filling
steps.text: Cook chopped onion and garlic in olive oil over medium-high heat in a sauté pan until soft, 3 minutes. Stir in diced tomatoes and let them cook down until the liquid thickens, 7 to 10 minutes. Add the chopped poblanos and minced jerky to combine.

steps.title: Roll and deep-fry
steps.text: Lay out a flour tortilla and place roughly ½ cup filling in the center, top with ½ cup cheese, then fold in the sides and roll away from you, tucking as you go. Repeat for all four. Heat safflower oil in a sauté pan to 365° over medium-high. Fry each chimichanga seam side down first until the exterior is golden brown all over, about 10 minutes total. Drain on paper towels before serving.

steps.title: Spice coating
steps.text: Mix turmeric, cumin, cinnamon, and red pepper flakes. Cube the chicken breasts, season with salt and pepper, and coat thoroughly with the spice blend.

steps.title: Sear and sweat
steps.text: Heat oil in a sauté pan over medium-high until shimmering. Brown the chicken on all sides, 3 to 4 minutes. Add onion, garlic, and ginger to the pan and let them soften, 2 to 3 minutes.

steps.title: Braise until tender
steps.text: Pour in tomatoes and coconut milk, scraping the browned bits from the bottom. Reduce heat to medium-low and simmer until the chicken is tender and the sauce clings to the back of a spoon, about 6 minutes. Take off the heat and fold in spinach and lime juice. Taste and season with salt and pepper.

steps.title: Pasta and water
steps.text: Cook the farfalle according to package directions in boiling salted water. Before draining, transfer ½ cup of the cooking liquid to a cup, then drain the pasta.

steps.title: Crisp and deglaze
steps.text: Warm olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add the diced prosciutto and let it render until crisp, 3 to 4 minutes, then move to a paper towel. Add minced garlic to the pan and cook until the aroma rises, about 1 minute. Pour wine in to deglaze, scraping the browned bits from the bottom, and cook until nearly dry.

steps.title: Cream and finish
steps.text: Stir in mascarpone with the reserved pasta water until smooth. Add fava beans and the drained pasta and heat through, 2 to 3 minutes. Fold in the crisp prosciutto and grated Romano. Season with salt and pepper. Plate and garnish each serving with orange zest and shredded Parmesan.

steps.title: Mince and blend
steps.text: Process yellow onions and garlic in a food processor until very fine. Add ground round and process until it becomes a thick paste.

steps.title: Brown and build
steps.text: Transfer this mixture to a sauté pan over medium-low heat and cook until the meat loses its pink color, then drain and return to the pan. Stir in cocoa, Worcestershire, vinegar, chili powder, tomato paste, sugar, cumin, cinnamon, celery salt, allspice, cayenne, and cloves. Cook for 5 minutes.

steps.title: Simmer down
steps.text: Add water and tomato sauce. Bring to a simmer and cook until the chili thickens slightly, about 25 minutes. Serve on cooked spaghetti topped with Cheddar and chopped red onions.

steps.title: Cook the linguine
steps.text: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and cook linguine according to package directions. Drain when done.

steps.title: Soften the aromatics
steps.text: Work an onion and carrot through a grater. In a large saucepan over medium-high heat, cook these shreds in oil until the pan is dry, 4 to 5 minutes. Stir in tomato paste, minced garlic, pepper flakes, and dried Italian herbs, and cook until aromatic, about 1 minute. Pour in diced tomatoes, tomato sauce, wine, and clam juice, then bring to a boil and simmer for 5 to 7 minutes.

steps.title: Shrimp at the end
steps.text: Drop the shrimp into the sauce, cover the pan, and let them cook over medium heat until they are pink and opaque throughout, 2 to 4 minutes. Taste the sauce and adjust with salt and black pepper. Ladle everything over the cooked pasta and top with shredded fresh basil.

steps.title: Brine the hindquarters
steps.text: Submerge the chicken hindquarters in the liquid from a 16 oz. jar of banana pepper rings. Cover the bowl and refrigerate, turning the chicken occasionally, for 4 hours or overnight.

steps.title: Dredge and brown
steps.text: Set the oven to 400°. Remove the chicken from its brine and dry it thoroughly with paper towels. Sprinkle black pepper on all surfaces. Combine flour and dried thyme, then dredge the chicken to coat completely. Sauté in a sauté pan with hot oil over medium-high until golden on both sides, 8 to 10 minutes.

steps.title: Roast to 165°
steps.text: Transfer the pan to the oven. Roast until the thickest part of the thigh or leg reaches 165° on an instant-read thermometer. Move the chicken to a plate and cover with foil to rest. Put the pan on the stovetop over medium-high heat.

steps.title: Pan sauce with honey
steps.text: Pour broth into the hot pan, scraping up all the brown stuck-on bits. Add minced garlic and honey and simmer until the liquid reduces to about ¼ cup, 3 to 5 minutes. Take off the heat and mount cubes of cold butter one at a time, whisking until the sauce becomes thick and glossy. Serve alongside the chicken.

steps.title: Build the broth
steps.text: Dice onion, celery, and carrot. Sauté in oil over medium-high heat in a saucepan until they soften, 3 to 4 minutes. Add minced garlic and tomato paste and cook 1 minute. Pour in broth with a bay leaf, Worcestershire, and beef base. Bring to a boil, then reduce and simmer until the liquid reduces by half, 10 minutes. Strain to remove solids. Taste and season with salt and pepper, then keep warm.

steps.title: Toast the rolls
steps.text: Heat broiler to high with the rack 6 inches from the element. Line a small baking sheet with foil. Brush hoagie rolls inside and outside with melted butter and sprinkle the tops with coarse salt. Broil until golden on both sides, about 1 minute per side.

steps.title: Build and melt
steps.text: Divide sliced roast beef among the bottom halves of the toasted rolls. Top each with cheese and broil until the cheese bubbles, 2 to 3 minutes. Top each with the other roll half, slice in half, and serve alongside a small cup of the warm jus for dipping.

steps.title: Cook the sausage
steps.text: Brown the bulk sausage in a skillet over medium-high, then move to a paper towel to drain.

steps.title: Warm the sauce
steps.text: In a saucepan over medium heat, combine store-bought salsa with the drained black beans and warm everything through. Add ¼ cup minced fresh cilantro and reduce to low, keeping it hot.

steps.title: Four omelets
steps.text: For each omelet, whisk 3 eggs with 1 Tbsp. sour cream. Pour into a lightly oiled nonstick skillet over medium-high and tilt the pan while pushing cooked edges toward the center until the top is barely set. Fill with one-fourth of the sausage and one-fourth of the pepper Jack cheese, fold, and slide to a plate. Repeat three more times.

steps.title: Plate and serve
steps.text: Spoon one-fourth of the warm sauce onto each serving plate, set an omelet on top, add a dollop of sour cream, and sprinkle with chopped cilantro. Serve immediately.

steps.title: Mix the sausage
steps.text: In a medium bowl, combine ground chicken, grated Pink Lady apple, minced onion, brown sugar, 1 Tbsp. minced parsley, kosher salt, black pepper, and cayenne. Divide into four equal portions.

steps.title: Shape with wells
steps.text: Form each portion into a 1-inch-thick patty. Press a 2-inch-wide well into the center of each patty, leaving a thin base.

steps.title: Cook and egg
steps.text: Warm oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high. Set the patties into the pan well side down and let them brown for 4 minutes, then turn them over. Break an egg into the well in each patty, cover the skillet, and reduce the heat to medium-low. Cook until egg whites set and yolks thicken, about 7 minutes. Serve the boats on toasted ciabatta if you like, garnished with the remaining 2 Tbsp. minced parsley.

steps.title: Cook pasta
steps.text: Boil the farfalle in salted water per package directions. Drain, reserving ½ cup pasta water.

steps.title: Prep peppers
steps.text: Work the orange and yellow peppers through a food processor until they reach a fine mince, then tip into a bowl. Do the same with the Peppadews and add them to the bowl.

steps.title: Sear chicken
steps.text: Heat 2 Tbsp. oil in a sauté pan over medium-high. Sear the seasoned chicken tenders until cooked through, 4 minutes per side; move to a plate.

steps.title: Build the dish
steps.text: Add the remaining 2 Tbsp. oil to the pan. Sauté the peppers and onions with a pinch of salt until they release their juice and it nearly evaporates. Add the snap peas and garlic; cook 1 minute. Stir in the pasta, Peppadew juice, capers, and chicken; bring to a gentle simmer. Loosen with pasta water to your liking and season.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Top each serving with shaved Parmesan and fresh basil.

steps.title: Preheat and plan
steps.text: Set the oven to 450° with racks in the upper and lower thirds so you can roast both the vegetables and lamb simultaneously.

steps.title: Roast vegetables
steps.text: Toss the eggplant and zucchini with 2 tsp. oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a sheet and roast on the lower rack until fork-tender, 15 minutes.

steps.title: Sear and roast lamb
steps.text: Season the lamb chops with oregano, salt, and pepper. Sear them in 2 tsp. oil over high heat until browned on one side, 4 minutes. Flip and transfer the pan to the upper rack. Roast until a thermometer reads 135° for medium-rare, about 4 minutes. Rest on a plate, tented with foil.

steps.title: Make sauce
steps.text: Return the pan to the stove over high heat. Sauté the halved tomatoes and garlic in the pan drippings until the liquid nearly evaporates, about 5 minutes. Blitz this with the yogurt in a mini food processor until smooth.

steps.title: Plate
steps.text: Serve the chops with the warm vegetables and sauce on the side.

steps.title: Pickle cucumbers
steps.text: Whisk the rice vinegar, sugar, and salt in a shallow dish. Add the cucumber ribbons and let them sit 20 minutes, tossing now and then.

steps.title: Make spread
steps.text: Stir the mayonnaise and chili garlic sauce together.

steps.title: Assemble wraps
steps.text: Spread the chili mayo on one half of each tortilla. Layer lettuce, chicken, pickled cucumbers, carrots, and cilantro on top of each. Roll tight like a burrito, fold in the ends, then slice on the bias.

steps.title: Prep the oven and sauce
steps.text: Set the oven to 200° and place wire racks in two baking sheets, lining one with paper towels. Whisk together the mayonnaise, mustard, honey, and vinegar; set the sauce aside.

steps.title: Season chicken
steps.text: Toss the strips with salt, pepper, and Cajun seasoning.

steps.title: Bread the strips
steps.text: Set up three shallow dishes: flour in one, panko in another, and egg whisked with 1 Tbsp. water in the third. Dredge each strip in flour, dip in egg, then coat with panko. Lay on the unlined rack.

steps.title: Deep fry
steps.text: Bring the oil to 350° in a sauté pan. Working in two batches to avoid crowding, fry the strips until golden, turning once or twice as they cook through, 3–4 minutes per batch. Drain each batch on the paper-towel rack; hold all of it warm in the oven.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Plate the strips alongside the sauce.

steps.title: Preheat and coat
steps.text: Set the oven to 400° and coat a baking dish with nonstick spray.

steps.title: Cook spinach base
steps.text: Sauté the shallots and garlic in 2 tsp. oil over medium-high until soft, 2 minutes. Add the spinach and sauté until any liquid evaporates, 1–2 minutes. Whisk the cream and Dijon, then stir into the spinach. Bring to a simmer for 1 minute. Season with salt, pepper, and nutmeg; set aside.

steps.title: Make topping
steps.text: Toss the bread crumbs, Parmesan, and lemon zest with 1 Tbsp. oil until coated.

steps.title: Assemble and bake
steps.text: Place the fish in the prepared dish. Squeeze the lemon half over it and season with salt and pepper. Spread the spinach mixture over each fillet, then top with the bread crumb mixture. Bake until the fish is firm and a thermometer reads 145° in the thickest part, 12–15 minutes.

steps.title: Mix and shape
steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350°. Mix the eggs, minced onion, parsley, Worcestershire, garlic, and crushed crackers. Add the sirloin, salt, and pepper; combine gently. Form into four 8 oz. oval patties.

steps.title: Cook the patties
steps.text: Heat an ovenproof skillet over medium-high and brown the patties on one side. Flip them, move the pan to the oven, and finish to 160° in the centre, 15–20 minutes. Tent loosely with foil to rest.

steps.title: Make gravy
steps.text: Melt the butter in the same pan over medium-high. Add the mushrooms and cook until brown and their moisture has evaporated, 8–10 minutes. Stir in the diced onion and flour; cook 2 minutes. Pour in the broth and simmer until it thickens slightly, about 5 minutes.

steps.title: Plate
steps.text: Spoon the gravy over the steaks and garnish with fresh parsley.

steps.title: Prep grill
steps.text: Heat the grill to high and brush the grate with oil. Soak wooden skewers in water so they don't char.

steps.title: Make dressing
steps.text: Whisk the oregano, lemon zest, lemon juice, oil, parsley, and honey. Season with salt and pepper. Reserve ¼ cup if making a side salad.

steps.title: Thread and season
steps.text: Thread the tuna cubes, onion pieces, and tomatoes onto skewers. Season with salt and pepper.

steps.title: Grill covered
steps.text: Grill the skewers with the lid on for 4 minutes total, flipping once. Transfer to a plate and drizzle with the dressing.

steps.title: Fire up and cook tuna
steps.text: Heat the grill to high and oil the grate. Season the tuna and grill 2–3 minutes per side; let it rest and cool before dicing into ½-inch pieces. Meanwhile, position the broiler rack 5–6 inches from the element and preheat to high.

steps.title: Make aioli
steps.text: Mix the mayonnaise, parsley, garlic, lemon and orange zests, lemon and orange juices, anchovy paste, and pepper flakes; season with salt and pepper. Gently fold in the tuna.

steps.title: Toast bread
steps.text: Brush both sides of the bread with oil and broil until golden, 1½ minutes per side.

steps.title: Assemble and broil
steps.text: Divide the tuna salad between the bread slices. Top each with two tomato slices and ⅓ cup cheese. Broil until the cheese bubbles and begins to brown, 2–3 minutes.

steps.title: Flatten the pork
steps.text: Split the tenderloin into four crosswise portions. Open each piece by cutting horizontally to the edge, then extend the cut partway into each flap so the whole thing spreads open. Pound flat between plastic sheets with a meat mallet to ¼-inch thickness. Season all over with salt and pepper.

steps.title: Set up stations
steps.text: Whisk the eggs, Dijon, and garlic powder in a shallow dish. Put the cracker crumbs in another.

steps.title: Heat oil
steps.text: Pour ¼ inch oil into a large skillet and heat to 350–360°.

steps.title: Bread and fry
steps.text: Get the oil to 350–360° in a large skillet. For each piece: drag it through the egg bath, shake off excess, then coat it all over with cracker crumbs, pressing gently to make them stick. Fry two at a time, turning once, until golden and cooked through, 2–4 minutes per side. Blot on a paper-towel plate before moving to the next batch.

steps.title: Assemble
steps.text: Serve each piece on a Kaiser roll with dill pickle chips, yellow mustard, and onion slices.

steps.title: Make honey mustard
steps.text: Combine both mustards with honey, lemon juice, and garlic powder in a bowl. Keep half this mixture set aside for serving; put the other half in a shallow dish for dipping.

steps.title: Prep the crust
steps.text: Crush the pretzel twists finely with a rolling pin inside a bag, then mix the crumbs with panko in another shallow dish. In a third dish, combine flour, paprika, and black pepper.

steps.title: Coat the chicken
steps.text: Halve the chicken breast lengthwise and season with kosher salt. Dredge each piece in the flour mixture, then dip into the mustard sauce, then press into the pretzel crumb coating.

steps.title: Sear and finish
steps.text: Heat oil in an ovenproof skillet over medium until shimmering. Lay the chicken in the pan and brown it on one side only, about 5 minutes, until the crust is crisp. Flip, transfer the skillet to a 400° oven, and bake until a thermometer reads 165° at the thickest part, 10–15 minutes. Tent with foil and rest 5 minutes before serving with the reserved mustard and lemon wedges.

steps.title: Make the relish
steps.text: Toss together pecans, thinly sliced plum, minced garlic, minced jalapeño, honey, and red wine vinegar. Season with salt and black pepper and set aside.

steps.title: Prepare the stuffing
steps.text: Lay each slice of aged Swiss cheese on a piece of prosciutto and roll up into a packet.

steps.title: Cut the pocket
steps.text: Working with one pork chop at a time, make a 3-inch slit in the side, then slide a knife blade into the opening parallel to the cutting board. Move the blade back and forth gently to create a pocket without breaking through the other side.

steps.title: Stuff and grill
steps.text: Slide a cheese packet into each chop's pocket and season both sides with salt and pepper. Grill over medium heat, covered, until a thermometer inserted near (but not into) the bone reads 145°, about 6–8 minutes per side. Remove from heat, tent with foil, and rest 5 minutes. Serve with the plum relish alongside.

steps.title: Mix the burger
steps.text: Pulse scallions, celery, and lemon zest in a food processor until minced. Add the chopped shrimp and pulse until coarsely chopped. Transfer to a bowl and stir in panko, 2 Tbsp mayonnaise, Old Bay, and ¼ tsp Tabasco. Form two thick patties (¾ inch) and chill for 20–30 minutes.

steps.title: Make remoulade
steps.text: Stir together ½ cup mayonnaise, Dijon mustard, minced shallots, minced dill pickle, and capers. Season with black pepper and Tabasco, then chill.

steps.title: Cook and serve
steps.text: Heat olive oil in a cast-iron skillet over medium-high. Spray the patties lightly with nonstick spray and set them in the pan, covered partially with a lid. Cook 5 minutes per side until golden and firm. Toast the buttered bun halves in the same skillet for about 1 minute. Serve each burger on a bun with red leaf lettuce and a generous dollop of remoulade.

steps.title: Pound the cutlets
steps.text: Starting with the trimmed tenderloin, cross-section it into a dozen pieces. Lay one piece between two sheets of plastic wrap and use the flat face of a meat mallet to strike and flatten it down to ¼ inch — do the same for all pieces. Once they're thin, season both surfaces with salt and black pepper.

steps.title: Brown in batches
steps.text: Divide 3 Tbsp oil among three batches: heat 1 Tbsp in a sauté pan over medium-high per batch, then lay in a cutlet and brown it, 2 minutes on each side. Transfer each batch to a warm baking sheet in a 250° oven.

steps.title: Build the sauce
steps.text: In the same pan, add the diced onions and sliced mushrooms. Sauté until the onions turn translucent and any released moisture cooks away, roughly 5 minutes. Deglaze with the sherry, scraping up the browned bits, and let it reduce until nearly gone. Pour in the broth and diced Black Forest ham, stir in the heavy cream, and simmer until the sauce is reduced by half, about 5 minutes. Season with a crack of black pepper and pour over the rested cutlets.

steps.title: Cook the shells
steps.text: Bring water to a boil and cook the medium shells according to package directions, then drain and rinse under cold water to stop the cooking. Set aside. Preheat the broiler to high with the rack 6 inches from the element, and coat six 6-oz baking dishes with nonstick spray.

steps.title: Make the sauce
steps.text: In a saucepan over medium-low heat, bring the heavy cream and shallots to a gentle steam, stirring in nutmeg. Add the butter and let it melt completely, whisking it in smoothly. Increase heat to medium, add 1½ cups grated Parmesan and 3 Tbsp parsley, then sprinkle in the black pepper. Cook the sauce while whisking often until it thickens, about 10 minutes. Finish with lemon juice and season with salt.

steps.title: Assemble and broil
steps.text: Transfer the sauce to a large bowl and fold in the pasteurized crabmeat and drained pasta until evenly combined. Divide the mixture among the six prepared baking dishes. Toss together the remaining ½ cup Parmesan with panko and scatter this over each dish. Broil until golden and bubbly, 3–4 minutes, then top each casserole with the remaining 1 Tbsp fresh parsley.

steps.title: Brine the ribs
steps.text: Bring 4 qt water to a rolling boil in a large pot. Stir in kosher salt, granulated sugar, smashed garlic cloves, bay leaf, and the reserved lime rinds. Add the ribs (membrane removed and cut into 2-rib pieces) and return to a boil. Drop the heat to medium-low and simmer until the meat has shrunk back from the bones, about 30 minutes, then remove from the brine and pat dry.

steps.title: Build the sauce
steps.text: Heat olive oil in a saucepan over medium until it shimmers, then add the diced yellow onions. Let them cook until translucent, 8–10 minutes. Stir in the ancho chile powder, minced fresh garlic, and tomato paste, cooking for 1 minute to release their flavors. Add the ketchup, ½ cup water, fresh lime juice, Worcestershire sauce, brown sugar, cider vinegar, and fresh orange juice along with lime zest. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low and simmer for 10 minutes. Purée the sauce in a blender until smooth, reserving 1½ cups to serve alongside the ribs.

steps.title: Grill and finish
steps.text: Get the grill to medium heat and oil the grate well. Place the ribs on the hot grate and cook them until the surface blackens, turning frequently and painting them with sauce every minute or two, taking about 6–8 minutes altogether. Move them to a platter and serve with the reserved sauce on the side.

steps.title: Set oven and prep
steps.text: Preheat the oven to 200° and set up two baking sheets with wire racks inside. Place the flat iron steaks between sheets of plastic wrap and pound them with the flat side of a meat mallet until they are ¼ inch thick. Combine 1 Tbsp flour with kosher salt, garlic powder, onion powder, and black pepper, then rub this mix onto both sides of each cutlet.

steps.title: Make batter and coat
steps.text: Whisk together 2 cups water, nonfat dry milk, powdered egg white, and baking powder in a bowl until smooth. Pour 1½ cups flour into another shallow dish. Dredge each steak in the flour, then dip it into the water batter, back into the flour, then into the batter a second time, and finally into the flour a third time. Lay the coated steaks on the prepared baking sheet and let the coating set for a few minutes.

steps.title: Fry the steaks
steps.text: Heat vegetable oil in a large sauté pan over medium-high to 350°. Working in 2–3 batches to avoid crowding, fry the coated steaks until golden, about 2 minutes on each side. Transfer each cooked steak to a paper-towel-lined baking sheet and keep warm in the oven.

steps.title: Make gravy and serve
steps.text: Pour off all but 3 Tbsp of the oil and warm it over medium-high heat. Whisk in ¼ cup flour and cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly. Gradually whisk in the whole milk and broth, then cook while stirring often until the gravy thickens and bubbles, about 5 minutes. Whisk in the cracked black pepper, Worcestershire sauce, and cayenne, then season with salt. Serve the steaks with this gravy and scatter fresh minced chives on top.

steps.title: Make the dressing
steps.text: Whisk together the extra-virgin olive oil, lemon zest, and fresh lemon juice. Season with salt and black pepper and divide the dressing into two equal portions.

steps.title: Cook lentils and couscous
steps.text: Boil the dry French green lentils according to package directions, then drain. Stir half the dressing and the fresh mint into the warm lentils. In another pot, cook the whole-wheat couscous according to package directions, then stir the remaining dressing and minced red onion into the warm couscous.

steps.title: Compose the bowls
steps.text: Divide the lentils and couscous between serving bowls or a platter, then top with the thinly sliced red onion, seeded and sliced cucumbers, halved grape tomatoes, and cubed feta cheese.

steps.title: Make the sauce
steps.text: Combine the toasted sesame oil with low-sodium soy sauce in a small bowl and set aside.

steps.title: Cook the vegetables
steps.text: Each vegetable is cooked and seasoned separately — that separation is the dish. Give each one 1 tsp oil and 1 tsp minced garlic in turn, then toss it with 1 tsp of the sesame-soy mixture and set it in its own bowl: spinach over medium until wilted, 3 minutes; mushrooms 2–3 minutes; carrots and zucchini together; bean sprouts last.

steps.title: Fry the eggs
steps.text: Add the remaining 2 tsp canola oil to the skillet and bring it over medium heat. Crack the eggs into the pan and fry until the whites have set but the yolks still jiggle slightly, then transfer to a platter.

steps.title: Assemble the bowls
steps.text: Divide the warmed cooked rice among serving bowls. Arrange each cooked vegetable around the rice, top with a fried egg, and drizzle with any remaining sesame-soy mixture. Serve with Korean chili sauce on the side.

steps.title: Make the packets
steps.text: Preheat the oven to 400°. Start with two 24-inch-wide pieces of parchment; fold each one in half, then unfold and cut them into heart shapes. Rub oil all over the insides. Toss the julienned carrots, leeks, and celery together with the dry vermouth, then divide this mixture between the two hearts, piling it in the center. Take the two salmon fillets (seasoned with salt and black pepper), lay them at a perpendicular angle across the vegetables, and you are ready to seal.

steps.title: Seal and bake
steps.text: Fold the parchment paper over the salmon and vegetables, then crimp tightly all the way around the edges to create a secure seal. Transfer the packets to a baking sheet and bake for 15 minutes, then carefully remove the hot packets to a plate.

steps.title: Make the sauce and serve
steps.text: In a small bowl, whisk together the sour cream (or plain yogurt), prepared horseradish, and minced scallions until smooth. Season with salt and black pepper. Carefully open the hot parchment packets and slide the salmon and vegetables onto plates. Drizzle or dollop the horseradish sauce alongside.

steps.title: Make the sauce
steps.text: Whisk together the low-sodium chicken broth, dry sherry, low-sodium soy sauce, cornstarch, and chili garlic sauce in a bowl until the cornstarch dissolves. Add the cubed boneless, skinless chicken breasts to this mixture and set aside to marinate for 10 minutes.

steps.title: Stir-fry the chicken
steps.text: Heat peanut oil in a wok or large skillet over high heat until it shimmers. Remove the chicken from the marinade, setting the liquid aside, and add the chicken to the pan. Stir and toss constantly until the chicken is cooked through, 3–4 minutes, then transfer it to a plate.

steps.title: Finish the dish
steps.text: Return the wok to high heat and add the sliced shiitake mushrooms and bias-cut snow peas. Stir-fry for 2 minutes, then add the minced garlic and ginger and stir-fry until fragrant, about 1 minute more. Return the cooked chicken to the pan and pour in the reserved marinade, scraping any browned bits from the bottom. Simmer the stir-fry while stirring until the sauce thickens, 2–3 minutes. Serve over cooked white rice.

steps.title: Season and coat
steps.text: Cut the whole chicken into 10 pieces and season each piece with salt and black pepper. Lightly beat the eggs in a large bowl with a tight-fitting lid, then add all the chicken pieces and seal the lid. Shake the bowl thoroughly until every piece is well coated with egg. Whisk together 2 cups flour, 2 tsp kosher salt, and 2 tsp black pepper in a shallow dish. Add the flour mixture to the bowl with the chicken, replace the lid, and shake vigorously until all pieces are evenly covered in flour.

steps.title: Fry in batches
steps.text: Heat 2 cups peanut oil in a large cast-iron skillet over medium-high until it reaches 360°. Add half the chicken pieces, skin sides down, then reduce heat to medium and fry without moving them until they turn deep brown, 6–8 minutes. Flip the pieces, drop the heat to low, cover the skillet, and continue frying until a thermometer inserted into the thickest part (but not touching bone) reads 165°, about 10 minutes. Uncover, raise the heat, and fry 3–4 minutes more to re-crisp the coating. Transfer to a paper-towel-lined baking sheet loosely tented with foil and repeat with the remaining chicken.

steps.title: Make the gravy
steps.text: Drain all but 3 Tbsp of the frying oil from the skillet and bring it to medium-high heat. Whisk in ¼ cup flour and cook for 1 minute while stirring constantly. Whisk in 1¼ cups whole milk and 1 cup low-sodium chicken broth slowly, cooking until thick and bubbly, about 5 minutes. Whisk in the cracked black pepper, Worcestershire sauce, and cayenne pepper. Season the gravy with salt and serve alongside the chicken.

steps.title: Layer in jar
steps.text: Layer the ravioli, chicken, spinach, garlic, and Italian seasoning in a large quart jar with a sealing lid.

steps.title: Add broth and pesto
steps.text: Whisk the broth and pesto together, pour it over the ingredients, seal the jar, and refrigerate until ready to eat.

steps.title: Microwave and season
steps.text: Remove the lid, microwave the soup on high until the pasta is tender, 6–8 minutes. Season with salt and pepper.

steps.title: Pound and season pork
steps.text: From the pork tenderloin, cut six thick 1-inch slices. Pound each one down to ½-inch medallions using a meat mallet. Season well with salt and pepper, then dust with flour, shaking off excess.

steps.title: Crisp prosciutto and sear pork
steps.text: Heat the oil in a sauté pan over medium. Render the diced prosciutto until it crisps, 3–4 minutes, and transfer to paper towels. In the same pan, brown the medallions, 2 minutes each side, then set aside.

steps.title: Make the mushroom sauce
steps.text: Return the pan to the heat and add the mushrooms. Let them cook, releasing and evaporating their liquid, 5–6 minutes. Drop the garlic in and cook 1 minute, stirring. Pour in the sherry and broth, scraping up all the dark bits from the bottom, and let the liquid reduce by half, about 3 minutes.

steps.title: Finish with sage and butter
steps.text: Off heat, whisk in the butter and sage until the sauce coats the back of a spoon. Return the medallions to the pan and turn them through the sauce. Serve topped with the crispy prosciutto.

steps.title: Sweat mushrooms and aromatics
steps.text: In a sauté pan over medium-high, melt 3 Tbsp. butter and add the quartered mushrooms. Let them cook until golden and their liquid evaporates, about 10 minutes; transfer to a bowl. Lower the heat to medium, add the remaining 2 Tbsp. butter, then the scallions and cayenne. Cook gently until the scallions soften, 1–2 minutes.

steps.title: Make the sauce
steps.text: Sprinkle the flour into the pan and cook 1 minute, stirring constantly. Slowly whisk in the broth, milk, and sherry until smooth. Simmer until thick, about 7 minutes, then season with more sherry, lemon juice, salt, and pepper.

steps.title: Fold in chicken and vegetables
steps.text: Stir in the chicken, peas, pimentos, and the cooked mushroom mixture. Simmer until heated through, 3–5 minutes.

steps.title: Serve over hash browns
steps.text: Serve over Waffle Hash Browns and garnish with Manchego cheese and sliced scallion greens.

steps.title: Make the relish
steps.text: Whisk together the oil, balsamic, and garlic, season with salt and pepper, then toss with the tomatoes. Add the fresh basil just before serving.

steps.title: Season the chicken
steps.text: Combine the Italian seasoning, granulated garlic, ½ tsp. salt, and ½ tsp. pepper and rub onto the chicken breasts.

steps.title: Cook chicken to temperature
steps.text: Heat the oil in a nonstick skillet over medium-high until shimmering. Add the chicken and cook until a thermometer reads 165° in the thickest part, about 5 minutes per side. Cool slightly, then slice.

steps.title: Finish with zoodles and mozzarella
steps.text: Add the zucchini, relish, and mozzarella to the same skillet and cook just until the zucchini and tomatoes soften, 2 minutes. Season with salt and pepper. Serve the chicken with the zoodles.

steps.title: Toast tortillas
steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350°. Brush the tortilla halves with bacon drippings, season with salt, place on a baking sheet, and bake until crisp, 10 minutes. Cool.

steps.title: Warm and mash beans
steps.text: Sauté the beans, oregano, and garlic in 2 tsp. bacon drippings in a saucepan over medium-high until heated through, 1–2 minutes. Add the salsa and mash until smooth.

steps.title: Assemble and broil
steps.text: Spread the bean mixture on the tostadas and top with cheese. Preheat the broiler to high with the rack 3–4 inches from the element. Broil until the cheese melts, 2 minutes.

steps.title: Marinate shrimp
steps.text: Whisk together the vinegar, soy sauce, brown sugar, and chili garlic sauce. Place the shrimp in a shallow dish, pour the marinade over, and let sit, flipping occasionally.

steps.title: Cook noodles
steps.text: In a pot of salted boiling water, cook the ramen until just tender, 3 minutes. Drain thoroughly, rinse under cold water, and drain again.

steps.title: Sear shrimp and vegetables
steps.text: Heat 2 tsp. oil in a sauté pan over medium-high. Remove the shrimp from the marinade, add to the pan, and cook until firm, 1–2 minutes per side; transfer to a plate. Add the remaining 2 tsp. oil to the pan, then add the mushrooms, scallion whites, shallots, and carrots and cook, stirring, until softened, 2 minutes. Stir in the ginger and garlic and cook until fragrant, 30 seconds.

steps.title: Finish with noodles and herbs
steps.text: Deglaze the pan with the reserved marinade and cook 1 minute. Toss in the noodles, scallion greens, and cilantro. Serve the ramen with the shrimp.

steps.title: Prepare and infuse oil
steps.text: While the oven preheats to 450°, whisk together the oil, fresh dill, chives, and parsley with the lemon zest and juice. Season this herb mixture well with salt and pepper. Line a baking sheet with parchment.

steps.title: Roast salmon
steps.text: Pat the salmon dry and season with salt and pepper. Lay the fillets skin side down on the prepared baking sheet and roast until the flesh is opaque and firm, about 12 minutes.

steps.title: Rest and finish with herbs
steps.text: Slide the cooked salmon onto a serving plate and pour the herbed oil over it. Tent loosely with foil and let it rest 5 minutes before serving.

steps.title: Cook noodles
steps.text: Preheat the oven to 325° and coat an 8-inch square baking dish with nonstick spray. Cook the noodles according to package directions, drain, and transfer to a bowl.

steps.title: Mix noodles with cheese
steps.text: Stir 2 Tbsp. butter and the Port-Salut into the noodles and season with salt and pepper. Transfer to the prepared dish, cover with foil, and bake 30 minutes.

steps.title: Make topping
steps.text: Combine the panko, Parmesan, rosemary, and remaining 2 Tbsp. butter. Sprinkle evenly over the noodles.

steps.title: Broil until golden
steps.text: Heat the broiler to high with the rack 6 inches from the element. Broil until the topping is golden brown, about 2 minutes. Let stand 5 minutes before serving.

steps.title: Build the filling
steps.text: Brown the ground pork in a nonstick skillet over medium-high heat, breaking it up with a potato masher as it cooks. Once no pink remains, add the garlic and ginger and cook 1 minute. Stir in the coleslaw mix and scallions and cook until wilted, 2 minutes. Add the soy sauce and cook until the liquid reduces. Cool the mixture thoroughly before filling.

steps.title: Fill and seal rolls
steps.text: Spoon 3 Tbsp. filling into the center of each egg roll wrap. Fold the corner up over the filling and fold in the sides. Brush the remaining corner with egg wash and seal.

steps.title: Deep fry
steps.text: Pour 2–3 inches of oil into a pot and bring to 350°. Working in two batches so the oil stays hot, fry the egg rolls until the wrappers turn deep golden, 2–3 minutes per batch. Transfer to paper towels to drain.

steps.title: Heat broth
steps.text: Simmer the broth in a saucepan over medium heat.

steps.title: Sweat shallots
steps.text: In a large saucepan over medium, cook the shallots gently in butter until they begin to soften, 2 minutes.

steps.title: Toast rice and add wine
steps.text: Add the rice and cook, stirring often, 1 minute. Add the wine and stir until completely absorbed, 1–2 minutes.

steps.title: Finish risotto
steps.text: Ladle the hot broth into the rice in three parts, stirring often and waiting until each addition nearly disappears into the rice before pouring the next, about 25 minutes total.

steps.title: Finish with cheese
steps.text: Stir in the grated Pecorino until it melts and season with salt and pepper. Garnish servings with shaved Pecorino and toasted walnuts.

steps.title: Scramble eggs and ham
steps.text: Set up a two-zone grill, one side hot, one side cool. Whisk the eggs with milk and season with salt and pepper. In a nonstick skillet over medium, melt the butter, add the ham, and sauté 3–4 minutes. Pour in the eggs and let them set 1 minute, then push them from the edges toward the center with a spatula, making large curds. Remove from heat.

steps.title: Build the pizza
steps.text: Spread the picante sauce over the crust and scatter the scrambled egg mixture on top, followed by the cheese. Set the pizza on the cool side of the grill, cover, and let the crust brown and the cheese melt, 5–7 minutes.

steps.title: Make fresh pico
steps.text: While the pizza finishes, combine the bell pepper, tomato, and scallions in a small bowl.

steps.title: Finish and cut
steps.text: Slide the cooked pizza onto a cutting board, top with the fresh pico de gallo, slice into 8 pieces, and serve right away.

steps.title: Combine oats and spices
steps.text: Combine the water, half-and-half, oats, mashed banana, honey, salt, nutmeg, cardamom, cinnamon, pepper, cloves, and ginger in a 4-cup Pyrex measuring cup. Add the tea bag, pressing it into the liquid.

steps.title: Slow cook overnight
steps.text: Nestle the measuring cup into a 6- to 8-qt. slow cooker and surround it with enough hot water to come halfway up. Cover everything and let the oats cook on low until they reach the tender stage, 7–8 hours. Pull out and discard the tea bag.

steps.title: Finish and serve
steps.text: Stir in the vanilla and top servings with toasted almonds and sliced bananas.

steps.title: Soften aromatics
steps.text: Melt butter and oil in a pot over medium-high. Add onion, garlic, paprika, and pepper flakes, cook until the onion softens, about 3 minutes.

steps.title: Build the soup
steps.text: Deglaze the pot with sherry, let it nearly evaporate. Add broth, tomatoes, and roasted peppers. Bring to a boil, then drop the heat to medium-low and simmer half-covered for 15 minutes.

steps.title: Blend and finish
steps.text: Purée until smooth using a hand blender or in batches with a standard blender. Stir in cream and season with salt, pepper, and vinegar. Top each serving with parsley and toasted almonds.

steps.title: Render bacon
steps.text: Cook bacon in a saucepan until crisp, transfer to paper towels. Leave 2 Tbsp. drippings in the pan.

steps.title: Brown onions
steps.text: Heat the drippings over medium-high. Add onions and cook until softened and browned, 3–5 minutes. Add garlic and cook until fragrant, 1 minute.

steps.title: Simmer slowly
steps.text: Stir in green beans, tomatoes, water, and bacon. Season with salt and pepper, drop to medium-low. Cover and simmer 45 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the beans are very tender.

steps.title: Prepare dish
steps.text: Heat oven to 375°. Coat a 2-qt baking dish with nonstick spray.

steps.title: Sweat spices
steps.text: Melt butter in a sauté pan over medium-low. Add onion, ginger, garlic, jalapeño, cumin, coriander, turmeric, and fenugreek. Sweat until the onion is soft, about 5 minutes.

steps.title: Make gravy
steps.text: Dust with flour and stir to coat everything, cook 1 minute. Whisk in milk and cook 5–8 minutes, stirring, until the gravy thickens slightly.

steps.title: Build casserole
steps.text: Fold in naan, cheese, and spinach, coating them with gravy. Season with salt and pepper. Pour into the prepared dish.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Bake 15–20 minutes until hot and bubbling at the edges. Serve with lime wedges.

steps.title: Boil vegetables
steps.text: Boil potatoes and celery root in salted water until fork-tender, about 20 minutes. Drain, reserving ½ cup liquid.

steps.title: Dry them out
