steps.text: Return them to the pan over medium-low heat for 1 minute to evaporate excess moisture. Rice or mash until smooth.

steps.title: Finish with dairy
steps.text: Stir in cream cheese and butter. Season with salt, pepper, and nutmeg. Work in reserved liquid a bit at a time until you have the texture you want. Garnish with celery leaves.

steps.title: Start the pan
steps.text: Melt butter in a large sauté pan over medium heat, getting it warm before you add the cabbage.

steps.title: Braise long
steps.text: Add cabbage, water, sugar, vinegar, and salt, tossing to coat evenly. Cover, drop to medium-low, and simmer 30 minutes, stirring occasionally.

steps.title: Finish with preserves
steps.text: Stir in preserves and simmer uncovered about 15 minutes until they melt and most of the liquid evaporates.

steps.title: Prepare fillings
steps.text: Cook asparagus in boiling salted water until just crisp-tender, 3 minutes. Cool in cold water. Whip the Brie with cream until fluffy, fold in chives and season with salt and pepper.

steps.title: Start potatoes
steps.text: Heat oil in a skillet over medium-high. When it shimmers, add butter and swirl for about 30 seconds until foaming to keep it from burning.

steps.title: First side
steps.text: Add potatoes and press into a disk with a spatula. Cook without stirring until golden on the edges, 7–8 minutes.

steps.title: Flip and finish
steps.text: Slide the hash onto a plate, cover with another plate, invert so the golden side is up. Slide back into the skillet and cook 5–6 minutes more until golden brown all over.

steps.title: Fill and fold
steps.text: Lay asparagus on half the hash, top with Brie mixture. Fold in half and let sit 1 minute for the cheese to melt and warm the asparagus. Plate and top with extra whipped Brie.

steps.title: Build filling
steps.text: Cook bacon in a sauté pan until crisp, then transfer to paper towels to drain. Leave 2 Tbsp. of fat in the pan. Pulse scallions and mushrooms in a food processor into fine pieces.

steps.title: Cook mushrooms
steps.text: In the same pan over medium-high, cook the mushroom-scallion mix until the mushrooms release and evaporate their liquid, about 3–4 minutes.

steps.title: Finish filling
steps.text: Deglaze the pan with sherry, scraping up brown bits, cook until the sherry evaporates. Off heat, fold in lobster, crackers, and parsley. Season with salt and pepper.

steps.title: Prepare steaks
steps.text: Heat grill to medium-high and brush the grate with oil. Trim excess fat from each steak to ⅛-inch. Cut a horizontal pocket into each, starting about 1-inch from one end, extending nearly to the other end.

steps.title: Stuff and season
steps.text: Stuff each pocket with about ¼ cup filling, press closed firmly. Season both sides generously with salt and pepper.

steps.title: Grill
steps.text: Grill the stuffed steaks covered, 3–4 minutes per side, to medium-rare. Tent loosely with foil and let them rest 5 minutes.

steps.title: Make sauce
steps.text: Heat water and 2 Tbsp. sugar in a saucepan over medium until the sugar dissolves. Off heat, add fish sauce, lime juice, shredded carrot, and chili garlic sauce. Chill until ready to serve.

steps.title: Prepare filling
steps.text: Mix vinegar, 2 Tbsp. sugar, and salt. Toss ¼ cup of this mixture with noodles. Toss coleslaw and julienned carrots with the remaining ¾ cup. Drain the noodles.

steps.title: Cook shrimp
steps.text: Sauté shrimp in oil over medium-high heat until pink and opaque, 2–3 minutes. Set 24 halves aside for garnish, chop the rest.

steps.title: Wrap and roll
steps.text: Soak a wrapper in hot water until it gives, about 30 seconds. Pat it dry on a towel. Set 2 Tbsp noodles, ¼ cup coleslaw mix, 2 Tbsp chopped shrimp, and 1 Tbsp scallions on the bottom third. Roll it up halfway, then arrange 3 mint leaves and 3 reserved shrimp halves across the top. Tuck in the sides and continue rolling to seal. Do the same with the rest. Cover with plastic wrap until ready to eat.

steps.title: Toast aromatics
steps.text: Heat oil in a large saucepan over medium-high. Add scallion whites, ginger, and garlic, cook until they begin to brown, about 3 minutes.

steps.title: Simmer broth
steps.text: Add broth and simmer 10 minutes. Whisk miso into 1 cup warm broth in a bowl until dissolved, then stir it back into the pot. Drop to medium-low and keep at a gentle simmer.

steps.title: Finish soup
steps.text: Add chicken, bamboo shoots, corn, carrot, and noodles. Cook 3–5 minutes until the noodles are tender and everything is hot. Off heat, fold in spinach and serve garnished with scallion greens.

steps.title: Heat iron
steps.text: Heat the waffle iron to medium-high following the maker's instructions.

steps.title: Mix potato batter
steps.text: Toss potatoes with scallions, garlic, flour, salt, pepper, and paprika. Stir in egg white and oil, let sit 5 minutes to soak.

steps.title: Cook hash browns
steps.text: Spray the iron, spread potato mix to the edges on the bottom, press the top down firmly. Cook about 15 minutes until golden and crisp (ignore automatic alerts). Lift out carefully.

strip-steak-with-pink-peppercorns-thyme-.title: Strip Steak with Pink Peppercorns & Thyme

steps.title: Heat oven
steps.text: Preheat oven to 425°.

steps.title: Crust the steak
steps.text: Crush peppercorns in a bag using a rolling pin. Mix with minced thyme and salt. Brush steak with oil on both sides, press firmly into the peppercorn mix to coat.

steps.title: Sear and roast
steps.text: Heat 2 tsp. oil in an ovenproof skillet over medium-high until it shimmers. Sear steak 2½ minutes per side, then transfer the pan to the oven. Roast to 130°F for medium-rare, about 8–10 minutes depending on thickness.

steps.title: Make sauce
steps.text: Sauté shallots in the pan drippings over medium heat until soft, 2 minutes. Deglaze with wine, scraping brown bits. Add a thyme sprig and bay leaf, bring to medium-high, and reduce by half, about 4–5 minutes.

steps.title: Finish sauce
steps.text: Whisk in demi-glace and boil 1 minute until the sauce thickens. Off heat, whisk in butter, season with salt and pepper.

steps.title: Plate
steps.text: Slice the steak across the grain and plate it. Spoon the sauce over top.

steps.title: Prepare pork
steps.text: Heat oven to 375°. Coat pork chops on both sides with crushed peppercorns.

steps.title: Sear and roast
steps.text: Heat oil in an ovenproof skillet over medium-high until it shimmers. Sear the pork 2 minutes per side until browned, then transfer the pan to the oven. Roast until a thermometer reads 145°F for medium, about 12–15 minutes.

steps.title: Build sauce
steps.text: Deglaze the pan with brandy, scraping brown bits, and cook over medium-high until it nearly evaporates, about 2 minutes.

steps.title: Reduce and mount
steps.text: Add broth, vinegar, and thyme, reduce over medium-high for 4 minutes more. Off heat, mount with butter one cube at a time, whisking until each piece emulsifies before adding the next.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Plate the pork and spoon sauce over it.

steps.title: Toast the rice
steps.text: Heat oil in a saucepan over medium-high. Cook onion, carrot, and garlic until soft, about 3 minutes. Add the rice blend and stir it constantly until lightly toasted, 1 minute.

steps.title: Cook with wine and broth
steps.text: Pour in the wine and let it reduce to nearly nothing, stirring. Add the broth and bring to a boil, then cover and drop the heat to low. Cook until the rice is tender, 25–30 minutes.

steps.title: Finish with nuts and herbs
steps.text: Stir in the almonds, lemon juice, and thyme. Taste and season with salt and pepper.

steps.title: Cook the pasta
steps.text: Get a pot of salted water boiling. Cook the penne according to package directions until al dente, then drain.

steps.title: Purée the cottage cheese base
steps.text: Blend the cottage cheese, onion, garlic, Dijon, salt, nutmeg, and cayenne in a food processor until completely smooth.

steps.title: Make the milk sauce
steps.text: Heat the milk in a large saucepan over medium until steaming. Whisk the flour in slowly — do it gradually to avoid lumps — and stir often until it thickens, 8–10 minutes. Add the cottage cheese mixture and whisk until smooth.

steps.title: Melt in the cheeses
steps.text: Mix the fontina, Parmesan, and mozzarella together. Add them to the milk by the handful, whisking between each addition until melted. Stir in the drained penne until well coated.

steps.title: Garnish and serve
steps.text: Divide among serving dishes and top each portion with quartered tomatoes and fresh basil.

steps.title: Soak the first batch
steps.text: Whisk eggs, milk, vanilla, and cinnamon together. Toss in half the bread cubes and let them soak until thoroughly wet, about 5 minutes.

steps.title: Fry and sugar the first batch
steps.text: Heat half the oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high and fry the soaked bread in a single layer, stirring now and then, until golden, about 8 minutes. Add half the butter and stir until it coats everything. Sprinkle half the sugar over the bread, toss it until the sugar melts into syrup, then move it to a serving platter.

steps.title: Soak and fry the second batch
steps.text: While the first batch cooks, soak the remaining bread in the remaining egg mixture. Fry it the same way with the remaining oil, butter, and sugar, then add to the platter and serve.

steps.title: Build the roux base
steps.text: Melt the butter in a pot over high. Cook the onions and 1 tablespoon marjoram until soft, 3–5 minutes. Stir in the flour and cook 2–3 minutes more.

steps.title: Add the liquids
steps.text: Whisk in the half-and-half and clam juice together.

steps.title: Cook the potatoes
steps.text: Add the diced potatoes and bring to a boil. Lower the heat to medium-low and simmer until the potatoes are fork-tender, about 20 minutes.

steps.title: Finish with clams and herbs
steps.text: Stir in the clams and the remaining tablespoon of marjoram until heated through. Season with salt and pepper. Serve with oyster crackers, Tabasco, and lemon.

steps.title: Make the marinade
steps.text: Blend the pear nectar, soy sauce, brown sugar, scallions, sherry, rice vinegar, sesame oil, garlic, and ginger until smooth. Pour into a resealable bag.

steps.title: Marinate the steak
steps.text: Add the sliced flank steak to the bag and refrigerate for 6 hours or overnight. Remove it from the marinade, pat it dry, and discard the liquid.

steps.title: Char the meat
steps.text: Heat a double-burner grill pan to high and brush it with oil. Grill the steak in batches, charring it hard, 1 minute per side, until cooked through.

steps.title: Assemble the tacos
steps.text: Sprinkle the meat with sesame seeds and serve on warm flour tortillas with Korean chili paste and any pickled sides you like.

steps.title: Proof the yeast
steps.text: Mix the warm water with the brown sugar and yeast; let it sit until foamy, 5 minutes. Stir in the oil.

steps.title: Mix the dough
steps.text: Measure out the bread flour, rye flour, potato flakes, caraway seeds, salt, and onion powder into the bowl of your stand mixer. Attach the dough hook. Pour the foamy yeast mixture into the dry ingredients and start mixing on low — it takes 2 minutes for the flour to disappear and the streaks to vanish. Switch to medium speed and let the mixer work the dough smooth and elastic, 10 minutes total. It should be sticky; if it seems impossible to manage, add 1–2 tablespoons more bread flour and let the hook knead it in.

steps.title: First rise
steps.text: Oil a bowl and put the dough in it. Cover with plastic wrap and set it in a warm spot to rise until doubled, 1 hour.

steps.title: Shape and second rise
steps.text: Dust a work surface with flour, turn the dough out, and shape it into an 8-inch loaf. Place it in an 8½×4½-inch loaf pan coated with nonstick spray. Cover the pan with plastic coated with nonstick spray and let it rise until it climbs above the rim, 1–2 hours.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Preheat to 350° with the rack at the very bottom. Bake the loaf until golden and a thermometer in the center reads 190°, 30–35 minutes. Cool in the pan for 5 minutes, then turn it out onto a rack to cool all the way through.

steps.title: Cook the pasta and beans
steps.text: Boil the orzo in salted water according to package directions. In the last 3–4 minutes, add the green beans. Drain both together.

steps.title: Dress with Parmesan and lemon
steps.text: Transfer to a bowl and toss with the Parmesan, lemon zest, and lemon juice.

steps.title: Season
steps.text: Taste and season with salt and pepper.

steps.title: Boil the broth
steps.text: Bring the broth to a boil in a 4-quart saucepan.

steps.title: Add rice and butter
steps.text: Stir in the rice, butter, and salt.

steps.title: Wilt in the greens
steps.text: Add the chopped collards a handful at a time, stirring between additions until all the greens have gone in. Bring to a boil, then cover, lower the heat to a simmer, and cook until the rice is tender, 15–20 minutes. Season with salt and pepper before serving.

steps.title: Heat the oil
steps.text: Bring the peanut or vegetable oil to 375° in a 7- to 8-quart pot, checked with a candy thermometer.

steps.title: Make the creamy pesto
steps.text: Heat the olive oil and butter in a saucepan over medium. Cook the garlic for 1–2 minutes, then stir in the flour and cook 1 minute more. Whisk in the milk and simmer until thickened, 3 minutes. Whisk in the pesto and season with salt and pepper.

steps.title: Cook the pepperoni and mushrooms
steps.text: Brown the pepperoni slices in a skillet over medium-high heat until crisp, 5–7 minutes, then transfer to a paper-towel-lined plate. Cook the mushroom slices in the drippings until they release their water and brown, 8–10 minutes. Preheat the broiler with the rack 6–8 inches from the element.

steps.title: Cut and fry the dough
steps.text: On a lightly floured surface, roll the pizza dough to ⅛-inch thick and cut it into 2-inch squares. Working in 6 batches, fry the squares until golden brown, 1½ minutes per batch. Use a slotted spoon to fish them out and toss with salt, then spread on a clean baking sheet.

steps.title: Assemble and broil
steps.text: Top each chip with the creamy pesto, pepperoni, mushrooms, bell pepper, onion, and cheeses. Broil until the cheese is melted and bubbly, about 2 minutes, and serve right away with warm pizza sauce.

steps.title: Prep and roast the mushrooms
steps.text: Move an oven rack to the middle and set the temperature to 425°. Put parchment on a baking sheet. On each portobello gill, spread 1 teaspoon of Dijon, scatter ½ teaspoon of thyme, then season with salt and pepper. Roast them until the tops brown slightly, 20 minutes.

steps.title: Make the duxelles
steps.text: Sauté the leeks, shallots, and garlic in oil over medium-high heat until soft, 4–5 minutes. Add the button and shiitake mushrooms and cook until the liquid has evaporated and everything is tender, about 7 minutes. Stir in the walnuts, chives, 1 teaspoon Dijon, and 1 teaspoon thyme. Season with salt and pepper.

steps.title: Assemble the Wellingtons
steps.text: Cut two 5-inch rounds from the puff pastry. On a floured surface, roll each one to 10 inches wide. Take a roasted portobello and top it with 1 teaspoon Roquefort, then divide the duxelles and heap it over the cheese. Place the mushroom in the center of one pastry round, gather the edges up around it, and fold them inward, leaving a small opening at the very top. Repeat with the second mushroom. Give each pastry parcel a brush of egg wash and slide both onto the baking sheet.

steps.title: Bake until golden
steps.text: Bake until the pastry is golden and puffed, 20–22 minutes.

steps.title: Make the crusts
steps.text: Heat the oven to 350° and fit mini muffin pans with paper liners. Crush the cookies in a food processor until they have broken into small pieces that just start to hold together when squeezed. Add the melted butter and pulse a few times until the mixture resembles wet sand and will hold its shape when pressed. Divide the crumb mixture among the liners — about 2 teaspoons per cup — and push it firmly into the bottom and up the sides. Bake 5 minutes, then take the pans out to cool.

steps.title: Steep the tea
steps.text: Set a metal bowl over a saucepan with 1 inch of water for a double boiler. Steep the tea bags in ½ cup heavy cream over medium-low heat for 15 minutes, then squeeze out the cream from the bags and discard them.

steps.title: Whip the cream
steps.text: Beat the remaining ½ cup heavy cream to stiff peaks, cover, and refrigerate.

steps.title: Bloom the gelatin
steps.text: Sprinkle the gelatin over the crème de menthe in a small bowl and let it sit for 5 minutes.

steps.title: Temper the yolks
steps.text: Whisk the egg yolks and sugar together in a separate bowl. Prepare an ice water bath. Add the gelatin mixture to the steeped cream in the double boiler and whisk to combine. When it steams, slowly whisk it into the yolk mixture to temper it. Return the yolk-cream mixture to the double boiler and cook, whisking occasionally, until an instant-read thermometer reads 150°, 1–2 minutes.

steps.title: Cool to pudding
steps.text: Transfer the bowl to the ice water bath and whisk constantly until cool and the consistency of thin pudding, about 1 minute — whisk it often so it cools evenly and stays smooth.

steps.title: Fill and chill
steps.text: Have your piping bag with the small star tip at the ready. Into a large bowl, transfer the cooled mint custard. Working in thirds, sweep the chilled whipped cream down from the top of the bowl and fold it into the custard, turning the bowl as you go, until no white streaks remain. Pipe the combined filling into each crust, filling it all the way to the rim. Cover with plastic wrap and set in the refrigerator for at least 1 hour before serving, or make them the night before.

steps.title: Garnish and serve
steps.text: Top with chocolate shavings before serving.

steps.title: Dressing
steps.text: Whisk together the vinegar, soy sauce, brown sugar, lime juice, chili garlic sauce, sesame oil, minced garlic, and minced ginger.

steps.title: Dress the slaw
steps.text: Toss the broccoli slaw, carrots, and bell peppers with the dressing, then cover and refrigerate for 2 hours.

steps.title: Finish and serve
steps.text: Scatter the ramen noodles, scallions, cilantro, and mint over the chilled slaw, add the peanuts, and toss gently to combine just before serving.

steps.title: Preheat and prepare
steps.text: Spray a 1-quart baking dish and set the oven to 400°. Combine the panko, ¼ cup Parmesan, parsley, and 1 Tbsp. oil in a bowl for the topping.

steps.title: Aromatics and base
steps.text: Warm 1 Tbsp. oil in a sauté pan over medium-high, add the scallions and bell pepper, and cook until just soft, 2 minutes. Stir in the minced garlic for 30 seconds, then pour in the sherry and reduce it nearly dry, scraping the pan.

steps.title: Build the filling
steps.text: Add the artichokes and cream; simmer 1 minute. Kill the heat and fold in the neufchatel until it melts completely, then fold in the ½ cup Parmesan, lemon zest and juice, Dijon mustard, tarragon, Tabasco, and Worcestershire sauce.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Gently fold the crabmeat into the mixture, pour into the prepared dish, sprinkle the topping over, and bake until the top is golden, 25–30 minutes. Serve hot with crostini.

oysters-rockefeller-with-tabasco-beurre-.title: Oysters Rockefeller with Tabasco Beurre Blanc

steps.title: Preheat and garlic butter
steps.text: Set the oven to 450°. In a small sauté pan, warm 4 Tbsp. butter over medium-low, add the garlic, and cook gently for 2 minutes.

steps.title: Divide and cook spinach
steps.text: Pour half the garlic butter into a bowl and toss it with the panko, scallions, and Parmesan for the topping. Return the pan to medium heat, add the spinach, parsley, and celery to the remaining butter, then pour in the Pernod and let it evaporate completely, 5 minutes. Season with salt and pepper.

steps.title: Assemble and roast
steps.text: Spread the salt on a baking sheet and nestle the oysters into it. Top each oyster with ½ tsp. spinach mixture, then the bread crumb mixture, then crumbled bacon. Roast until the oysters begin to curl and the crumbs are golden, 10–15 minutes.

steps.title: Beurre blanc
steps.text: On high heat, cook down the wine, lemon juice, shallots, and Tabasco until only half remains, 5 minutes. Take the pan off the heat and whisk in the cold butter bit by bit, making sure each piece melts completely before the next goes in. Season to taste with salt and pepper.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Spoon the warm beurre blanc over the oysters and serve immediately.

steps.title: Prep wings and mango sauce
steps.text: Trim the wing tips and discard them. Separate each wing at the joint, then put all the pieces into a 3- to 4-quart slow cooker. Blend the fresh mangoes, garlic, hot sauce, mango jelly, butter, and salt until the mixture is smooth.

steps.title: Slow cook
steps.text: Reserve half of the mango sauce. Stir the remaining half into the slow cooker, cover, and cook on low until an instant-read thermometer inserted into a wing registers 165°, about 3 hours.

steps.title: Broil
steps.text: Preheat the broiler to high with the rack 6 inches from the element. Line the broiler pan with foil and coat the rack with nonstick spray. Arrange half the wings on the pan and broil 7–8 minutes, turn, and broil 7–8 minutes more until they begin to char. Repeat with the remaining wings.

steps.title: Cilantro dipping sauce
steps.text: Purée the cilantro, yogurt, cream cheese, and lime juice in a food processor until smooth, then season with salt. Serve alongside the wings with the reserved mango sauce for dipping.

steps.title: Sear the filets
steps.text: Combine butter and oil in a sauté pan over medium-high. Sear the filets until an instant-read thermometer reads 130° at the thickest part for medium-rare, 2 minutes per side, then transfer to a plate and tent with foil.

steps.title: Mushroom sauce
steps.text: Add the mushrooms to the pan and sauté until browned and tender, 3–4 minutes. Stir in the minced garlic, basil, and oregano and cook until fragrant, 1 minute. Pour in the cream and vermouth, stir, and let it reduce by half, 2–3 minutes.

steps.title: Finish and serve
steps.text: Return the filets with all their accumulated juices to the pan, heat through, and serve garnished with chopped fresh parsley.

steps.title: Prepare grill and gremolata
steps.text: Preheat the grill to medium and lightly oil the grate. Combine the parsley, lemon zest, minced garlic, and minced rosemary, then season with salt and black pepper for the gremolata.

steps.title: Grill the veal
steps.text: Coat the veal chops lightly with nonstick spray and grill until an instant-read thermometer inserted near (but not touching) the bone reads 135°, about 4 minutes per side. Tent with foil and let rest 5 minutes.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Spoon the gremolata over the chops and garnish each with a lemon twist and a fresh rosemary sprig.

steps.title: Brown the sausage and shrimp
steps.text: Brown the diced andouille sausage in oil in a sauté pan over medium-high heat, 3–5 minutes. Add the shrimp and cook until firm and opaque, 3 minutes, then transfer both to a plate.

steps.title: Build the base
steps.text: Add the diced onion, bell pepper, celery, and minced garlic to the pan and sauté until just beginning to soften, 2 minutes. Stir in the Italian seasoning, smoked paprika, black pepper, and cayenne pepper and cook until aromatic, 30 seconds.

steps.title: Deglaze and reduce
steps.text: Pour in the chicken broth, scrape up the brown bits, and simmer until the liquid reduces by half, 3–5 minutes. Stir in the fire-roasted tomatoes with their juice and tomato paste, then simmer until the sauce is thick, 2–3 minutes.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Return the sausage and shrimp to the pan and season with salt. Garnish with chopped scallions and serve with Tabasco sauce on the side.

steps.title: Cook the mango sauce
steps.text: In a saucepan over medium-low, cook the mango, shallots, butter, curry powder, and ⅓ cup water gently until both the mango and shallots break down, 10–15 minutes. Scrape the whole thing into a mini food processor.

steps.title: Purée and season
steps.text: Purée the mango mixture with the lemon juice and honey. Thin the sauce with water, 1 Tbsp. at a time, to reach your desired consistency, then season with salt and cayenne pepper.

steps.title: Sear the scallops
steps.text: Pour 1 Tbsp. oil into a sauté pan and get it smoking over high heat. Add half the scallops and cook until they're golden at the edges, 2–3 minutes per side. Do the same with the remaining oil and scallops.

steps.title: Plate and garnish
steps.text: Divide the sauce between two plates, arrange five scallops on each pool of sauce, and garnish with quartered red seedless grapes, chopped fried salted Marcona almonds, and minced fresh cilantro.

steps.title: Whisk the eggs
steps.text: Whisk the eggs and half-and-half together in a bowl.

steps.title: Melt the butter
steps.text: Melt the butter in an 8-inch nonstick skillet over medium-high heat until it bubbles.

steps.title: Cook the omelet
steps.text: Tip the eggs into the skillet and season with salt and pepper. Start shaking the pan gently back and forth while stirring quickly with a spatula at the same time. When the eggs stop running but still look wet on top, drop the heat to low.

steps.title: Fill and fold
steps.text: Spoon the filling in a line at right angles to the pan handle. Fold the edge of the omelet nearest the handle up and over the filling, then tilt the pan over a plate and slide the omelet out, folding the far edge over on top as it lands. Rest it 1 minute before serving.

steps.title: Sweat the base
steps.text: Melt butter in a large pot over medium heat, add diced onions and cook until softened, about 5 minutes. Stir in the minced garlic, tomato paste, and red pepper flakes; cook 1 minute more to deepen the flavors.

steps.title: Build the broth
steps.text: Tip in the tomatoes, lightly crush them with the back of a spoon, then add the broth. Bring to a simmer and cook for 10 minutes.

steps.title: Smooth it
steps.text: Working in batches if needed, purée the entire pot with a handheld blender until completely smooth. If you prefer a standard blender, do it in manageable batches so you don't overfill it.

steps.title: Melt in the cheese
steps.text: Turn the heat down to medium. Begin stirring in the shredded Cheddar in small handfuls, waiting for each one to disappear completely before you add more — this gradual method prevents the cheese from becoming grainy and separating.

steps.title: Finish and season
steps.text: Off the heat, stir in the milk and season with salt and pepper. Top each bowl with a sliver of fresh basil and a scatter of Cheddar.

steps.title: Cook the noodles
steps.text: Boil the egg noodles in salted water according to package directions. Add the green beans during the last 3 minutes so they finish together. Drain both and set aside.

steps.title: Make the mustard sauce
steps.text: Melt butter in the same pot over medium heat. Whisk in the coarse-grain mustard, stirring until the flavors are fully blended and the butter is smooth and glossy.

steps.title: Combine and season
steps.text: Return the drained noodles and green beans to the pot, add the chopped parsley, and toss everything together until each strand is coated with the mustard butter. Season with salt and pepper and serve immediately.

steps.title: Rice the cauliflower
steps.text: Pulse the cauliflower florets in a food processor until they are the size of rice grains. Do not overprocess; you want texture, not purée.

steps.title: Sweat the shallots
steps.text: Combine butter and olive oil in a sauté pan and warm over medium heat. Once the butter has melted, scatter in the minced shallots and let them cook gently for 3–4 minutes, stirring occasionally, until they are translucent and tender but have not taken on any color. Now turn the heat up to medium-high.

steps.title: Toast the cauliflower
steps.text: Stir in the riced cauliflower, season with salt and pepper, and cook for 2 minutes to dry it slightly and toast the flavor.

steps.title: Deglaze and build
steps.text: Pour in the white wine and let it cook down nearly completely. Then add the broth in ½-cup increments, stirring constantly and letting each addition absorb before adding the next. This takes about 15–20 minutes. The constant stirring and gradual liquid create the creamy texture.

steps.title: Finish off heat
steps.text: When the cauliflower is tender and the liquid is absorbed, take the pan off the heat. Stir in the Parmesan and heavy cream. Top with chopped parsley and serve immediately.

steps.title: Prep the broiler
steps.text: Preheat the broiler to high with the rack positioned 6 inches from the element. Coat a baking sheet with nonstick spray.

steps.title: Mash roasted garlic
steps.text: Sauté the unpeeled garlic cloves in a small skillet over medium heat for 3 minutes, stirring often, until the skins brown. When cool enough to handle, remove the skins and mash the garlic into a paste.

steps.title: Brown the bacon
steps.text: Cook the bacon strips in a sauté pan over medium heat in batches just until they begin to brown around the edges. Transfer to a paper-towel-lined plate to drain and cool slightly.

steps.title: Make the filling
steps.text: Beat together the mashed garlic, softened cream cheese, shredded Monterey Jack, fresh cilantro, panko, minced chipotle, and lime juice with a hand mixer until the mixture is smooth and blended.

steps.title: Stuff and wrap
steps.text: Flatten each butterflied shrimp along the cut to open it fully. Mound 2–3 tsp. of filling onto each opened shrimp. Wrap one bacon strip around each shrimp to enclose the filling and place it seam-side down on the prepared baking sheet.

steps.title: Broil until done
steps.text: Broil the shrimp until they are opaque and the bacon is fully cooked through, about 7 minutes. Do not walk away — they cook fast.

steps.title: Heat the oil
steps.text: Pour peanut oil into a 7- to 8-quart pot and position a deep-fry thermometer inside, then place over high heat. Watch it until the temperature climbs to 375°. A piece of tortilla dropped in should sizzle and brown right away.

steps.title: Make the dressing
steps.text: Whisk together olive oil, grated Parmesan, mayonnaise, fresh lemon juice, minced garlic, anchovy paste, Dijon mustard, Worcestershire sauce, and Tabasco. Season with salt and pepper. Preheat the broiler with the rack 6–8 inches from the element.

steps.title: Fry the chips
steps.text: Slice each tortilla into 6 wedges. Work in six batches, frying each batch for about 1½ minutes until the pieces are light golden and crisp. Lift them out with a slotted spoon, settle them into a bowl, and toss with salt right away so it sticks. Move the seasoned chips to a clean baking sheet, then go back to frying the next batch.

steps.title: Assemble the nachos
steps.text: Top the fried tortilla chips with half the shaved Parmesan, some of the remaining dressing, the chopped rotisserie chicken that you have tossed with ⅓ cup dressing, and the rest of the shaved Parmesan.

steps.title: Finish under the broiler
steps.text: Broil the nachos until the cheese melts, about 2 minutes. Remove from the heat and top with romaine that you have tossed separately with 3 Tbsp. dressing, and scatter diced tomato over the top. Serve immediately.

steps.title: Preheat and prep
steps.text: Preheat the oven to 400° and coat an 8×8-inch baking pan with nonstick spray.

steps.title: Sauté fennel and onion
steps.text: Sauté the grated fennel bulb and grated onion in 1 Tbsp. olive oil over medium-high heat until the liquid evaporates, about 5 minutes. Season with salt and pepper and set aside to cool.

steps.title: Mix the dry goods
steps.text: Whisk together the cornmeal, all-purpose flour, baking powder, ground fennel, and kosher salt in a large bowl.

steps.title: Combine wet and dry
steps.text: Whisk together the buttermilk, ⅓ cup olive oil, honey, and eggs in a separate bowl. Fold the wet mixture and the cooled fennel mixture into the dry ingredients just until blended — do not overmix. Pour the batter into the prepared pan.

steps.title: Bake until set
steps.text: Bake the cornbread until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean, 15–20 minutes. The top should be golden and firm to touch.

steps.title: Make the vinaigrette
steps.text: Whisk together the fresh lime juice, olive oil, white wine vinegar, honey, kosher salt, and black pepper. Add the minced red onion, minced jalapeño, and chopped fresh cilantro and let it sit for a few minutes so the flavors marry.

steps.title: Slice the tomatoes
steps.text: Cut the tomatoes into ¼-inch-thick slices and arrange them on a serving plate or individual plates.

steps.title: Dress and serve
steps.text: Pour the vinaigrette and its onion and jalapeño over the tomato slices just before serving. Let it sit for 2–3 minutes so the tomatoes can absorb the dressing.

steps.title: Mix the dressing
steps.text: Whisk together the fresh lime juice, fresh orange juice, extra-virgin olive oil, sugar, ground cumin, kosher salt, and black pepper.

steps.title: Prep the slaw
steps.text: Combine the coleslaw mix, sliced mini sweet peppers, thinly sliced red onion, chopped fresh cilantro, and sliced jalapeño in a large bowl.

steps.title: Dress and rest
steps.text: Pour the vinaigrette over the slaw and toss well to coat everything evenly. Let it sit for 5 minutes before serving so the vegetables soften slightly and soak up the dressing.

steps.title: Sauté the aromatics
steps.text: Heat the canola oil in a small sauté pan over medium-high heat. Add the diced onion, ground cumin, and bay leaf; cook until the onion softens, about 5 minutes.

steps.title: Add the beans
steps.text: Stir in the drained black beans, frozen corn kernels, dried epazote, chopped scallions, and minced garlic. Heat through, stirring occasionally, until everything is warmed and the flavors blend, about 3–4 minutes.

steps.title: Finish with lime
steps.text: Discard the bay leaf. Stir in the fresh lime juice and season the sauté with salt and black pepper to taste. The acid from the lime brightens everything.

steps.title: Sweat onion and spice
steps.text: Warm the olive oil in a large pot over medium-low heat. Add the diced onion, minced garlic, and red pepper flakes; cook until the onion softens, about 5 minutes.

steps.title: Simmer the base
steps.text: Increase the heat to high and add the diced tomatoes with their juice and the vegetable broth. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer.

steps.title: Add the kale and finish
steps.text: Stir in the chopped kale, balsamic vinegar, and kosher salt. Simmer for 15 minutes until the kale is tender. Season with black pepper. The vinegar adds depth to the tomato.

steps.title: Hollow the tomatoes
steps.text: Slice the top off each tomato and reserve it. Using a spoon, gently scrape out the pulp and seeds into a fine-mesh strainer; save that pulp. Season the inside of each tomato shell with salt and pepper, then invert them on a paper-towel-lined plate to drain for a few minutes.

steps.title: Make the dressing
steps.text: Pass the strained tomato pulp through the strainer to release the juice. Whisk together the extra-virgin olive oil, fresh mint, chopped fresh basil, fresh lemon juice, and 3 Tbsp. of that strained tomato juice.

steps.title: Build the filling
steps.text: Combine the chopped kalamata olives, minced red onion, minced garlic, chopped croutons, and fresh mozzarella pearls in a bowl. Toss everything with the vinaigrette.

steps.title: Stuff and serve
steps.text: Divide the filling evenly among the hollowed tomatoes, mounding it gently. Serve at room temperature or slightly chilled.

steps.title: Preheat and prep
steps.text: Preheat the oven to 425°. Halve the fingerling potatoes lengthwise, cut the fennel bulb into 8 wedges lengthwise, and quarter the shallots lengthwise.

steps.title: Dress the vegetables
steps.text: Toss the potatoes, fennel, and shallots with the olive oil. Scatter the minced fresh thyme, kosher salt, and black pepper over them and toss again until well coated.

steps.title: Roast and turn
steps.text: Set the baking sheet in the oven and let it cook for 15 minutes until the edges start to color. Take it out, flip each vegetable piece over and give the pan a quarter turn to ensure even browning, then put it back in for another 15 minutes. The vegetables are done when they are caramelized on all sides and fork-tender.

steps.title: Salt the rims
steps.text: Combine the kosher salt and ground cumin on a small plate. Rub the rim of each glass with a lime wedge, then dip it into the salt mixture to coat. Set the glasses aside.

steps.title: Mix the cocktail
steps.text: Stir together the tomato juice, silver tequila, fresh lime juice, minced chipotle in adobo, Worcestershire sauce, chopped fresh cilantro, grated onion, and hot sauce in a pitcher. Taste and adjust seasoning if needed.

steps.title: Serve and garnish
steps.text: Fill each prepared glass with ice and pour in the Bloody Maria mixture. Lay a whole scallion across the top of each glass as a garnish. Serve immediately while cold.

steps.title: Bloom the aromatics
steps.text: Melt the unsalted butter in a large sauté pan over medium-low heat. Add the sliced jalapeño, minced fresh ginger, and minced garlic; cook for 1 minute, stirring gently, until fragrant.

steps.title: Wilt the spinach
steps.text: Stir in the fresh spinach and golden raisins. Increase the heat to medium-high and cook, stirring occasionally, until most of the liquid from the spinach is released and evaporated, about 5 minutes. The spinach will shrink dramatically.

steps.title: Add the cream
steps.text: Off the heat, stir in the cream cheese until it melts completely into the spinach. Season with salt and black pepper. If you like, garnish with toasted cashews for crunch and richness.

steps.title: Soften the scallion whites
steps.text: Slice the scallions, keeping the white and green parts separate. Sweat the whites with minced garlic in 1 Tbsp. oil over medium-low heat.

steps.title: Warm the beans
steps.text: Add the drained beans to the pan and stir until warmed through.

steps.title: Pickle dressing
steps.text: Whisk together the lime juice, pickle juice, remaining 1 Tbsp. oil, and mustard in a small bowl. Stir this into the beans.

steps.title: Finish off the heat
steps.text: Take the pan off the burner. Add the pickles, Swiss cheese, and scallion greens. Season with salt and pepper.

steps.title: Char and steam poblanos
steps.text: Set the oven to 425°. Working over a gas flame, blacken the poblanos on all sides. Trap them in a covered bowl for 15 minutes — they'll steam loose in their own heat. Once soft, peel off the skin, remove the seeds, and cut into pieces.

steps.title: Mix the cheeses
steps.text: Toss together the pepper Jack, Monterey Jack, queso fresco, and flour.

steps.title: Sauté the mushrooms and poblanos
steps.text: Set butter to melt in a skillet on medium-high. When foaming, add mushrooms and let them brown, 4–5 minutes. Stir in the garlic and poblano pieces; cook 1 minute more. Pour the beer into the pan and let it reduce away. Season to taste.

steps.title: Bake until bubbly
steps.text: Pour the mushroom mixture over the cheese, toss to combine, and turn it into a 1-qt. baking dish. Bake until the cheese is bubbly and lightly browned at the edges, 10–12 minutes. Serve with tortilla chips.

steps.title: Preheat the oven
steps.text: Heat the oven to 350°.

steps.title: Mix the topping
steps.text: Combine the feta, pepperoncini, parsley, 2 tsp. oil, lemon zest, and garlic. Season with salt and pepper.

steps.title: Brush and top the pitas
steps.text: Brush both sides of each pita with oil. Top with the feta mixture and set on a baking sheet.

steps.title: Toast and cut
steps.text: Run them through the oven for 10 minutes until the edges brown lightly. Slice into wedges.

steps.title: Crisp the tortillas
steps.text: Heat the oven to 350°. Brush both sides of the corn tortillas with oil, set them on a baking sheet, and bake until crisp, 20 minutes.

steps.title: Build the topping
steps.text: Toss the grapefruit segments with avocado, jalapeño, bell pepper, cilantro, cumin, and coriander in a large bowl. Season with salt and pepper, then add 1 Tbsp. of the reserved grapefruit juice and toss.

steps.title: Top and garnish
steps.text: Divide the topping evenly among the crisped tortillas. Sprinkle queso fresco over each one.

steps.title: Toss the berries
steps.text: Combine the thawed raspberries and blueberries with sugar and cornstarch in a large bowl.

steps.title: Butter the bread
steps.text: Give 2 slices of cinnamon swirl bread a quick toast and brush with melted butter on both sides. For the remaining 4 slices, leave them untoasted but brush those with melted butter too.

steps.title: Assemble the shell
steps.text: Into a 3- to 4-qt. slow cooker, lay your toasted slices flat on the bottom for the foundation. Now build the walls: press the untoasted buttered bread vertically against the sides, patching gaps with cut pieces as needed. Pour the berry mixture in.

steps.title: First cook
steps.text: Cover and cook on high for 1 hour. Gently stir without breaking the bread crust, then cover again and cook until the berries are thick and bubbling, 30–40 minutes more.

steps.title: Toast the topping
steps.text: Set 2 Tbsp. butter over medium heat in a sauté pan. When it melts, add almonds and oats. Watch them toast for about 5 minutes. Stir in brown sugar and keep stirring until it melts, 3 minutes.

steps.title: Finish the crisp
steps.text: Fold the crushed almond biscotti into the warm almond mixture and cook until syrupy, then pull from the heat.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Top the berry mixture with the crisp, then top each serving with vanilla ice cream or lemon yogurt.

steps.title: Prepare the pan
steps.text: Heat the oven to 450°. Coat a baking sheet with nonstick spray.

steps.title: Season and toss
steps.text: Mix together the salt, garlic powder, thyme, paprika, cayenne, and black pepper. Toss the potato sticks with oil, then toss with the seasonings.

steps.title: Bake until crisp
steps.text: Spread the potatoes in a single layer on the baking sheet and bake 15 minutes. Flip them and continue baking until golden and crisp, 10–15 minutes more.

steps.title: Preheat and prep
steps.text: Set the oven to 400°. Mix the softened butter with oil, minced garlic, and lemon zest; season with salt and pepper.

steps.title: Butter the baguette
steps.text: Brush the cut sides of the halved baguette with the butter mixture, making sure it soaks into the crumb.

steps.title: Toast and finish
steps.text: Bake until the edges are golden and the butter has crisped the surface, 12–13 minutes. Scatter fresh parsley over the top before serving.

steps.title: Set up and cook pasta
steps.text: Turn the oven to 350° and line a 9×13-inch baking dish with nonstick spray. Boil the elbow macaroni in salted water according to the box and drain.

steps.title: Brown the meat
steps.text: Cook the bacon in a large skillet until crisp; transfer to a paper towel. Add beef, diced onion, and garlic to the same skillet; cook until the meat is browned, 5–7 minutes.

steps.title: Build the casserole
steps.text: Stir in the diced tomatoes, ketchup, mustard, and Worcestershire; cook until heated through. Add the pickle chips, 1 cup cheese, and the cooked macaroni. Season with salt and pepper.

steps.title: Bake until cheese melts
steps.text: Transfer the mixture to the baking dish and top with the remaining 1 cup cheese. Bake until the cheese melts, 15 minutes. Crumble the reserved bacon over the top and serve.

steps.title: Make the broth base
steps.text: For the broth, shred the carrots until you have ⅓ cup for garnish and set aside. Dice the rest. Cook the diced carrots and onion in 1 tsp. oil in a saucepan over medium heat until the onion softens, 3–5 minutes.

steps.title: Finish the broth
steps.text: Deglaze the pan with white wine. Add carrot juice and ginger; bring to a boil. Drop the heat to a simmer and cook uncovered for 15 minutes. Season with ⅛ tsp. salt and a dash of Tabasco.

steps.title: Ready the fish
steps.text: Score the skin of each fillet with a knife. Brush both sides with 2 tsp. oil and sprinkle with ¼ tsp. salt, pepper, and paprika.

steps.title: Sauté the fillets
steps.text: Heat a large nonstick skillet over medium. Sauté the fish skin-side down until the skin is crispy, 4 minutes. Flip and sauté until the flesh flakes easily, 4–5 minutes more.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Divide the broth between bowls, set a fillet in each, and garnish with the shredded carrots.

sauteed-red-snapper-with-carrot-broth.title: Sautéed Red Snapper with Carrot Broth

steps.title: Prepare the grill
steps.text: Heat the grill to medium-low and brush the grate with oil.

steps.title: Season the wedges
steps.text: Mix together the garlic powder, salt, and black pepper. Toss the potato wedges with oil, then toss with the spice blend.

steps.title: Grill until fork-tender
steps.text: Set the wedges on the grate and let them char slightly while they soften inside, 5–7 minutes per side. Pour the reserved lime vinaigrette over them and serve.

steps.title: Spice blend
steps.text: Mix dried garlic, dried onion, poppy seeds, sesame seeds, and 1 tsp salt in a small bowl.

steps.title: Coat the cauliflower
steps.text: Whisk yogurt, oil, lemon juice, salt, and minced fresh garlic in a bowl. Season with pepper. Toss cauliflower to coat, then lay it on a foil-lined baking sheet. Sprinkle 1 Tbsp spice blend over the top.

steps.title: Roast
steps.text: Roast at 400° until golden and fork-tender, about 1 hour. Rest 10 minutes before serving.

steps.title: Herbed cheese sauce
steps.text: Purée cream cheese, goat cheese, buttermilk, lemon juice, and minced garlic in a food processor. Add parsley, chives, and dill; pulse until combined. Season with salt and pepper.

steps.title: Sweat aromatics
steps.text: Melt butter in a pot over medium heat. Add onions and celery, cover, and cook gently until soft, 10 minutes. Add garlic, tomato paste, and celery seeds; cook until fragrant, 1 minute.

steps.title: Simmer
steps.text: Tip in the whole tomatoes with their juice and broth. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low and simmer gently 10 minutes.

steps.title: Blend and finish
steps.text: Work through the soup in a handheld blender, or use a standard blender in batches if you prefer. Once smooth, stir the cream through. Taste, then add salt and pepper as needed. Pour into bowls and top each with a few celery leaves and a pinch of celery seeds.

steps.title: Build sandwiches
steps.text: Brush one side of each bread slice with melted butter. Lay them buttered-side down. Mix the cheeses, then divide between 4 slices; season with salt and pepper. Top each with a second slice, buttered-side up.

steps.title: Cook first side
steps.text: Heat a nonstick skillet over medium heat. Lightly coat with nonstick spray. Set sandwiches in the pan and cook until golden on one side, 2 minutes.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Flip, cover, and cook another 2 minutes until the cheese melts and the bread is golden. Serve hot.

steps.title: Herb butter
steps.text: Combine oil, butter, lemon zest, and oregano in a small bowl. Spread the mixture over the cut sides of the baguette halves.

steps.title: Top and broil
steps.text: Set the baguette on a foil-lined baking sheet. Scatter pecorino over both halves. Broil at high, 6 inches from the element, until golden, 2 minutes.

steps.title: Garnish
steps.text: Scatter fresh parsley over the warm toasts before serving.

steps.title: Blanch and dry
steps.text: Blanch broccoli florets and stems in boiling salted water until crisp-tender, 2 minutes. Drain, plunge into ice water to stop the cooking, then drain again. Spin dry in a salad spinner; transfer to a bowl.

steps.title: Make dressing
steps.text: Whisk vinegar, soy sauce, chili garlic sauce, sesame oil, and minced shallots together in a small bowl.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Pour the dressing over the broccoli and toss to coat. Stir in peanuts just before serving, so they stay crisp.

steps.title: Make vinaigrette
steps.text: Whisk oil, vinegar, ginger, Dijon, and sugar together. Season with salt and pepper to taste.

steps.title: Prepare slaw
steps.text: Toss slaw mix, jicama, beets, carrots, radishes, and scallions together in a large bowl.

steps.title: Dress
steps.text: Pour the vinaigrette over the slaw and toss to coat evenly.

steps.title: Cook pasta
steps.text: Boil the pappardelle in salted water (or leftover pork cooking liquid if you have it) according to package directions. Drain well.

steps.title: Toss with butter
steps.text: Return the pasta to the pot. Add butter and toss gently until the pasta is coated and glossy.

steps.title: Add arugula and cheese
steps.text: Add the arugula and Parmesan, toss gently to combine, then transfer to a serving bowl. Serve alongside the Pork Ragu.

steps.title: Toast grains
steps.text: Toast oats, almonds, cinnamon, and salt in a large skillet over medium heat, stirring occasionally, until fragrant, 7–8 minutes. Transfer to a large bowl.

steps.title: Add dried fruit
steps.text: Toss the toasted oat mixture with cherries, coconut, and brown sugar.

steps.title: Bind with syrup
steps.text: Pour maple syrup over the mixture and stir to coat evenly.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Spread the granola on a lined baking sheet. Bake at 375° for 18 minutes, stirring halfway through, until golden and crispy.

steps.title: Cook pasta
steps.text: Boil penne in salted water following package time. Reserve 1/2 cup cooking water before draining.

steps.title: Sear shrimp
steps.text: Dust shrimp in flour, then sear in hot oil over high heat until golden and opaque, 4–5 minutes. Transfer to a plate and lower the heat to medium.

steps.title: Build sauce
steps.text: Stir in garlic and ginger for 30 seconds until fragrant. Add reserved pasta water, lemon zest and juice, and the cooked penne. Simmer until the sauce coats the pasta.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Off heat, toss in the watercress and shrimp until the greens wilt.

steps.title: Heat skillet
steps.text: Preheat the oven to 425° with an 8-inch cast-iron skillet inside.

steps.title: Mix cheese
steps.text: Combine Cheddar and pepper Jack in a small bowl.

steps.title: Make batter
steps.text: Whisk cornmeal, flour, salt and baking powder together. In a separate bowl, whisk 1/2 cup of the cheese mixture with buttermilk, egg and chiles. Fold wet into dry until just combined.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Pour batter into the hot skillet, smooth the top, then bake until a skewer comes out clean, about 20 minutes. Top with remaining cheese, cover and let it melt for 3 minutes. Garnish with chives.

steps.title: Make honey butter
steps.text: Process 1½ sticks of butter with 1/3 cup honey in a food processor until smooth. Season with salt, wrap in plastic and roll into a log. Chill for 1 hour or until firm.

steps.title: Prepare skillet
steps.text: Preheat oven to 425° and coat an 8-inch cast-iron skillet with nonstick spray.

steps.title: Mix batter
steps.text: Whisk together cornmeal, flour, baking powder and salt. In a separate bowl, combine eggs, buttermilk, 1/4 cup honey and melted butter; stir into dry ingredients until just combined.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Pour batter into the prepared skillet and bake until lightly browned and the top springs back when touched, 15–20 minutes.

steps.title: Heat broth
steps.text: Bring broth and milk to a boil in a large saucepan.

steps.title: Add cornmeal
steps.text: Whisk in cornmeal slowly to avoid lumps, then reduce heat to low and continue whisking for 5 minutes.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Remove from heat, then stir in Parmesan, mascarpone and sage. Season with salt and pepper.

steps.title: Soften aromatics
steps.text: Sauté onion and garlic in oil over medium-high heat until the onion begins to soften, about 3 minutes.

steps.title: Wilt greens
steps.text: Add spinach and arugula, tossing with tongs until wilted.

steps.title: Add peppers
steps.text: Stir in banana peppers and raisins, then season with salt and black pepper.

steps.title: Render bacon
steps.text: Cook bacon in a sauté pan until crisp; transfer to a paper-towel-lined plate and keep 2 Tbsp. drippings in the pan.

steps.title: Sauté squash
steps.text: Sauté the chayote in the drippings over medium-high heat until tender, 15–20 minutes. Add onions and chile, cooking until softened, 3–4 minutes more.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Stir in lime juice, cilantro and crumbled bacon. Season with salt and pepper.

steps.title: Prepare bread
steps.text: Preheat the broiler to high with the rack 6 inches from the element. Brush both sides of each bread slice with oil and season one side with salt and pepper.

steps.title: Broil
steps.text: Broil until golden on both sides, flipping halfway through, about 4 minutes total.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: While still hot, rub the toasts with a lemon half, gently squeezing as you rub. Top with lemon zest and serve immediately.

steps.title: Make vinaigrette
steps.text: Whisk together vinegar, oil, shallots, sage and honey in a small bowl. Season with salt and pepper.

steps.title: Prep salad
steps.text: Cut cucumber into chunks and place in a large bowl with salad greens, raisins and pumpkin seeds.

steps.title: Dress and serve
steps.text: Pour vinaigrette over the salad greens and toss well to coat.

steps.title: Cook bacon
steps.text: In a skillet over medium-high heat, cook the bacon until crisp and dark, then transfer to paper towels. When cool enough to handle, crumble it into bite-sized pieces.

steps.title: Build the base
steps.text: Pour off most of the bacon fat, leaving 1 Tbsp in the pan. Add the scallion whites and cook over medium heat for about 1 minute until they yield. Move to a large bowl and add the onion dip, Cheddar, milk, scallion greens, and cream cheese. Stir in the hash browns and crumbled bacon; taste and season with salt and pepper.

steps.title: Prep dish
steps.text: Coat a 9×13-inch baking dish with nonstick spray and pour in the hash brown mixture. Toss the corn flakes with melted butter, season with salt and pepper, and scatter over the top.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Bake at 350° until the surface is golden and bubbling at the edges, about 45 minutes.

steps.title: Make feta dip
steps.text: Pulse the yogurt, feta, 2 tsp oil, and minced garlic in a food processor until the mixture turns creamy and smooth. Taste and adjust with salt and pepper.

steps.title: Prepare and grill
steps.text: Heat the grill to medium and brush the grate with oil. Brush the pitas on both sides with 2 Tbsp oil and season with salt and pepper. Grill for 1–2 minutes per side until marked and warm.

steps.title: Finish and serve
steps.text: Rub the grilled pitas with the cut side of a raw garlic clove to infuse them. Cut each into four wedges and scatter chopped parsley over both the pitas and the dip.

steps.title: Make compound butter
steps.text: In a bowl, beat together the butter, oil, grated Parmesan, and minced garlic until well mixed. Season with salt, black pepper, and a pinch of pepper flakes.

steps.title: Spread and broil
steps.text: Spread the butter mixture generously on the cut sides of the bread and lay the slices on a foil-lined baking sheet. Broil 6 inches from the element on high until lightly toasted, 1–2 minutes.

steps.title: Garnish
steps.text: Scatter chopped scallions over the hot bread. Cut into single servings and serve at once.

steps.title: Toast baguette
steps.text: Brush both sides of the baguette slices with 2 tsp oil and season with salt and pepper. Arrange on a baking sheet and broil 6 inches from the element on high until golden, about 1 minute per side.

steps.title: Make dressing
steps.text: Whisk together 1 Tbsp oil, vinegar, and minced garlic in a small bowl; season with salt and pepper. Pour over the mozzarella, tomatoes, and torn basil and toss gently.

steps.title: Top and finish
steps.text: Divide the tomato mixture among the toasted slices and return to the broiler just long enough for the cheese to soften and start bubbling, about 1 minute.

steps.title: Toast base
steps.text: Brush both sides of the baguette slices with oil and season with salt and pepper. Lay on a baking sheet and broil 6 inches from the element on high until golden, about 1 minute per side.

steps.title: Top slices
steps.text: Spread 1 tsp of Boursin onto each toasted slice and sprinkle 2 tsp of grated Parmesan over the top.

steps.title: Broil until melted
steps.text: Return to the broiler until the cheese bubbles and begins to brown at the edges, 1–2 minutes.

steps.title: Prepare relish
steps.text: Mix the sauerkraut, sliced scallions, grated carrot, vinegar, and caraway seeds in a bowl and let sit while you grill.

steps.title: Grill
steps.text: Heat the grill to medium and brush the grate with oil. Grill the hot dogs to your preferred doneness, then toast the buns for about 1 minute until warmed and marked.

steps.title: Assemble and serve
steps.text: Nestle each hot dog into a bun and top with the relish, pickle spears, and a good squirt of mustard.

steps.title: Marinate beef
steps.text: In a large bowl, combine the vinegar, soy sauce, brown sugar, ginger, minced garlic, sesame oil, and cornstarch. Add the thinly sliced steak and toss to coat evenly. Let rest for 20 minutes, stirring often, so the flavors penetrate.

steps.title: Cook bulgogi
steps.text: Heat canola oil in a nonstick skillet over high heat until shimmering. Working in 2 or 3 batches, add the beef and shake the pan often for 2–3 minutes per batch until browned and caramelized. Return all the meat to the skillet briefly to warm through.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Transfer to a serving plate and scatter sesame seeds over the top. Serve with Korean Rice Bowl and Korean Chili Sauce.

steps.title: Prep potatoes
steps.text: Rinse the potatoes under cold running water, rubbing them between your hands until the water runs clear. Pat dry thoroughly on a clean towel and cut into fries.

steps.title: First fry
steps.text: Heat oil in a large pot to 325° (about one-third full). Line one baking sheet with paper towels. Fry the potatoes until tender and just starting to crisp, 5–6 minutes. Spread on the towel-lined sheet to drain, let sit in one layer for 10 minutes, then raise the oil temperature to 375°.

steps.title: Second fry and finish
steps.text: Return the fries to the hot oil and fry until crisp and golden all over, 2 minutes. Drain on a fresh paper-towel-lined sheet and finish generously with salt.

steps.title: Mix spice blend
steps.text: In a large bowl, combine the ground pork, brown sugar, minced garlic, sage, salt, fennel seeds, pepper flakes, and nutmeg. Mix until the spices are evenly distributed but do not overwork the meat.

steps.title: Shape and chill
steps.text: Split the mixture evenly and hand-form each portion into a compact log. Wrap each one tightly in plastic film and set in the fridge to firm up—at least 1 hour, or overnight for best results.

steps.title: Cook patties
steps.text: Slice each log into six patties, reshaping gently with your hands if needed. Coat a nonstick skillet with nonstick spray and fry the patties over medium-high heat for 5–7 minutes per side until cooked through. Transfer to paper towels to cool.

steps.title: Cook rice
steps.text: Boil the rice according to package directions, then fold in vinegar and sesame seeds while hot.

steps.title: Make the broth
steps.text: Combine stock, tamarind paste, garlic, lemongrass, and ginger in a pot. Bring to a boil, then drop the heat to medium and simmer for 20 minutes. Fish out the lemongrass and ginger.

steps.title: Add tofu and vegetables
steps.text: Stir in tofu, tomatoes, and mushrooms, cook 2 minutes, then add coconut milk, basil, cilantro, scallions, chili garlic sauce, and soy sauce. Heat through gently.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Divide the rice among bowls and ladle the soup over. Pass lime wedges at table.

steps.title: Cook pasta
steps.text: Boil the angel hair in salted water following the package time. Reserve ¼ cup pasta water before draining.

steps.title: Make the sauce
steps.text: Whisk together cream, Parmesan, butter, and zest in a large bowl. Season with salt, black pepper, and pepper flakes, then add spinach.

steps.title: Toss
steps.text: Add the drained pasta and reserved water to the bowl, tossing gently until the spinach wilts. Garnish with walnuts.

steps.title: Cook mushrooms
steps.text: Heat oil in a 10–12 inch nonstick skillet over medium-high. Add mushrooms and garlic; cook 3–4 minutes until the mushrooms give up their liquid. Stir in tomatoes, cook 2 minutes more, then season and transfer to a bowl. Wipe the skillet clean.

steps.title: Assemble
steps.text: On each tortilla, layer ½ cup cheese, ½ cup mushroom mixture, and 1 Tbsp. scallions. Fold in half. Coat the skillet with nonstick spray.

steps.title: Cook and cut
steps.text: Arrange 2 quesadillas in the skillet and cook over medium-high heat until the cheese melts and the tortillas brown. Flip and cook the other side. Transfer to a board, cut into fourths, then repeat with the remaining quesadillas.

steps.title: Cook pasta
steps.text: Get the spaghetti going in a large pot of salted boiling water, following the package timing. Before draining, set aside ½ cup of the cooking water.

steps.title: Sear scallops
steps.text: In a sauté pan with 2 Tbsp. oil over medium-high, get the scallops golden on both sides—3–4 minutes per side. Move them to a plate and tent with foil.

steps.title: Build sauce
steps.text: Keeping the same pan, warm the remaining 2 Tbsp. oil and flash-cook garlic, thyme, and pepper flakes until fragrant, about 30 seconds. Tip the tomatoes, wine, lemon juice, and any scallop juices into the pan. Bring to a simmer.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Put the spaghetti in to warm through, loosening it with the reserved pasta water to reach the consistency you want. Finish with parsley and serve with the scallops on top.

steps.title: Make the sauce
steps.text: Whisk together mayonnaise, ketchup, lemon juice, scallions, horseradish, relish, and Worcestershire sauce.

steps.title: Add shrimp
steps.text: Fold the shrimp, bell pepper, and celery into the sauce. Season with salt and a pinch of cayenne.

steps.title: Build sandwiches
steps.text: Layer lettuce, the shrimp mixture, and avocado slices on rolls.

steps.title: Prepare grill
steps.text: Heat the grill to medium and brush the grate with oil.

steps.title: Make the mustard
steps.text: Stir together mustard and preserves.

steps.title: Make the relish
steps.text: Combine fresh pineapple, onion, tomato, and cilantro in a bowl.

steps.title: Grill
steps.text: Grill the hot dogs to your preferred doneness. Toast the buns for 1 minute until lightly golden.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Put each hot dog in a bun and top with the mustard, relish, and avocado.

steps.title: Prepare beans
steps.text: Soak beans in 3 cups water overnight. Next day, add ¼ tsp. baking soda and bring to a boil over high heat. Reduce heat and simmer 5 minutes, skimming any foam from the top. Drain, reserving 1¼ cups liquid. Transfer beans and liquid to a 4–6 qt. slow cooker.

steps.title: Brown the meat
steps.text: In a large skillet, brown the chuck with all the spices—onion, garlic, cumin, paprika, chili powder, salt, oregano, and cayenne—in oil over medium-high heat, 8–10 minutes. Pour off the fat, slide the mixture into the slow cooker without stirring, cover, and let it go on high for 3 hours until the beans turn creamy and tender.

steps.title: Add toppings
steps.text: Stir in tomatoes and corn, then stir in tomato paste. Top the filling with cornbread batter. Cover and cook on low until a toothpick comes out clean from the center of the cornbread, 1 hour. Top with cheese and chives; cover until the cheese melts, about 5 minutes.

steps.title: Prep
steps.text: Turn the oven on to 450°. Run the mini food processor with 2 Tbsp. oil, 2 Tbsp. walnuts, shallots, vinegar, Dijon, and honey until the walnuts break down fine. Season your vinaigrette with salt and pepper.

steps.title: Sear and roast
steps.text: Heat remaining 1 Tbsp. oil in an ovenproof skillet over high heat. Sear the steak until browned on one side, 2 minutes. Flip it, transfer the skillet to the oven, and roast to medium-rare, 3 minutes. Let it rest 5 minutes, then slice.

steps.title: Assemble
steps.text: Toss romaine with blue cheese, apple, the remaining 4 Tbsp. walnuts, and the vinaigrette. Serve with the sliced steak.

steps.title: Toast oats and nuts
steps.text: Heat the oven to 350°. Spread oats on one baking sheet and walnuts on another. Toast both until golden and fragrant, about 15 minutes. Line a third sheet with parchment paper.

steps.title: Make the glaze
steps.text: In a skillet over medium heat, combine brown sugar, marmalade, cinnamon, ginger, nutmeg, zest, orange juice, and salt. Stir until the sugar dissolves, 3–4 minutes.

steps.title: Coat
steps.text: Toss the toasted oats and walnuts with cranberries and coconut flakes, then pour the glaze over and toss until everything is coated. Spread on the prepared sheet in a single layer.

steps.title: Bake and cool
steps.text: Bake until golden brown, 30 minutes, stirring halfway through. Press into clumps if you like, then let cool on the sheet. Store in an airtight container.

steps.title: Bloom the aromatics
steps.text: Cook the scallions, ginger, garlic, and pepper flakes in oil in a saucepan over medium-low for 1 minute until fragrant.

steps.title: Toast the rice
steps.text: Stir in the rice to coat it well with oil and cook 1 minute. Raise the heat to high and add water and tea bags, bringing the water to a boil.

steps.title: Simmer and rest
steps.text: Once boiling, drop the heat to low and clamp the lid down. The rice will cook gently for about 20 minutes as it absorbs all the liquid. When done, take it off the flame and let it rest under the lid for another 10 minutes.

steps.title: Season and serve
steps.text: Remove and discard the tea bags. Fold in salt, black pepper, and vinegar, then scatter the scallions over the top.

steps.title: Cook the pasta
steps.text: Boil the cavatappi in salted water following the package directions, then drain.

steps.title: Make the tofu cream
steps.text: Throw the tofu, onion, and garlic into a food processor and run it until the mixture becomes completely smooth with no lumps.

steps.title: Build the sauce
steps.text: Melt the butter in a large saucepan over medium heat. Whisk in the tofu purée, milk, mustard, and Tabasco, and warm it through. Once hot, add the Cheddar and stir until the cheese melts completely.

steps.title: Toss and season
steps.text: Stir the drained pasta into the cheese sauce to coat it evenly. Season with salt and pepper to taste.

steps.title: Mix the dry
steps.text: Whisk together the flour, baking soda, and salt in a large bowl.

steps.title: Mix the wet
steps.text: In a separate bowl, whisk the mashed bananas, buttermilk, sugar, butter, egg, and vanilla until combined.

steps.title: Combine and cook
steps.text: Fold the wet ingredients into the dry, stirring gently just until no flour streaks remain — overworking the batter makes tough pancakes. Set a griddle or nonstick pan to 375°, or use medium-low on the stovetop, and coat with nonstick spray. Working in batches, spoon batter onto the hot surface using 2 Tbsp. per pancake. Cook until bubbles break across the surface and the bottoms turn golden brown, roughly 4 minutes. Flip and give the other side 2 minutes to brown.

steps.title: Serve warm
steps.text: Serve the pancakes with Bananas Foster Syrup, sliced bananas, and pecans.

steps.title: Dredge the fillets
steps.text: Pat the flounder fillets dry and coat both sides in flour, shaking off the excess.

steps.title: Sear in batches
steps.text: Heat 2 tsp. oil in a nonstick skillet over medium-high until shimmering. Working in two batches, cook the fillets until golden, about 2 minutes per side. Set each batch on a platter and tent with foil.

steps.title: Make the sauce
steps.text: In the same skillet, add the wine, lemon juice, and capers and cook 30 seconds. Off the heat, swirl in the butter until it melts, then season with ½ tsp. pepper and ¼ tsp. salt.

steps.title: Plate and serve
steps.text: Spoon the sauce over the fillets and garnish each serving with parsley.

steps.title: Build the base
steps.text: Heat oil in a saucepan over medium-high and cook the onion, stirring, until it turns soft and golden, 3–5 minutes. Stir in the garlic and cook until you smell it, about 1 minute.

steps.title: Toast and cook
steps.text: Stir in the orzo to coat it with oil and cook 1–2 minutes. Pour in the broth and water, stirring often, and cook until the liquid is absorbed and the orzo is tender, 9–10 minutes.

steps.title: Finish and serve
steps.text: Off the heat, fold in the spinach, zest, butter, salt, pepper, and nutmeg, stirring until the spinach wilts into the warm orzo.

steps.title: Set up broiler
steps.text: Preheat the broiler to high with the rack positioned 6 inches from the element. Line a baking sheet with foil and lightly coat with nonstick spray.

steps.title: Make the glaze
steps.text: Whisk together the miso, vinegar, mirin, oil, brown sugar, ginger, and garlic until smooth.

steps.title: Prepare the fish
steps.text: Lay the salmon fillets skin side down on the prepared sheet. Spread the miso glaze evenly over the flesh side of each fillet.

steps.title: Broil and serve
steps.text: Broil until the glaze caramelizes and the center is just opaque, about 10 minutes. Using a fish spatula, transfer the fillets to a plate, leaving the skin behind. Scatter scallion greens over each serving.

steps.title: Heat the pan
steps.text: Heat oil in a nonstick skillet over medium-high until hot.

steps.title: Sauté the peas
steps.text: Add the peas and sauté until they turn crisp-tender and bright green, about 4 minutes.

steps.title: Season and serve
steps.text: Stir in the chili garlic sauce, sesame seeds, and salt, tossing until everything is coated evenly.

steps.title: Cook the shrimp
steps.text: Get 1 qt. water going in a saucepan over medium-high until it boils, then slip in the shrimp with their shells, the juice of 1 lime, and salt. Once you see them turn opaque and firm, 2–3 minutes, drain them. Dunk them into ice water to stop the cooking, then drain again. Chop half of them fine for the salad and keep the rest whole for garnish.

steps.title: Make the salsa
steps.text: Fold the tomatoes, cucumber, onion, olives, and minced cilantro into the chopped shrimp.

steps.title: Dress and serve
steps.text: Whisk together the ketchup, ⅓ cup lime juice, oil, and hot sauce. Toss this dressing with the shrimp mixture, then fold in the avocado at the last moment. Garnish each serving with whole shrimp.

steps.title: Prepare the dish
steps.text: Heat the oven to 425°. Coat a 1 qt. baking dish with nonstick spray.

steps.title: Make the filling
steps.text: In a saucepan, combine the pinto beans, refried beans, ½ cup Cheddar, salsa, and jalapeños. Heat over medium, stirring, until the cheese melts, 5–6 minutes. Season with salt and pepper.

steps.title: Assemble and bake
steps.text: Scrape the bean mixture into the prepared dish and sprinkle with the remaining ½ cup Cheddar. Bake until the cheese begins to brown, 12–15 minutes.

steps.title: Garnish and serve
steps.text: Scatter cilantro and scallions over the warm dip and serve with chips.

steps.title: Cook aromatics
steps.text: Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high and add celery and scallion whites. Cook until softened, 4–5 minutes. Add garlic and ginger; cook 1 minute more.

steps.title: Build the mixture
steps.text: Add ground sirloin, soy sauce, chili garlic sauce, and brown sugar. Crush the meat to a fine consistency with a potato masher and cook 5 minutes.

steps.title: Finish and serve
steps.text: Stir in water chestnuts, tomatoes, and hoisin. Crush the tomatoes with the masher, drop heat to medium, and cook until thickened, about 5 minutes. Off heat, stir in scallion greens and lime juice; season with salt. Serve on buns with cilantro.

steps.title: Make the sauce
steps.text: Blend yogurt with 1 Tbsp. each mint and cilantro, grated garlic, grated ginger, salt, and pepper.

steps.title: Toast the aromatics
steps.text: Use a food processor to mince the garlic, onion, and ginger. Heat oil in a large sauté pan over medium-high. Add the minced mixture with salt, black pepper, cardamom, and pepper flakes; cook until the onion dries and turns golden, 5 minutes. Cool.

steps.title: Form patties
steps.text: Pulse the ground sirloin to a fine consistency in the food processor, then combine with the cooled aromatics, ¼ cup each of mint and cilantro. Form the mixture into 12 patties, pressing each firmly.

steps.title: Sear patties
steps.text: Sear on a nonstick-sprayed griddle over medium heat, 8–10 minutes total, until browned on both sides.

steps.title: Plate and serve
steps.text: Place 3 patties on each flatbread and top with sauce, mint leaves, and cilantro sprigs.

steps.title: Prepare ramekins
steps.text: Coat eight 4-oz. ramekins with a mixture of 2 Tbsp. butter, 2 Tbsp. sugar, and cocoa; arrange on a baking sheet. Preheat oven to 450°.

steps.title: Melt chocolate
steps.text: Combine butter and chocolate in a double boiler over medium heat, stirring until smooth. Remove from heat, fold in vanilla, and set aside to cool 10 minutes, stirring from time to time.

steps.title: Make the batter
steps.text: In a bowl, whisk eggs, yolks, and 6 Tbsp. sugar on high speed until the mixture is pale and thick, 7 minutes. Sprinkle in flour, espresso powder, and salt; mix 30 seconds. Fold in the cooled chocolate until just combined.

steps.title: Fill ramekins
steps.text: Spoon a generous ⅓ cup batter into each prepared ramekin.

steps.title: Bake and turn out
steps.text: Bake until the sides are set and centers are sunken and soft, 8–9 minutes, rotating the pan halfway through. Cool 30 seconds; run a paring knife around the edges of each ramekin.

steps.title: Invert and finish
steps.text: Place an inverted plate over each cake and flip carefully. Wait 5 minutes while they cool in the ramekins, then unmold and serve at once.

steps.title: Make filling
steps.text: Dice 6 olives for garnish. Pulse the remaining olives, tomatoes, bread crumbs, zest, garlic, and oregano until minced.

steps.title: Pound and fill
steps.text: Place chicken between plastic sheets. Use the flat side of a meat mallet to pound it to ¼-inch thick. Distribute the filling over the flattened pieces. Roll up each one and fasten closed with toothpicks.

steps.title: Brown and braise
steps.text: Heat oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high. Sear the roulades until golden, 4 minutes, then move to a plate. Sauté the onion until soft, 2 minutes. Deglaze with wine and simmer until nearly dry, 1–2 minutes. Pour in broth, bring to a boil, add olives, and return roulades to pan.

steps.title: Finish sauce
steps.text: Reduce heat to medium-low, cover the pan, and cook the roulades gently 10 minutes. Take them out and set aside. Mix lemon juice and cornstarch into a smooth paste, then stir into the sauce; cook 1 minute more. Slice the roulades and serve with the sauce spooned over.

steps.title: Start broth
steps.text: Bring broth to a boil in a small saucepan.

steps.title: Cook orzo
steps.text: Add orzo and bring back to a boil. Continue cooking uncovered, stirring now and then, until all the broth has been absorbed, 9 minutes.

steps.title: Add cheese
steps.text: Off heat, stir in tomatoes and feta, mixing until the feta melts slightly. Season with salt and pepper. Serve with Chicken Roulades.

steps.title: Season and dredge
steps.text: Season chicken with salt and pepper. Mix panko with garlic and oregano; dredge both sides of chicken in the mixture.

steps.title: Make glaze
steps.text: Whisk together zest, lemon juice, honey, and Tabasco.

steps.title: Cook chicken
steps.text: Warm oil in a nonstick skillet over medium heat. Cook the chicken, turning once, until the outside is golden and the meat is cooked through, 6 minutes per side. Move to a plate.

steps.title: Reduce glaze
steps.text: Add lemon mixture to the skillet and reduce until syrupy, about 1 minute. Return chicken and toss to coat in the glaze.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve chicken with Pesto Green Beans.

steps.title: Set up
steps.text: Preheat broiler with rack 6–8 inches from the element. Coat an 8-inch square baking dish with nonstick spray.

steps.title: Cook filling
steps.text: In a nonstick skillet over medium-high, cook bell pepper, onion, and garlic in oil until the onion is tender, 3 minutes. Stir in spinach, turkey, and corn; cook 2 minutes until the spinach collapses.

steps.title: Thicken filling
steps.text: Sprinkle flour over the mixture and add milk; simmer 2 minutes until thickened. Stir in neufchatel, salt, and black pepper.

steps.title: Assemble
steps.text: Warm salsa in a small skillet over medium. Dip each tortilla quickly in the hot salsa, lay it sauce-side up in the baking dish, add ¼ cup filling to the center, roll, and lay seam-side down. Repeat until all tortillas are filled.

steps.title: Broil and finish
steps.text: Pour remaining salsa over the enchiladas and top with feta. Broil 3 minutes and garnish with scallions.

steps.title: Zest citrus
steps.text: Zest an orange and a lime; set the zests aside.

steps.title: Make dressing
steps.text: Whisk together the zests, orange juice, lime juice, sugar, salt, and Tabasco.

steps.title: Plate and serve
steps.text: Arrange tomatoes on two plates. Pour the dressing over each portion and top with chives.

steps.title: Marinate pork
steps.text: Toss pork strips with 1 Tbsp. soy sauce, cover, and refrigerate while you prepare the other components.

steps.title: Mix sauce
steps.text: Whisk together remaining 2 Tbsp. soy sauce, broth, sherry, cornstarch, honey, tomato paste, and pepper.

steps.title: Cook pork
steps.text: Preheat wok over medium-high. Spray with nonstick spray. Add 1 tsp. oil and stir-fry half the pork until cooked through, 2–3 minutes. Move to a plate. Stir-fry remaining pork; add to the plate.

steps.title: Start vegetables
steps.text: Pour the remaining oil into the wok. Quick-fry the garlic and ginger, 10–15 seconds, then add snow peas and cook 2 minutes.

steps.title: Finish stir-fry
steps.text: Return pork and add sauce; cook until thickened, 1–2 minutes. Add carrots and stir-fry 1 minute.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve stir-fry over Pineapple-Ginger Brown Rice and scatter scallions and sesame seeds over each serving.

steps.title: Bring to boil
steps.text: Bring water, pineapple juice, ginger, and rice to a boil in a saucepan over medium-high heat.

steps.title: Simmer rice
steps.text: Lower heat to medium-low, cover, and simmer until the water is absorbed, 10–12 minutes.

steps.title: Finish rice
steps.text: Fluff rice with a fork. Fold in pineapple, soy sauce, sesame oil, and salt. Serve with Pork Stir-Fry.

steps.title: Brown the chops
