steps.text: Season the pork with salt and pepper. Heat oil in a skillet over medium-high and brown the chops 5 minutes per side. Transfer to a plate and tent loosely with foil.

steps.title: Build the sauce
steps.text: In the same pan, sauté the apples and onion for 4–5 minutes. Stir in the mustard, cinnamon and salt until fragrant, then add apple juice and lemon juice. Cook until the apples soften.

steps.title: Finish and serve
steps.text: Return the chops and their juices to the skillet. Cook uncovered to an internal temperature of 155°. Spoon the apple mixture over each chop and scatter toasted pecans on top.

steps.title: Render the bacon
steps.text: Cook the bacon in a skillet until crisp, then transfer to paper towel to drain and cool. Crumble when it's dry.

steps.title: Cook and dry potatoes
steps.text: Boil the potatoes in salted water, covered, until tender (12–15 minutes). Drain well, then return to the pot. Stir over medium heat for about 1 minute to evaporate any remaining moisture.

steps.title: Mash and finish
steps.text: Off the heat, add milk, yogurt and salt to the potatoes. Mash until smooth, fold in the crumbled bacon and 2 Tbsp. Cheddar. Garnish with the last tablespoon of Cheddar and scallions.

steps.title: Sear steaks, make sauce
steps.text: Season the filets with salt and press peppercorns onto one side. Heat oil in a sauté pan over medium-high, cook the filets 3–4 minutes per side for medium-rare, then transfer to a plate and tent with foil. Off heat, add bourbon and return to heat; simmer until the liquid reduces by half (about 1 minute). Add broth and shallots, simmer 2–3 minutes. Stir in the half-and-half, mustard and any drippings from the filets.

steps.title: Sauté vegetables
steps.text: Heat oil in a large skillet over medium. Sauté the tomatoes and garlic until fragrant (1–2 minutes), then add the spinach and cook until wilted, about 2 minutes.

steps.title: Season and plate
steps.text: Season the spinach mixture with lemon juice, salt and pepper. Serve the steak with the sauce, vegetables and galettes on the side.

steps.title: Season vegetables
steps.text: Toss the potatoes and parsnips with oil, salt and pepper to coat evenly.

steps.title: Layer in skillet
steps.text: Spray a large skillet and place it over medium heat. Layer the potatoes and parsnips in two overlapping circles about 5 inches wide, working through all the slices.

steps.title: Brown and finish
steps.text: Cook uncovered until the bottoms are light brown (12–14 minutes). Raise the heat to medium-high, cook 3 minutes more, then carefully flip the galettes. Cook until tender, about 5 minutes more.

steps.title: Soften onion
steps.text: Heat oil in a skillet over medium. Add the onion and cook until it begins to soften, about 3–5 minutes.

steps.title: Cook peas
steps.text: Add the peas and cook for 3 minutes, stirring gently.

steps.title: Mash and finish
steps.text: Off the heat, add the cream cheese and mint. Mash everything together with a potato masher until well combined, then season with salt to taste.

steps.title: Prepare grill
steps.text: Heat the grill to high and brush the grate with oil.

steps.title: Spice the ham
steps.text: Combine brown sugar, paprika, granulated garlic, black pepper and cayenne. Rub the spice mixture onto both sides of the ham steak.

steps.title: Blacken ham
steps.text: Grill the ham steak covered until blackened, 4–5 minutes per side.

steps.title: Make vinaigrette
steps.text: Whisk together the lemon zest, lime juice, oil, honey and vinegar. Season with salt and pepper. Set aside 3 Tbsp. for any potato wedges.

steps.title: Assemble salad
steps.text: Toss the arugula, cantaloupe, honeydew, cucumbers, mozzarella, basil and mint with the vinaigrette. Serve the salad with the blackened ham steak.

steps.title: Make citrus syrup
steps.text: Heat the water, sugar and orange and lemon zests in a saucepan over medium until the sugar dissolves. Off the heat, stir in the orange juice and lemon juice, then chill.

steps.title: Add soda
steps.text: Just before serving, strain the chilled mixture and add the club soda.

steps.title: Mix and serve
steps.text: Pour the citrus soda and Campari into a pitcher with a pinch of salt and stir gently. Distribute across ice-filled glasses and crown each with an orange slice.

steps.title: Make vinaigrette
steps.text: Whisk together the lemon zest, lemon juice, oil and garlic. Season with salt and pepper. Reserve 3 Tbsp. to brush on the mushrooms.

steps.title: Cook bulgur
steps.text: Cook the bulgur according to package directions, then transfer to a baking sheet and let cool.

steps.title: Prepare grill
steps.text: Heat the grill to medium-high and brush the grate with oil.

steps.title: Assemble tabbouleh
steps.text: Combine the tomatoes, cucumber, chickpeas, parsley, scallions, mint, olives and cooled bulgur. Toss with the vinaigrette and chill until ready to serve.

steps.title: Grill mushrooms
steps.text: Coat the portobello caps on both sides with the reserved vinaigrette and season with salt and pepper. Set on the grill uncovered; they're done when marked and tender (about 2 minutes per side).

steps.title: Plate and serve
steps.text: Slice the grilled mushrooms into ½-inch-thick strips and serve on top of the tabbouleh, crumbled feta scattered over.

steps.title: Make dressing
steps.text: Whisk together the lemon zest, lemon juice, oil, parsley and honey in a small bowl. Season to taste with salt and pepper.

steps.title: Prepare berries and nuts
steps.text: Slice the strawberries and roughly chop or halve the pistachios, keeping some texture. Place in a serving bowl.

steps.title: Toss and serve
steps.text: Pour the dressing over the strawberries and pistachios and toss gently to coat. Serve at once.

steps.title: Sweat onions and garlic
steps.text: Heat oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Cook the onion, stirring, until it softens, about 3–4 minutes. Stir in the garlic and cook 1 minute more.

steps.title: Add tomatoes
steps.text: Add the tomatoes and cook, stirring, until they break down, about 4–5 minutes.

steps.title: Finish with vinegar and spice
steps.text: Pour in the vinegar and let it bubble down by half. Stir in the Dijon, honey, and cayenne. Bring to a boil, then lower the heat and simmer, stirring now and then, until the sauce thickens, about 5 minutes.

steps.title: Make vinaigrette
steps.text: Whisk together the oil, cumin, oregano, salt, black pepper, paprika, and lemon juice. Toss the green beans, corn, and bell pepper in the vinaigrette.

steps.title: Shape foil basket
steps.text: Fold a 36×18-inch foil sheet to make a 12×18-inch basket, then fold up the edges. Lay the coated vegetables in the basket.

steps.title: Grill until crisp-tender
steps.text: Set the basket on a grill preheated to medium-high. Cook, stirring occasionally, until the vegetables are crisp-tender, about 10 minutes.

steps.title: Cook potatoes
steps.text: Boil the potatoes in salted water until a fork goes through, about 10 minutes. Drain.

steps.title: Cool and combine
steps.text: Rinse the potatoes with cold water, then drain again. In a large bowl, toss the potatoes with the onion, yogurt, mayonnaise, goat cheese, zest, lemon juice, and thyme.

steps.title: Chill before serving
steps.text: Cover and refrigerate until you are ready to serve.

steps.title: Macerate the fruit
steps.text: Toss the strawberries and pineapple with the Amaretto and lemon juice. Let them sit for 15 minutes so the flavours meld.

steps.title: Layer the trifles
steps.text: Lay half the angel food cake into each of four 1½-cup trifle dishes. Top each with half the macerated fruit, half the yogurt, and half the nuts. Repeat the layers once more.

steps.title: Garnish and serve
steps.text: Scatter mint over each trifle. Serve at once or chill until needed.

steps.title: Boil potatoes
steps.text: Cook the potatoes in salted boiling water for 30 minutes, until they are tender enough to break with a fork. Drain well.

steps.title: Mash with oil and aromatics
steps.text: Add the oil and smash the potatoes coarsely with a masher. Fold in the mayonnaise, garlic, lemon zest, lemon juice, and anchovy paste, mashing gently until everything is distributed. Stop when the potatoes still have some texture.

steps.title: Season with cheese and salt
steps.text: Fold in the Parmesan. Taste and adjust with salt and pepper.

steps.title: Whisk the dressing
steps.text: Whisk together the steak sauce, oil, vinegar, horseradish, and Dijon. Season with salt and pepper.

steps.title: Grill the onions
steps.text: Brush the onion slices with steak sauce. Set them on a grill preheated to medium-high, cover, and cook until they soften slightly, about 5 minutes. Chop them coarsely.

steps.title: Dress and serve
steps.text: Place the tomatoes and grilled onions in a bowl. Drizzle with the vinaigrette and scatter parsley over the top.

steps.title: Reduce the cream
steps.text: In a small saucepan over medium-high heat, simmer the cream with the garlic and pepper flakes until it reduces to about ⅔ cup, roughly 10 minutes.

steps.title: Process spinach and herbs
steps.text: In a food processor, pulse the spinach, parsley, oil, and lemon juice until coarsely chopped. Add the hot cream and pulse again until the spinach is finely minced.

steps.title: Season and serve
steps.text: Taste and season with salt and black pepper. Serve warm.

steps.title: Mix dry ingredients
steps.text: Whisk the flour, baking powder, salt, and baking soda together. Heat your oven to 425°.

steps.title: Make the dough
steps.text: Rub the cold butter and shortening into the flour mixture with your fingertips until the pieces are pea-sized. Stir in the buttermilk gently, then turn the shaggy dough onto a floured surface and knead it just until it comes together. Pat it to 1 inch thick and cut out biscuits with a 2¾-inch-round cutter. Set them on a baking sheet.

steps.title: Bake until golden
steps.text: Bake until the biscuits are golden, 14–15 minutes. Brush or drizzle with the Sriracha-Honey Butter before serving.

steps.title: Make vinaigrette
steps.text: Whisk rice vinegar, oil, garlic, ginger, sugar, and chili powder together; season with salt. Set aside.

steps.title: Acidulate and soak
steps.text: Combine cold water and distilled vinegar, then divide into thirds. Trim and peel the lotus root, slice into ¼-inch rounds, and place in the first third of the acidulated water as you cut it to prevent browning.

steps.title: Blanch lotus
steps.text: Bring the second third of acidulated water to a boil, then drain and add the lotus. Cover and let it sit 10 minutes. Drain again, rinse well, then immerse in the final third of cold acidulated water and allow to cool.

steps.title: Dress and serve
steps.text: Pat the lotus dry; toss with vinaigrette and cilantro. Serve cold.

steps.title: Make sauce and prep
steps.text: Heat grill to medium and brush the grate with oil. Whisk mayonnaise, hot sauce, and lemon juice together; set aside.

steps.title: Grill hot dogs and buns
steps.text: Grill hot dogs until done, then grill buns until lightly toasted, about 1 minute.

steps.title: Assemble
steps.text: Set each hot dog in a bun, top with sauce, diced celery, blue cheese, and celery leaves.

steps.title: Make pimento cheese
steps.text: Blend Cheddar, mayonnaise, and cream cheese in a food processor until entirely smooth. Add pimentos and pulse just to combine without overworking; season with Tabasco.

steps.title: Prep grill
steps.text: Heat grill to medium and brush the grate with oil.

steps.title: Wrap and grill hot dogs
steps.text: Wrap bacon around each hot dog and secure the ends with toothpicks. Grill until the bacon is crisp, then remove toothpicks. Grill buns until lightly toasted, about 1 minute.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Set each hot dog in a bun with romaine and a generous dollop of pimento cheese.

steps.title: Heat oven
steps.text: Get oven to 500° with a baking stone positioned on the lowest rack — give it 30 minutes to preheat. Ready the pie dough as directed.

steps.title: Make cream filling
steps.text: Use a mixer to beat cream cheese with 1 egg until smooth. Incorporate ½ cup cream of coconut and beat again until smooth; spread this across the crust bottom. Drop oven to 400°.

steps.title: Top with blueberry mixture
steps.text: Combine the remaining ½ cup cream of coconut with lemon juice, tapioca, and coconut extract, whisking to blend. Coat the blueberries in this mixture, then scatter over the cream cheese.

steps.title: Cut and arrange topping
steps.text: Roll the remaining dough to a 12-inch square and cut into 2½×2½-inch squares (you will have extra). Mix 1 egg with cream and brush over each square.

steps.title: Checkerboard pattern
steps.text: Overlap the dough squares on the pie in diagonal lines to make a checkerboard pattern. Dust the surface with sugar.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Bake 35–40 minutes until the top is golden. Let cool entirely before slicing.

steps.title: Make salsa
steps.text: Combine orange segments, tomatoes, onion, cilantro, serrano, and a pinch of salt in a bowl. Chill until ready to serve.

steps.title: Prep grill and steak
steps.text: Heat grill to medium-high and brush the grate with oil. Mix chili powder, oregano, 1 tsp salt, and black pepper; stir in vinegar and rub the paste over both sides of the steak.

steps.title: Grill steak
steps.text: Put steaks on grill with lid down, cook 4–5 minutes on each side for medium-rare doneness. Tent with foil and rest 5 minutes.

steps.title: Slice and serve
steps.text: Cut thinly against the grain. Plate the meat and crown with salsa.

steps.title: Sauté collards
steps.text: Warm oil in a large sauté pan over medium-high until it shimmers. Cook garlic for 30 seconds, then add collard greens and toss with tongs until wilted, 3–4 minutes.

steps.title: Add broth and beans
steps.text: Pour in broth and simmer until the liquid evaporates. Stir in beans and season with salt and pepper flakes; cook until the beans are heated through.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Drizzle in vinegar and serve.

steps.title: Make marinade
steps.text: Whisk soy sauce, rice vinegar, molasses, garlic, ginger, sesame oil, and 2 tsp chili garlic sauce together. Pour into a baking dish.

steps.title: Marinate steaks
steps.text: Add steaks and marinate uncovered for 10–15 minutes, flipping every 2 minutes.

steps.title: Make kimchi
steps.text: Combine distilled vinegar and 1 Tbsp chili garlic sauce in a large bowl; add pears, cucumbers, bell pepper, and onion. Toss until coated and chill until ready to serve.

steps.title: Grill steaks
steps.text: Heat grill to medium-high and brush the grate with oil. Grill steaks covered, 3–4 minutes per side for medium-rare. Tent with foil and let rest 5 minutes.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Set steaks on plates with kimchi alongside and garnish with sesame seeds.

steps.title: Make dipping sauce
steps.text: Whisk together soy sauce, lemon juice, chili garlic sauce, and sesame oil; set aside.

steps.title: Make batter
steps.text: Combine eggs, water, and flour in a bowl, stirring until smooth. Fold in scallions and bean sprouts.

steps.title: Cook pancake
steps.text: Heat vegetable oil in a 10-inch nonstick skillet over medium-high until shimmering. Pour in the batter and cook until the bottom is brown, 7–8 minutes. Flip and brown the other side, 7–8 minutes more.

steps.title: Cut and serve
steps.text: Cut into 8 wedges and serve with dipping sauce.

steps.title: Cook pasta
steps.text: Boil pasta in salted water following package directions. Run through a sieve to drain, rinse under cool water, then transfer to a bowl.

steps.title: Toast almonds and combine
steps.text: Brown almonds in a small nonstick skillet over medium heat with frequent stirring, 3–4 minutes. Toss into the pasta along with onion, mint, capers, and orange zest.

steps.title: Make vinaigrette and dress
steps.text: Combine orange juice and oil, whisking together. Pour over the salad and toss to coat; taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Divide among four plates and serve with fresh orange or tomato slices.

steps.title: Season the chops
steps.text: Mix paprika, black pepper, and salt together, then coat both sides of the pork chops evenly with the mixture.

steps.title: Brown in skillet
steps.text: Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high. Add the chops and brown, 3 minutes per side. Transfer to a plate.

steps.title: Finish with wine
steps.text: Pour wine into the skillet and let it simmer until almost all the liquid evaporates, about 2 minutes, scraping the browned bits as it cooks. Return the chops, check they register 145° on an instant-read thermometer near the bone, tent with foil, and rest 3 minutes before serving with the pan sauce.

steps.title: Pound the pork
steps.text: Slice the pork tenderloin into 4 thick pieces. Butterfly each one, place between plastic sheets, and pound to an even ¼ inch thickness using the flat of a mallet.

steps.title: Sear pork
steps.text: Warm 2 teaspoons oil in a nonstick skillet to medium-high heat. Once it shimmers, cook the pork, flipping halfway through, until the outside is lightly browned and the inside cooked through, 3–4 minutes on each side. Set the pork on a plate and cover loosely with foil.

steps.title: Cook vegetables
steps.text: In the same skillet, sauté the radishes in the remaining 1 teaspoon oil until they begin to soften, about 2 minutes. Add the shallots and stir for another 30 seconds.

steps.title: Reduce Madeira
steps.text: Pour in the Madeira and simmer until it reduces to about half its original volume. Using a slotted spoon, transfer the radishes to the plate with the pork.

steps.title: Make sauce
steps.text: Pour the broth into the reduced Madeira in the skillet; whisk in the cream and Dijon mustard until smooth. Let it simmer gently for a moment until it thickens slightly, then stir in 1 tablespoon tarragon. Plate the pork and radishes, spoon sauce around them, and scatter the remaining tarragon over each serving.

steps.title: Cook barley
steps.text: Pour 1 cup grape juice and 1 cup water into a medium saucepan and bring to a rolling boil over high heat. Add barley and salt, then lower the heat, cover, and let it simmer gently until the liquid is nearly all absorbed and the grains are tender, 14–16 minutes. Drain well and rinse.

steps.title: Combine
steps.text: Toss the cooked barley with grapes and fresh spinach in a large bowl.

steps.title: Dress and chill
steps.text: Whisk together ⅓ cup grape juice, vinegar, Dijon, honey, and ⅛ teaspoon salt. Pour over the barley mixture, toss well, and refrigerate until ready to serve.

steps.title: Make glaze
steps.text: In a saucepan over medium heat, combine barbecue sauce, jam, brown sugar, vinegar, and 1 chipotle in adobo, chopped. Simmer until it thickens, about 5 minutes. Add fresh cherries and cook for another 2 minutes. Finish with lime juice.

steps.title: Prep grill
steps.text: Heat your grill to medium-high and brush the grate with oil. Coat the chicken with nonstick spray and season with salt.

steps.title: Grill chicken
steps.text: Grill the chicken, covered, 4 minutes per side until lightly cooked.

steps.title: Glaze and finish
steps.text: Brush both sides with the cherry glaze and grill until the glaze caramelizes and the chicken is cooked through, about 2 minutes more. Serve with the remaining sauce on the side.

steps.title: Shred vegetables
steps.text: Run the kohlrabi and carrot through a food processor (or work them over a box grater) to produce fine shreds.

steps.title: Combine with herbs
steps.text: Toss the shreds together in a large bowl with the chopped parsley and sliced scallions.

steps.title: Dress
steps.text: Whisk together mayonnaise, vinegar, Dijon, honey, celery seeds, salt, and cayenne. Pour over the vegetables, toss well to coat, and refrigerate. This slaw keeps up to 1 day ahead.

steps.title: Make piri-piri sauce
steps.text: Heat butter and oil in a small saucepan over medium. Add garlic, ginger, red pepper flakes, hot sauce, lemon zest, paprika, and salt. Simmer to cook the garlic through, 3–4 minutes, then add lemon juice and simmer another 2–3 minutes.

steps.title: Prep grill and shrimp
steps.text: Heat your grill to medium-high and brush the grate with oil. Toss the shrimp with ¼ cup of the sauce in a bowl.

steps.title: Grill shrimp
steps.text: Set the shrimp on the hot grill, covered, and cook until the surface turns pink and the flesh feels firm to the touch, about 1–2 minutes per side.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Remove from the grill and toss with the remaining sauce. Divide among four plates and serve.

steps.title: Sauté onion
steps.text: Heat oil in a saucepan over medium. Add the onion and sauté until softened, 4–5 minutes.

steps.title: Cook rice
steps.text: Stir in the rice and lemon zest; cook for 1 minute. Add the broth and bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and cook until the rice is tender, 15 minutes.

steps.title: Finish with spinach
steps.text: Remove from heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes. Add the spinach to the rice and toss with tongs until it wilts completely into the grains.

steps.title: Make topping
steps.text: Stir together lemon juice, grated Parmesan, 1 tablespoon oil, honey, salt, and red pepper flakes; set aside.

steps.title: Wrap fish
steps.text: Dry the tilapia fillets thoroughly with paper towels. Lay 2 sage leaves across each fillet, then wrap the bundle with 1 slice of prosciutto and fix it in place with a long toothpick. Brush the top of each package with 1 teaspoon oil.

steps.title: Prep grill
steps.text: Heat your grill to medium-high and brush the grate with oil.

steps.title: Grill fillets
steps.text: Grill the wrapped fillets, covered, until cooked through, 3–4 minutes per side. Remove toothpicks.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Divide the risotto and wrapped fillets among four plates. Scatter walnuts over both, then pour the lemon-Parmesan mixture across the fish and the risotto.

steps.title: Start risotto
steps.text: Get the grill going at medium-high and oil the grate well. Meanwhile, warm 1 tablespoon oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Toss in the shallots and let them cook until soft and translucent, 3–4 minutes. Add the rice and cook for another minute.

steps.title: Build risotto
steps.text: Pour in the wine and simmer, stirring constantly, until the liquid evaporates. Add ½ cup hot water and stir frequently until absorbed. Continue adding hot water in ½-cup increments, stirring often, waiting for each portion to be mostly absorbed before adding more, until the rice is tender and creamy—about 15–20 minutes total.

steps.title: Grill and finish
steps.text: Rub the broccolini with the remaining 1 tablespoon oil and place on the hot grill, covered. Turn it every minute or so until the edges blacken all around, about 5 minutes. Chop into bite-sized pieces and fold into the risotto.

steps.title: Prep chops
steps.text: Season the pork chops on both sides with salt and pepper. Dredge them in flour, shaking off any excess but setting the excess aside for the sauce.

steps.title: Sear in cast iron
steps.text: In a 12-inch cast-iron skillet over medium-high heat, melt 2 tablespoons butter until it foams. Add the chops to the hot pan and cook until their surfaces brown deeply and an instant-read thermometer shows 140° (inserted near but not touching the bone), 7–10 minutes per side. Transfer to a plate, tent loosely with foil, and rest 10 minutes.

steps.title: Build sauce base
steps.text: Melt 1 tablespoon butter in the same skillet over medium-high heat. Add the onions and garlic; cook until softened, 3–5 minutes. Stir in about 2 tablespoons of the reserved flour and cook for 1–2 minutes, stirring constantly.

steps.title: Finish sauce
steps.text: Deglaze the skillet with broth and cider, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom. Bring to a boil, reduce heat to medium, and simmer until the sauce thickens, about 5 minutes. Stir in the apples, vinegar, and minced sage; season with salt and pepper. Simmer until the apples begin to soften, about 3 minutes more.

steps.title: Complete dish
steps.text: Return the chops to the skillet along with any juices from the plate. Coat them well with the warm sauce and garnish with fresh sage leaves.

steps.title: Boil potatoes
steps.text: Boil the sweet potatoes in salted water until fork-tender, 10–15 minutes.

steps.title: Cook and dry
steps.text: Drain the potatoes and return them to the pot, then cook over medium-low heat, stirring, to evaporate the excess moisture, 1–2 minutes.

steps.title: Mash and season
steps.text: Off heat, add the butter, half-and-half, brown sugar, and cinnamon, then crush everything with a potato masher until you reach the consistency you want. Season with salt and pepper, then garnish with parsley.

steps.title: Prepare ingredients
steps.text: Segment the grapefruit, peel and slice the cucumber into half-moons, thinly slice the onion, and chop the parsley.

steps.title: Make vinaigrette
steps.text: Whisk the lemon juice, oil, honey, and Dijon together.

steps.title: Dress and season
steps.text: Toss the grapefruit, cucumber, onion, and parsley in a bowl with the vinaigrette, then season with salt and pepper.

steps.title: Cook and dry potatoes
steps.text: Boil the potatoes in salted water until fork-tender, 10–12 minutes, then drain. Cook them over medium-low heat, stirring, to remove the excess moisture, 1–2 minutes.

steps.title: Mash with cheese
steps.text: Stir in the half-and-half and butter, crushing with a potato masher until smooth, then add the cheese and scallions. Season with salt and cayenne.

steps.title: Build the filling
steps.text: Warm a 10-inch cast-iron skillet over medium with oil. Soften the onion, celery, carrot, and garlic in it, 5–7 minutes, then raise the heat to medium-high and add the ground sirloin. Brown it, 5–7 minutes more.

steps.title: Simmer until thick
steps.text: Stir in the rosemary, flour, and tomato paste, cook 1–2 minutes, then deglaze with wine, scraping the browned bits, and reduce until nearly evaporated. Add the broth, corn, green beans, and Worcestershire, bring to a boil, then simmer until the liquid reduces nearly away, 7–8 minutes. Transfer the skillet to a baking sheet.

steps.title: Broil until brown
steps.text: Preheat the broiler to high with the rack 6 inches from the element. Spread the potato topping over the filling and broil until the potatoes are browned, 3–4 minutes. Let the pie rest 5 minutes before serving.

steps.title: Prepare ingredients
steps.text: Chop the romaine into bite-sized pieces, halve the grapes, and measure the sunflower seeds.

steps.title: Make vinaigrette
steps.text: Whisk the oil, vinegar, honey, Dijon, and shallots together, then season with salt and pepper.

steps.title: Dress the salad
steps.text: Toss the romaine, grapes, and sunflower seeds in a large bowl with the vinaigrette.

steps.title: Simmer the figs
steps.text: Combine the figs, 2½ cups water, zest, orange juice, brandy, ¼ cup brown sugar, allspice, and ⅛ tsp. salt in a saucepan over medium-high. Bring to a boil until the sugar dissolves, then reduce to medium-low and simmer until the liquid evaporates and the figs soften enough to flatten easily with a spatula, about 1 hour, adding ¼ cup water at a time as needed.

steps.title: Process and cool
steps.text: Once the figs are tender enough to crush easily, run them through a food processor until completely smooth, then let the purée come to room temperature.

steps.title: Prepare the pan
steps.text: Fit your pan with a parchment sling — it makes lifting out the bars much easier — and coat it well with butter.

steps.title: Mix the crust
steps.text: Whisk together the flours, oats, walnuts, baking powder, and ½ tsp. salt.

steps.title: Cream the dough
steps.text: On medium speed with a mixer, blend the butter with the brown sugar (1 cup) and honey until pale and fluffy, 3–5 minutes. Then add the egg, yolk, and vanilla and mix until combined.

steps.title: Build and chill
steps.text: Mix in the flour mixture on low speed until just combined. Divide the dough in half; wrap one half in plastic and shape into a rectangle, then press the other half into the prepared pan. Chill both for at least 1 hour.

steps.title: Assemble and bake
steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350°. Lay out the remaining dough between two pieces of parchment, rolling it to a 9×13-inch rectangle, then freeze it until rigid. Lay that top dough over the fig filling already spread in the pan. Bake until golden and set on top, 35–40 minutes. Cool fully in the pan, then lift out by the parchment handles.

steps.title: Toast the bread
steps.text: Set the oven to 350° and ready a 9×13-inch baking dish with nonstick spray. Dry the bread on a baking sheet, 10 minutes each side, then transfer to a cooling rack and turn off the oven.

steps.title: Make the caramel
steps.text: Combine the brown sugar, butter, corn syrup, and salt in a saucepan and heat over medium until the butter melts. Raise the heat to medium-high, bring to a boil, and cook until the sugar dissolves, 2 minutes. Stir in the pecans and pour into the prepared dish.

steps.title: Soak the bread
steps.text: Whisk together the eggs, half-and-half, vanilla, and cinnamon, then dip both sides of each bread piece in the custard and arrange on top of the caramel.

steps.title: Chill overnight
steps.text: Spoon the remaining custard over the bread layer, cover with plastic wrap, and refrigerate for at least 2 hours or as long as overnight.

steps.title: Bake and invert
steps.text: Heat the oven to 350°. Take the casserole from the fridge and let it sit for about 30 minutes at room temperature, then peel off the plastic. Bake until the custard is set and registers 160° on a thermometer at the center, 40–45 minutes. Rest for 5 minutes, then flip the whole thing onto a serving platter with the caramel facing up. Top with whipped cream and bacon.

steps.title: Prepare aromatics
steps.text: Separate bok choy whites from greens. Mince the ginger and garlic. Slice the scallions, keeping whites and greens separate.

steps.title: Simmer broth base
steps.text: Combine the broth, bok choy whites, mirin, ginger, garlic, and scallion whites in a pot and bring to a boil over medium-high. Drop the heat to medium and let it simmer until the bok choy whites are tender, 5 minutes.

steps.title: Cook chicken and egg
steps.text: Raise the heat to high, stir in the bok choy greens and chicken, and simmer until cooked through, 2 minutes. Slowly pour in the eggs in a steady stream, let them sit 30 seconds, then stir to break them into pieces. Lower the heat to medium and let them cook 1 minute, then stir in the scallion greens and sesame oil. Season with pepper.

steps.title: Cook the noodles
steps.text: Following package directions, cook the noodles and set them aside.

steps.title: Build the broth
steps.text: Anchovies and both oils go into the pot together over medium-high. Give them about 3 minutes — they will collapse into the oil and all but disappear, which is the point. Garlic, minced chile and ½ cup of the pineapple follow, cooked only until they soften.

steps.title: Simmer with herbs
steps.text: Stir in the broth, vinegar, shallots, and lemongrass, bring to a boil, then reduce to medium and simmer 15–20 minutes. Discard the lemongrass, then stir in the noodles, remaining ½ cup pineapple, basil, mint, and cilantro.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Divide the steak among four bowls and ladle the soup over it. Garnish each serving with sliced chile.

steps.title: Mix dry
steps.text: Pulse the flour, sugar, parsley, thyme, salt, and pepper together in a food processor.

steps.title: Cut in fat
steps.text: Add the butter and shortening and pulse until they break into pea-sized bits. Sprinkle the water over in 2-Tbsp. additions, pulsing after each addition, until the dough just comes together.

steps.title: Rest and portion
steps.text: Tip it out and work it by hand only as long as it takes for the dry crumbs at the bottom of the bowl to come together. Split the dough into 8 for individual pies, or 2 for one large. Press each piece flat into a disc, wrap in plastic, and chill: 30 minutes at the least, 3 days at the most.

steps.title: Brown the mushrooms
steps.text: Melt the butter in a sauté pan over medium-high. Add the mushrooms, onions, and rosemary and thyme sprigs, then cook, stirring occasionally, until the mushrooms begin to brown, 8–10 minutes. Season with salt and pepper, then remove from heat and discard the herb sprigs.

steps.title: Render the bacon
steps.text: Cook the bacon in a sauté pan until crisp, then transfer to a paper-towel-lined plate and reserve the drippings.

steps.title: Brown the steak
steps.text: Toss the steak with the dried rosemary, 2 tsp. salt, and 2 tsp. pepper. Working in batches, sear the steak in the drippings over medium-high heat on all sides, 5–6 minutes per batch, then transfer to a plate.

steps.title: Make the sauce base
steps.text: Add the carrots, celery, and garlic to the pan, season with salt and pepper, cover, reduce to medium, and sweat until crisp-tender, 6–8 minutes. Stir in the tomato paste and cook 1 minute, then add the flour and cook 1 minute more.

steps.title: Build the filling
steps.text: Wine goes in next, straight into the hot pan so the fond lifts off the bottom; the broth follows. Bring it up hard to a boil, then drop it back to a simmer for 3–5 minutes — it is ready when it coats the back of a spoon. Off the heat, fold through the rosemary and thyme with the mushrooms, bacon and steak.

steps.title: Bottom crust
steps.text: Set one dough disc between 2 sheets of parchment and roll it into a 13-inch round. Press it into a 9-inch pie plate without stretching, then pour the filling in.

steps.title: Cover the filling
steps.text: The second disc gets the same treatment — parchment above and below, rolled to a 13-inch round — but this one goes over the filling. Leave a ½-inch overhang, press the edges together and tuck them under, crimp, and cut a slit in the top. Wrap and freeze. Pull it out 30 minutes before it bakes and unwrap it, but do not let it thaw.

steps.title: Bake until done
steps.text: Heat the oven to 425° and line a baking sheet with foil. Mix the egg with water and paint it over the crust. Set the pie on the sheet and bake until the crust is golden and a thermometer reads 165° at the center, 100–110 minutes, covering the edge with foil if it browns too fast. Rest 15 minutes before slicing.

steps.title: Dry mix
steps.text: Set oven to 425° and line a sheet with parchment. In a bowl, combine flour, cornmeal, granulated sugar, baking powder, and salt.

steps.title: Work in butter
steps.text: Dice cold butter and cut it through the flour mixture with your fingers or a pastry cutter until it resembles rough breadcrumbs, keeping some pea-sized lumps. Add cream and stir gently — stop as soon as the mixture holds together.

steps.title: Shape and finish
steps.text: Flour your work surface lightly. Press the dough into a compact disk about 8 inches across and 3/4-inch thick. Divide it into 8 equal wedges using a knife. Arrange them on the parchment, brush generously with honey, and top with sparkling sugar.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Bake 15–18 minutes until the tops brown. Cool for a few minutes on the sheet, or serve at room temperature.

steps.title: Oven and prep
steps.text: Start the oven at 425°. Line a baking sheet with parchment.

steps.title: Make spice coat
steps.text: In a small bowl, combine granulated sugar, 2 Tbsp brown sugar, 1/4 tsp salt, and cinnamon; set aside.

steps.title: Coat fruit
steps.text: Coat apples and pears with lemon juice to prevent browning, then dust them with the spice mixture.

steps.title: Assemble and bake
steps.text: Set puff pastry halves on the sheet and shingle the apple and pear slices over them, keeping a margin at the edge. Fold the edges in slightly to frame the fruit. Bake 20–25 minutes until the pastry browns and puffs.

steps.title: Caramel sauce
steps.text: As the tarts bake, combine 1/4 cup brown sugar, butter, cream, vanilla, and 1/8 tsp salt in a saucepan. Cook over medium-low heat, stirring now and then, until thick, 5–7 minutes. Pour over the baked tarts and top with pecans.

steps.title: Steam cauliflower
steps.text: Boil an inch of water in a pot fitted with a steamer basket. Set florets in and steam them, covered, tossing once or twice, until they soften, roughly 10 minutes. Drain into a bowl and season to taste with salt and pepper.

steps.title: Make roux and build sauce
steps.text: In a saucepan over medium heat, melt butter then work in flour to make a smooth paste. Gradually pour in half-and-half, beer, Dijon, and Worcestershire, whisking as you go. When the sauce is glossy and coats a spoon thickly, leaving a trail that does not disappear when swiped, 5–7 minutes total, reduce heat to low.

steps.title: Finish with cheese
steps.text: Pull from heat. Add Cheddar in handfuls, letting each batch melt before the next arrives. Adjust with salt, pepper, and a few drops of Tabasco. Ladle over the florets and top with fresh chives.

steps.title: Sweat aromatics
steps.text: Heat oil in a saucepan over medium. Add onion, anchovy paste, and oregano; cook until the onion softens and liquid evaporates, 5 minutes.

steps.title: Deepen with paste
steps.text: Stir in tomato paste and cook 1 minute, letting it caramelize slightly.

steps.title: Add tomatoes and simmer
steps.text: Add crushed tomatoes and tomato sauce; bring to a simmer and cook 10 minutes until the sauce thickens. Stir in vinegar, then season with salt and pepper.

steps.title: Build base in processor
steps.text: Set half the olives, parsley, basil, pecorino, and the orange and lemon zests plus honey in a food processor. Pulse to a rough chop.

steps.title: Wet it down
steps.text: Add the orange and lemon juice. Pulse again until the olives break down to a fine chop.

steps.title: Warm through
steps.text: Warm oil in a saucepan over medium. When it moves easily, add garlic and pepper flakes and let them release their perfume, 1 minute. Fold in the minced olive mixture and the remaining halved olives. Let everything warm through, 3–4 minutes, and finish with cracked pepper.

steps.title: Render pancetta
steps.text: In a sauté pan over medium-high heat, cook pancetta until the edges crisp. Lift to a paper towel and reserve the fat in the pan.

steps.title: Build aromatics and tomatoes
steps.text: Add oil to the pan if needed, then warm it gently. Sauté onion until it yields, 3–4 minutes. Stir in garlic and tomato paste; let them darken a bit, 1 minute. Add fresh tomatoes and give them 2–3 minutes to collapse.

steps.title: Deglaze and sauce
steps.text: Pour in vodka, scraping hard at the pan bottom to lift any stuck bits. Cook off most of the alcohol, about 3 minutes. Stir in cream and bring to a bubble; let it cook 1 minute. Off heat, fold in basil and the pancetta. Season with salt, black pepper, and red pepper flakes.

steps.title: Reduce cream base
steps.text: In a saucepan, combine cream and vermouth. Simmer gently over medium heat until it thickens and reduces slightly, roughly 10 minutes.

steps.title: Add cheese and finish
steps.text: Introduce Gorgonzola and Parmesan slowly, whisking as they melt in. Cook another 5 minutes until the sauce is glossy and dense. Whisk in lemon zest and juice, then adjust seasoning with salt, pepper, and a pinch of nutmeg.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Plate and scatter toasted walnuts and fresh parsley over each portion.

steps.title: Ready the oven and pans
steps.text: Start oven at 325°. Cut parchment to fit three 9×2-inch-round cake pans, then coat each pan well with nonstick spray, lay in a parchment round, and spray the paper too.

steps.title: Mix cake batter
steps.text: Sift flour, 1 cup sugar, baking powder, and 1/2 tsp salt together. In another bowl, whisk 6 egg yolks with 3/4 cup milk, oil, 4 Tbsp melted butter, and 1 Tbsp vanilla until smooth and pale. Fold in the dry mix, stirring just until no flour specks remain.

steps.title: Whip and fold egg whites
steps.text: In a clean bowl with a hand mixer, beat egg whites and cream of tartar on medium until pillowy peaks appear, 5 minutes. Crank to medium-high and rain in the remaining 1/4 cup sugar while beating, 3–4 minutes more, until glossy and firm peaks hold. In four turns, fold the whites into the batter, scraping the bowl between each addition, until no white streaks show.

steps.title: Bake cakes
steps.text: Split the batter among the pans. Bake 30 minutes, rotating the pans halfway, until the tops spring back when touched lightly and the cakes smell golden. Cool in the pans 10 minutes, then turn out onto racks and cool completely.

steps.title: Pastry cream foundation
steps.text: Whisk 6 egg yolks, cornstarch, 1/4 cup sugar, and liqueur until the yolks lighten. Warm 2½ cups milk and remaining 1/2 cup sugar in a saucepan until it just begins to bubble, 12 minutes. Remove from heat and stir in 4 oz chocolate until it dissolves.

steps.title: Cook pastry cream
steps.text: Pour half the chocolate-milk into the yolk mixture, whisking steadily, then return everything to the saucepan and return to medium heat. Whisk constantly until it thickens, 2–3 minutes. Take off heat. Stir in 1 Tbsp vanilla mixed with espresso powder, then 5 Tbsp butter and 1/4 tsp salt. Pour into a bowl, press plastic wrap flush to the surface, and refrigerate until chilled through, at least 2 hours.

steps.title: Prepare ganache
steps.text: In a saucepan, warm cream and corn syrup over medium until they shimmer. Remove from heat. Drop in 4 oz chocolate, let it sit 8 minutes undisturbed, then whisk until smooth and glossy. Stir in 1/2 tsp vanilla.

steps.title: Assemble and set
steps.text: Place one cake layer on a plate. Spread 1½ cups pastry cream over it, stopping short of the edge by 1/4 inch. Set the second layer on top, repeat the cream, then crown with the last layer. Pour ganache over the top and tilt to spread it gently to the edges. Let rest at room temperature 30 minutes before slicing.

steps.title: Make crema dressing
steps.text: Whisk together vinegar, crema, shallots, sugar, thyme, and Dijon in a small bowl. Season with salt and pepper. Set aside.

steps.title: Combine greens and vegetables
steps.text: In a large bowl, toss together romaine, nopales, queso fresco, and onion.

steps.title: Dress and serve
steps.text: Drizzle the salad with dressing and toss gently to coat. Serve immediately.

steps.title: Heat oven, coat pans
steps.text: Heat the oven to 400°. Coat two mini-muffin pans with nonstick spray and set them on a baking sheet.

steps.title: Dry mix
steps.text: Combine the cornmeal, flour, baking powder, sugar, and salt in a bowl.

steps.title: Wet and fold
steps.text: Whisk together the corn, sour cream, oil, and eggs in a large bowl. Add the dry mix and stir just until the batter comes together — do not overwork it.

steps.title: Bake and cool
steps.text: Fill every other well — this prevents uneven browning. For 15–20 minutes, bake until a toothpick pushed into the centers meets no batter. Cool them 5–10 minutes in the pans, then release.

steps.title: Heat skillet
steps.text: Have a 10-inch cast-iron skillet sitting on a baking sheet. Transfer it all to a 425° oven so the skillet heats through.

steps.title: Purée tomatoes
steps.text: Run the tomatoes (two cups), onion, and garlic through a food processor, pulsing until they turn nearly into a purée.

steps.title: Build sauce
steps.text: Heat oil in a saucepan over medium. Stir in chili powder, one tablespoon flour, and cumin; cook one minute. Whisk in the broth and tomato purée; bring to a boil. Drop the heat to medium-low and simmer until thickened, about 10 minutes, stirring now and then. Season with salt and pepper, then cool. Reserve half a cup of sauce, then stir the remaining cup of tomatoes and chicken into what's left.

steps.title: Cornbread batter
steps.text: Combine the cornmeal, half a cup flour, baking powder, sugar, and one teaspoon salt.

steps.title: Fold in wet
steps.text: Whisk together the buttermilk, melted butter, and egg. Fold in the dry mix just until combined, then stir in the corn and green chiles.

steps.title: Assemble and bake
steps.text: Melt one tablespoon butter in the preheated skillet and carefully pour in the batter. Bake 20 minutes. Poke holes all over the cornbread, spread the reserved sauce on top, then add the chicken mixture. Sprinkle cheese over and bake until the cheese melts, about 10 minutes.

steps.title: Combine base
steps.text: Toss together the beans, corn, radishes, and scallions in a bowl.

steps.title: Garlic paste
steps.text: Crush the garlic on a cutting board with a quarter teaspoon of salt, then press and drag it with the flat of the knife blade until it becomes a paste — this is the reliable way.

steps.title: Dress and chill
steps.text: Whisk together the zest, lemon juice, oil, and garlic paste, then pour over the beans and toss. Season with salt and pepper and chill until you are ready to serve.

steps.title: Heat pan
steps.text: Heat oil in a large sauté pan over medium-high.

steps.title: Build base
steps.text: Add onion and pepperoni and sauté until the onions soften, about 4 minutes. Stir in garlic, pepper flakes, and basil; cook until fragrant, one minute. Stir in tomato paste to coat everything and sauté one minute more.

steps.title: Simmer and finish
steps.text: Pour in the tomatoes, vodka, bay leaf, and salt. Use a spoon to break the tomatoes into chunks. Bring to a boil, then turn the heat down to medium-low and simmer until the volume drops by a third, about 30 minutes. Pull out the bay leaf. Stir in the vinegar, cream, and Parmesan to finish.

steps.title: Blend base
steps.text: Combine in a blender: milk, ricotta, yogurt, onion, garlic, salt, and nutmeg. Process until completely smooth. Pour into a covered container and keep in the fridge for up to a week if not using right away.

steps.title: Cook roux
steps.text: Warm the oil in a large sauté pan over medium heat. Sprinkle in the flour and whisk until smooth.

steps.title: Build sauce
steps.text: Whisk in the blended mixture until smooth. Simmer the sauce until it thickens, about 8 minutes. Stir in Parmigiano-Reggiano and zest, then season with pepper and serve.

steps.title: Brown meat
steps.text: Heat oil in a large sauté pan over medium-high. Add turkey breast and sausage, breaking them into smaller chunks, and cook until browned.

steps.title: Soften vegetables
steps.text: Process the onion, carrot, celery, and garlic in a food processor until minced; add to the browned meat. Cook the vegetables until softened, about 5 minutes. Process the cottage cheese in the food processor until smooth, about 2 minutes, then stir it into the meat mixture.

steps.title: Build sauce
steps.text: Stir in tomato paste and cook one minute. Add tomatoes, wine, vinegar, oregano, basil, salt, and pepper flakes. Drop the heat to medium-low and simmer the sauce for 40–45 minutes, stirring from time to time. Add the neufchâtel, stirring until melted, then stir in parsley.

steps.title: Combine fruit and vegetables
steps.text: Toss the mangoes, onion, bell peppers, and cilantro together in a bowl.

steps.title: Add citrus
steps.text: Pour in the orange and lime juices and toss to coat.

steps.title: Season and serve
steps.text: Season with salt and pepper to taste and serve.

steps.title: Prepare spice coating
steps.text: Heat the oven to 450°. Whisk together oil, cumin, coriander, salt, and pepper in a large bowl until combined.

steps.title: Coat and roast
steps.text: Add the cauliflower and toss to coat every piece. Transfer to a baking sheet and roast, stirring halfway through, until tender and golden brown, 20–30 minutes.

steps.title: Finish and serve
steps.text: Remove from the oven, season with salt and pepper, and serve with lemon wedges.

steps.title: Make aioli
steps.text: Whisk together mayonnaise, garlic, paprika, zest, and orange juice in a bowl.

steps.title: Cook chorizo
steps.text: Brown the chorizo in a skillet, about 5 minutes; drain on a paper towel.

steps.title: Heat oil
steps.text: In a 7- to 8-quart pot, bring peanut oil to temperature over high heat; use a candy thermometer to check for 375°.

steps.title: Slice potatoes
steps.text: Slice the potatoes into quarter-inch-thick rounds using a mandoline or sharp knife.

steps.title: Fry chips
steps.text: Fry potatoes in six batches until golden, about 4 minutes per batch. The oil temperature will drop; let it recover between batches. Drain on paper towels, season with salt, and serve warm with the aioli and chorizo on top.

steps.title: Make vinaigrette
steps.text: Whisk together champagne vinegar, shallots, and honey in a bowl. Drizzle in oil while whisking until emulsified.

steps.title: Toss greens
steps.text: Toss spinach and arugula together with the desired amount of vinaigrette and season with salt and pepper.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Divide among plates and serve immediately.

steps.title: Make custard
steps.text: In a large bowl, combine eggs, whole milk, coconut milk, 1 cup sugar, currants, and 1 Tbsp vanilla by whisking together.

steps.title: Soak bread
steps.text: Add bread to the custard and stir until combined. Leave at room temperature uncovered for 30-45 minutes to soak.

steps.title: Bake pudding
steps.text: Coat a 9×13-inch baking dish with 2 tsp butter. Pour in the bread custard. Whisk together 3 Tbsp sugar and 2 tsp cinnamon and spread over top. Place in a 350° oven for 1 hour until the centre is firm. Cool on a rack 20-30 minutes.

steps.title: Cook sauce
steps.text: In a saucepan over medium, combine 1 stick butter with brown sugar and whisk constantly for about 2 minutes until melted and smooth. Add cream, rum, ½ tsp cinnamon, and salt; bring to a simmer and cook 5 more minutes until thickened and reduced to 1½ cups.

steps.title: Finish sauce
steps.text: Off heat, fold in pecans, coconut, 1 tsp vanilla, and lemon juice. Serve warm spooned over the pudding.

steps.title: Prepare batter
steps.text: Combine cornmeal, scallions, jalapeño, garlic, salt, and pepper in a bowl. Whisk beer, buttermilk, and egg; stir into the dry mixture. Set oven to 450°.

steps.title: Fry fish
steps.text: Get oil shimmering in a 10-inch cast-iron skillet over high heat. Coat each fish piece in fish-fry mix and fry on one side only for 2 minutes.

steps.title: Bake with topping
steps.text: Spread the hush puppy batter over the fish directly in the skillet. Move to the oven and bake 15 minutes until golden brown and a toothpick in the centre comes out clean. Let rest 5 minutes.

steps.title: Turn out
steps.text: Run a knife around the edges to loosen. Set a serving plate over the hot skillet and flip both together quickly—keep your hands back, it's very hot.

steps.title: Make sauce
steps.text: Stir together ketchup, mayonnaise, relish, and horseradish.

steps.title: Make filling
steps.text: Stir bananas into mascarpone and set aside.

steps.title: Prepare bread
steps.text: Slice four bread slices horizontally three-quarters through to make pockets. Pulse the two remaining slices until fine breadcrumbs; spread on a shallow plate.

steps.title: Stuff and coat
steps.text: Divide the banana-mascarpone filling between the bread pockets. Whisk creamer and eggs together. Dunk each stuffed slice in the egg mix—about 1 minute each side—then roll in crumbs, pressing them on.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Melt butter on a griddle or nonstick skillet over medium. Brown the stuffed slices golden on both sides, 3-4 minutes per side.

steps.title: Warm sauce
steps.text: Microwave the hazelnut spread, stirring every 20 seconds, for about 1 minute until pourable. Spoon over the cooked toast.

steps.title: Make caramel
steps.text: In a saucepan over medium, combine ½ cup sugar, water, corn syrup, and salt. Stir until sugar dissolves. Brush down the sides with a wet pastry brush to prevent crystals. Turn heat to medium-high and cook at a boil until the colour is deep amber, 10-15 minutes.

steps.title: Melt chocolate
steps.text: Combine milk chocolate and semisweet chips with ½ tsp espresso powder in a bowl.

steps.title: Make ganache
steps.text: Into a bowl with ¾ cup cream and butter, pour the hot caramel—it will bubble vigorously. Whisk until the butter melts and the whole thing comes back to a boil, then pour over the chocolate. Let rest 1 minute. Add vanilla and whisk until completely smooth. Cool to room temperature, whisking occasionally.

steps.title: Cheese layer
steps.text: Whisk together mascarpone, 2 Tbsp sugar, Marsala, and 1 tsp espresso powder until light and smooth. Fit a piping bag with a medium tip and fill it with this mixture.

steps.title: Assemble trifles
steps.text: In each trifle dish, layer 2 tsp ganache, then about 1 Tbsp cheese, then 1 Tbsp ladyfingers, then ½ tsp pine nuts. Repeat the entire layer once. Top with 2 tsp ganache and 1 tsp cheese. Serve right away.

steps.title: Heat oil
steps.text: Get oil to 350° in a large pot—use a candy thermometer to check.

steps.title: Prepare sugar
steps.text: Combine ½ cup sugar, cinnamon, and cardamom on a wide shallow plate.

steps.title: Make dough
steps.text: In a sauté pan over medium, melt butter with water, 2 tsp sugar, salt, and zest. When it boils, stir in flour until the mixture pulls away from the pan walls. Cook 1 more minute and transfer to a bowl.

steps.title: Beat dough
steps.text: With a hand mixer on medium, beat dough 30 seconds. Add eggs one at a time, beating between additions until each one is incorporated and dough turns shiny. Transfer to a piping bag with a star tip. Let cool while you make the chocolate.

steps.title: Make hot chocolate
steps.text: In a small saucepan over high heat, cook brandy down until almost dry, 7-9 minutes. Drop heat to medium and add cream and ¼ cup sugar, whisking. Heat until steam rises and bubbles form around the edges.

steps.title: Thicken chocolate
steps.text: Mix milk and cornstarch smooth, then pour slowly into the cream and sugar. Bring to a simmer and cook 1 minute, stirring constantly. Whisk in chocolate until fully incorporated.

steps.title: Fry churros
steps.text: Squeeze 3-inch dough strips into the hot oil, cutting from the piping tip with an oiled knife as you go. Fry until both sides turn golden brown, about 4 minutes total. Drain on a paper-towel-lined plate and immediately toss in the spiced sugar mixture.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Bring churros and hot chocolate to the table hot.

steps.title: Cook noodles
steps.text: Cook noodles in salted boiling water following the package. Drain and rinse under cold water.

steps.title: Make dashi
steps.text: In a large saucepan over medium-high, bring water and kombu to near boiling—about 10 minutes. Remove kombu. Add bonito flakes and simmer, then remove from heat and let rest 5 minutes until most flakes have sunk.

steps.title: Strain broth
steps.text: Pour through a sieve into a bowl; discard the solids. Whisk miso into 1 cup of the warm broth in a small bowl until smooth, then stir this back into the full amount of broth.

steps.title: Cook vegetables
steps.text: In the same saucepan over medium, warm oil and add shiitake mushrooms and scallion whites. Cook 5 minutes until mushrooms soften. Stir in ginger and garlic and cook 1 minute more until fragrant.

steps.title: Simmer soup
steps.text: Pour in the miso broth and add tofu; simmer 10 minutes. Off heat, drop in chard and let it wilt.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Put noodles in bowls and ladle soup over top. Scatter scallion greens and sliced radishes on each.

steps.title: Prepare greens
steps.text: Combine mushrooms, spinach, shallots, parsley, and mint in a large bowl.

steps.title: Cook bacon
steps.text: In a large sauté pan over medium-high, render bacon until it crisps. Set on a paper-towel-lined plate and toss into the salad.

steps.title: Sear steak
steps.text: In the same pan, use the bacon fat to sear the steak to your liking—6-7 minutes per side gives medium-rare. Rest 5 minutes before slicing thin against the grain.

steps.title: Plate and serve
steps.text: Mound salad on four plates and lay steak slices over top. Pass Lemon Pepper Vinaigrette on the side.

steps.title: Prepare breading
steps.text: Combine cornmeal, cumin, coriander, salt, black pepper, and cayenne.

steps.title: Heat oil
steps.text: Get oil hot in a large sauté pan over medium-high.

steps.title: Coat fish
steps.text: Thin the egg whites with water in a small bowl. Slice fillets into 2-inch lengths and ½-inch-wide strips. Dip in cornmeal, then egg white, then cornmeal a second time.

steps.title: Fry and drain
steps.text: Fry in batches until golden; drain on paper towels.

steps.title: Assemble salad
steps.text: Mix cabbage, cucumber, tomatoes, radishes, and cilantro and divide among four bowls. Top each with the fried fish and pass Creamy Jalapeño Dressing at table.

steps.title: Prepare pan
steps.text: Set oven to 400°. Spray a 2-qt ovenproof baking dish with nonstick cooking spray.

steps.title: Make topping
steps.text: Stir breadcrumbs, parsley, and melted butter together. Season with salt and pepper.

steps.title: Cook pasta
steps.text: In salted boiling water, cook pasta to al dente. Drain well.

steps.title: Brown kielbasa
steps.text: Get oil hot in a large skillet over medium-high and brown kielbasa, about 5 minutes. Set aside on a paper-towel-lined plate.

steps.title: Toast seeds
steps.text: In the same pot, melt 2 Tbsp butter over medium. Add shallots and caraway seeds and cook until the seeds smell toasted, 3 minutes.

steps.title: Make sauce
steps.text: Sprinkle flour over the shallots and whisk to coat; cook 1 minute. Pour in milk and whisk over gentle heat for 5-8 minutes until the sauce thickens a bit. Lower heat to low. Add cheeses a handful at a time, stirring each one smooth before the next goes in.

steps.title: Assemble and bake
steps.text: Fold in Dijon and Worcestershire, then fold in pasta and kielbasa. Tip into the baking dish and sprinkle the crumb topping over. Bake 20-25 minutes until bubbly and the crumbs are brown. Let rest 5 minutes.

steps.title: Prepare packets
steps.text: Heat oven to 400°. Crease two parchment sheets (18 to 24 inches) down the middle and coat the interior surfaces with olive oil.

steps.title: Assemble
steps.text: Stir together tomatoes, onion, olives, capers, lemon juice, and garlic. Divide this between the parchment sheets, placing it oil-side up near the fold. Lay fillets over the mixture and top with sliced jalapeño and lemon.

steps.title: Seal and bake
steps.text: Fold the open edge of each packet closed and tie with kitchen string, tucking the ends under. Set on a baking sheet and bake 20 minutes until the parcels steam and puff.

steps.title: Avocado butter
steps.text: Whizz avocado with cilantro, scallions, lemon juice, oil, and salt in a food processor until spreadable — takes about 1 minute.

steps.title: Toast the bread
steps.text: Get the broiler going with rack 6 inches from the heat. Mix Parmesan, oil, garlic, salt, and pepper flakes in a bowl. Coat ½-inch baguette slices and lay on foil. Broil until golden, about 1 minute.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Top each slice with avocado butter and garnish with jalapeño. Serve.

steps.title: Toast the grain
steps.text: Heat oil in a saucepan over medium-high and add couscous, stirring, for 1 minute.

steps.title: Simmer
steps.text: Pour in water, raisins, and salt; bring to a boil. Cover, drop the heat to low, and cook until al dente, 9–10 minutes.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Off the heat, stir in scallions, zest, and lemon juice. Season with pepper. Top each serving with toasted walnuts.

steps.title: Preheat
steps.text: Set oven to 350°. Line a baking sheet with foil and lightly oil an 8-inch cast-iron skillet.

steps.title: Make dough
steps.text: In a saucepan, combine masa harina with water and salt. Place over medium-high heat and stir constantly, cooking until the mixture becomes very thick and comes away from the sides, about 6 minutes. Transfer onto the prepared baking sheet and let cool until you can touch it. Press into the oiled skillet and bake for 30 minutes, keeping oven on.

steps.title: Bean layer
steps.text: Toast garlic powder, cumin, oregano, and coriander in oil in a skillet over medium until fragrant, 30 seconds. Add beans and heat through, about 1 minute. Spread into the crust.

steps.title: Meat layer
steps.text: In the same skillet, sauté diced onion in oil over high heat, 1 minute. Add ground chuck and cook until done, 5 minutes. Drain all but 2 Tbsp. drippings. Stir in chipotle, adobo, and chili powder; season with salt and pepper. Spread over the beans.

steps.title: Avocado topping
steps.text: In a food processor, blend avocado, cream cheese, cilantro, lime juice, and minced garlic until creamy and smooth. Adjust the seasoning with salt and pepper, then spread a generous layer over the assembled pie.

steps.title: Garnish and serve
steps.text: Top with shredded Cheddar, romaine lettuce, corn chips, pico de gallo, and sour cream. Serve warm or at room temperature.

steps.title: Render bacon
steps.text: Cook bacon in a sauté pan over medium-high heat until crisp. Transfer to paper towels and set aside. Reserve the drippings.

steps.title: Make filling
steps.text: In a bowl, combine softened cream cheese, jalapeño, Jack cheese, scallions, cumin, coriander, and crumbled bacon using a hand mixer on medium speed until everything is evenly distributed. Taste and season generously with salt and pepper.

steps.title: Fry and serve
steps.text: For each tortilla, distribute ¼ cup filling across it edge to edge. Fold it closed with seam facing down, then lay in the pan with the bacon drippings. Fry over medium heat in batches until the tortillas turn golden brown — about 5 minutes. Once crispy and cooked through, slice each into thirds. Set out with pico de gallo and guacamole.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.text: Preheat oven to 350°. Line baking sheets with parchment.

steps.title: Dry mix
steps.text: Whisk flour, 1 cup crushed potato chips, baking powder, and salt in a bowl. Set aside.

steps.title: Cream
steps.text: In a large bowl, use a mixer on medium speed to combine shortening, granulated sugar, and brown sugar until light and fluffy — this takes 3–5 minutes. Add eggs and vanilla extract and beat until everything is incorporated. Fold in the flour mixture gently until just combined.

steps.title: Fold in
steps.text: Fold 2 cups coarsely-crushed potato chips and pecans into the dough gently.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Using a #30 scoop (2 Tbsp.), portion dough onto prepared baking sheets. Bake 12–14 minutes — they're done when edges just begin to set. Leave on the sheets 2 minutes, then move to a wire rack to cool completely.

steps.title: Cook pasta
steps.text: Bring salted water to a boil and add ditalini. Cook following package directions until al dente. Drain well.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Immediately stir in butter, parsley, and lemon zest. The residual heat will melt the butter into the pasta.

steps.title: Season
steps.text: Taste for salt and pepper and adjust. Serve straightaway.

steps.title: Cook rice
steps.text: Combine water, chicken broth, and rice in a saucepan and bring to a boil. Cover, drop heat to low, and cook according to package directions until liquid is absorbed and rice is tender.

steps.title: Finish with herbs
steps.text: Off the heat, fold in cilantro, minced bell pepper, and lime zest. Fluff gently.

steps.title: Season
steps.text: Taste and adjust salt and pepper.

steps.title: Make dressing
steps.text: Whisk olive-oil mayo and fresh lemon juice together in a medium bowl until combined.

steps.title: Mix filling
steps.text: Fold in drained tuna, sliced scallions, diced bell pepper, and kalamata olives. Stir until incorporated.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Divide among pita pockets lined with green leaf lettuce, or mound on a bed of greens.

steps.title: Prepare pan
steps.text: Set the oven to 350° and start preheating. Prepare an 8-inch square baking pan by coating it generously with nonstick spray.

steps.title: Toast
steps.text: Scatter oats and almonds across a baking sheet in a single layer, then place in the oven and toast until deep golden brown, about 10 minutes.

steps.title: Melt binder
steps.text: Heat peanut butter, honey, and vanilla in a saucepan over medium until the peanut butter is melted and the mixture is fluid.

steps.title: Mix and press
steps.text: In a large bowl, combine cereal, dried cherries, salt, toasted oats, and almonds. Pour in the peanut butter mixture and stir until everything is coated. Press into the prepared pan.

steps.title: Chill and cut
steps.text: Set in the fridge to firm up, 10–15 minutes. Once set, cut into bars and wrap each one in plastic wrap.

steps.title: Potato base
steps.text: Boil potatoes in salted water until fork-tender, about 15 minutes. Press through a ricer until completely smooth. Reserve 1½ cups of the cooking water and let both cool to 105°–115°.

steps.title: Start the dough
steps.text: Whisk yeast, sugar, mashed potatoes, and reserved water in a stand mixer bowl; let it stand 10 minutes until foamy.

steps.title: Mix and knead
steps.text: Add 4½ cups flour, salt, and oil. Mix on low with the paddle, then switch to the dough hook and knead on medium speed for 5–8 minutes until the dough pulls away from the bowl sides. It will be wet and sticky.

steps.title: First rise
steps.text: Put the dough into an oiled bowl and cover it with plastic wrap. Set in a warm spot to rise until it has nearly doubled, about 1 hour.

steps.title: Shape and second rise
steps.text: Generously oil two 8¼×11¾-inch baking sheets and press the dough evenly out to the edges. If the dough resists, cover and let it relax for 10 minutes before you try again. Top with kitchen towels and let it rise until puffy, 1–2 hours.

steps.title: Dimple and bake
steps.text: Have your oven at 425° with a baking stone inside. Using your fingertips, make shallow indentations all over the dough surface. Coat with olive oil and sea salt. Bake until deep gold, 20–25 minutes. Let it cool on a rack; eat it the same day.

steps.title: Graham crust
steps.text: Set your oven to 325°. In a food processor, work graham crackers, sugar, and salt until fine crumbs form. Drizzle melted butter over the top and pulse just until the mixture binds. Press firmly into the bottom and up the sides of a 9-inch springform pan. Bake for 10 minutes.

steps.title: Chocolate layer
steps.text: Melt chocolate with 2 tablespoons butter and espresso powder in a double boiler. Let it cool slightly before using.

steps.title: Fill
steps.text: In a stand mixer, whip cream cheese and sugar until the mixture is smooth and pale, scraping the bowl often. One at a time, add the eggs and beat well after each addition. Fold the cooled chocolate into the batter, then fold in the whipped cream and vanilla. Pour into your crust.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Bake until the edges have set but the very center still jiggles slightly when you move the pan, 40–45 minutes.

steps.title: Cool gently
steps.text: Turn off the oven and prop the door shut. Leave the cheesecake inside for 30 minutes, then remove it and let it cool all the way down. Cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, preferably overnight.

steps.title: Ganache
steps.text: Pour ½ cup cream into a microwave-safe bowl and heat on high until it boils, 1–2 minutes. Add chocolate chips, wait 2 minutes, then stir until glossy and smooth. Let it cool for 5 minutes.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Unhinge and remove the springform ring. Swirl ganache across the top of the cheesecake and crown it with fresh raspberries and chocolate curls.

steps.title: Simmer fruit
steps.text: In a medium saucepan over medium-high heat, combine cherries, wine, sugar, and salt. Bring to a boil, then drop the heat to a gentle simmer and cook for 10 minutes.

steps.title: Thicken
steps.text: In a small bowl, mix cornstarch with a tablespoon of cherry juice until smooth, then stir this slurry into the simmering sauce. Cook until it thickens slightly, about 2 minutes more.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Remove from heat and stir in almond extract. Taste for seasoning and serve warm with chocolate cheesecake.

steps.title: Toast aromatics
steps.text: Heat oil in a saucepan over medium-high heat. Cook shallots, stirring often, until they soften, about 3 minutes.

steps.title: Cook rice
steps.text: Pour in water and broth and bring to a boil. Add rice and ancho chile, cover the pan, drop the heat to medium-low, and simmer until the liquid is absorbed, 15–20 minutes.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Fold in the sun-dried tomatoes and season with salt and pepper to taste.

steps.title: Toast spice
steps.text: Toast pepitas and cumin seeds in a nonstick pan over medium heat for about 5 minutes until fragrant. Remove and set aside.

steps.title: Cook beans
steps.text: In a large skillet, warm oil over medium-high heat and add onion. Once it begins to soften, 1–2 minutes, add green beans and bell pepper. Cook for 3–4 minutes more, then drizzle with honey and vinegar.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Scatter the cumin pepitas over the vegetables and toss everything together. Taste and season with salt and pepper.

steps.title: Simmer rice
steps.text: Bring coconut water to a boil in a large saucepan. Stir in rice, butter, and salt and return to a boil.

steps.title: Add aromatics
steps.text: Cover the pan, drop the heat to low, and simmer gently until the rice is tender and the liquid is gone, 15–20 minutes. Stir in the raisins and scallions.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Fold in shredded coconut and taste. Adjust the seasoning with salt and pepper.

steps.title: Make sauce
steps.text: In a food processor, combine sour cream, coconut, scallions, jelly, ginger, lime juice, and ¼ teaspoon jerk seasoning. Pulse until smooth and well combined.

steps.title: Season sauce
steps.text: Taste and season with salt and pepper. Transfer to a serving bowl.

steps.title: Fries
steps.text: Cook the sweet potato fries following the package instructions. When they're hot off the heat, toss them with jerk seasoning, salt, and pepper. Serve alongside the sauce.

steps.title: Toast peanuts
steps.text: In a large nonstick skillet over medium heat, toast the peanuts until aromatic, about 3 minutes. Remove and set aside.

steps.title: Cook rice
steps.text: In the same skillet, bring rice and broth to a boil over medium-high heat. Cover, drop to medium-low, and simmer until the liquid is absorbed, 15–18 minutes.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Return the peanuts to the skillet. Stir in scallions and lime juice and season with salt and pepper.

steps.title: Cook cauliflower
steps.text: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add cauliflower florets and cook until very tender, about 12 minutes. Drain thoroughly and return to the pot.

steps.title: Mash
steps.text: Work the cauliflower with a potato masher or ricer until completely smooth. Set over low heat, then stir in olive oil and minced garlic. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Fold in the manzanilla olives. Season with pepper and a squeeze of lemon juice.

steps.title: Cook potatoes
steps.text: Peel and cut potatoes into chunks. Boil them in salted water until fork-tender, about 15 minutes. Drain thoroughly and return to the pot.

steps.title: Mash
steps.text: Work the potatoes with a masher or ricer until completely smooth.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Set the pot over low heat and fold in Greek yogurt, grated Gouda cheese, and butter. Taste and season with salt and white pepper.

steps.title: Anchovy-garlic base
steps.text: In a large bowl, whisk together red wine vinegar, minced garlic, and anchovy paste until the paste dissolves completely into the vinegar.

steps.title: Emulsify with oil
steps.text: Slowly drizzle in olive oil while whisking constantly to form an emulsion. Season with salt and pepper.

steps.title: Dress and toss
steps.text: Add lettuce, artichoke hearts, roasted peppers, and red onion to the bowl. Toss everything until the leaves and vegetables are evenly coated with vinaigrette.

steps.title: Blanch and shock
steps.text: Cook trimmed beans in plenty of boiling salted water until they yield slightly when pressed, 5 minutes. Transfer straight to ice water, let them cool completely, then drain.

steps.title: Warm butter and garlic
steps.text: In a sauté pan over medium heat, warm butter until it foams. Add sliced garlic and cook gently for 2 minutes until soft and sweet.

steps.title: Heat and season
steps.text: Toss the blanched beans into the garlic butter to heat through, about 3 minutes. Season with salt and pepper to taste.

steps.title: Plump the cherries
steps.text: Pour hot apple cider over dried tart cherries in a bowl and leave them to soak for 15–20 minutes until softened.

steps.title: Cook the apples
steps.text: Melt butter in a sauté pan over medium-high heat. Add sliced apples and fresh thyme; cook until the apples are crisp-tender, about 5 minutes.

steps.title: Simmer and season
steps.text: Pour the cherries and their soaking liquid into the pan and bring to a boil. Reduce heat and simmer until the mixture thickens slightly, about 3 minutes. Add cider vinegar and season with salt and pepper.

steps.title: Bloom the garlic
steps.text: Heat oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Add minced garlic and cook until fragrant, about 1 minute — do not brown it.

steps.title: Toast the orzo
steps.text: Add dry orzo to the pan and stir constantly, coating each grain in oil, for 2 minutes.

steps.title: Simmer with broth
steps.text: Pour in chicken broth, cover the pan, and reduce heat to low. Simmer gently until the orzo is tender and the liquid is mostly absorbed, 10–15 minutes.

steps.title: Add tomatoes and zest
steps.text: Off the heat, stir in cherry tomatoes, parsley, and lemon zest. Season with salt and pepper.

steps.title: Make the vinaigrette
steps.text: Whisk together oil, fresh orange juice, red wine vinegar, orange zest, and honey in a bowl. Season with salt and pepper.

steps.title: Toss the greens
steps.text: Combine arugula, sliced red onion, and chopped pistachios in a large bowl.

steps.title: Dress and finish
steps.text: Crumble goat cheese over the greens, pour on the vinaigrette, and toss to coat. Top with halved fresh or dried figs just before serving.

steps.title: Caramelize the sauce
steps.text: In a large sauté pan, warm butter over medium heat until it foams. Stir in brown sugar, banana liqueur, rum, vanilla extract, cinnamon, and salt. Whisk constantly until the mixture thickens and darkens slightly, about 3 minutes.

steps.title: Cook the bananas
steps.text: Stir in banana slices and golden raisins. Cook gently until the bananas are tender but still hold their shape, about 1 minute.

steps.title: Serve over ice cream
steps.text: Chill eight serving glasses. Pour the warm banana mixture into each glass over a scoop of vanilla ice cream. Crown with toasted pecans and a pinch of cinnamon.

steps.title: Prepare and mix wet
steps.text: Set oven to 400° with a 12-cup muffin pan preheating inside. In a bowl, whisk eggs, melted butter, sour cream, and creamed corn together and set aside.

steps.title: Combine dry ingredients
steps.text: In another bowl, combine cornmeal, all-purpose flour, baking powder, salt, and cayenne pepper.

steps.title: Fold in okra and fill
steps.text: Whisk dry into wet just until the ingredients are combined — do not overmix. Fold sliced okra into the batter. Pull the hot pan from the oven, spray each cup lightly with nonstick spray, and divide batter among the cups.

steps.title: Bake and cool
steps.text: Place in the oven and bake for 20 minutes; a toothpick should come out clean when the centers are done. Cool in the pan for 5 minutes before turning out.

steps.title: Blanch and ice bath
steps.text: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and add broccoli florets. Cook for 20–30 seconds only — they should still be bright green. Transfer to a bowl of ice water, drain well, and set aside.

steps.title: Mix the salad
steps.text: Combine broccoli, sweet pickled onions, currants, sunflower seeds, and crumbled cooked bacon in a large bowl.

steps.title: Dress and toss
steps.text: Whisk together the pickled onion liquid, mayonnaise, and celery seeds in a small bowl. Season with salt and pepper. Pour dressing over the broccoli salad and toss to coat thoroughly.

steps.title: Prepare the dry mix
steps.text: Start by heating your oven to 400° and lining a baking sheet with parchment. In a bowl, whisk flour, baking powder, salt, pepper, and baking soda together. Rub cold diced butter into the flour with your fingertips until the largest pieces are no bigger than a pea.

steps.title: Mix the wet
steps.text: Whisk together buttermilk, egg, parsley, thyme, sage, rosemary, and minced garlic in a small bowl.

steps.title: Combine and shape
steps.text: Pour the wet ingredients into the dry and stir with a fork just until a shaggy dough forms. Scoop onto the prepared baking sheet using a #12 scoop (½ cup portions), spacing them about 2 inches apart.

steps.title: Bake and finish
steps.text: Bake until golden on the bottom, about 35 minutes. Brush with melted butter, sprinkle with salt, and bake 2 minutes more. Cool on a rack.

steps.title: Soften the wrappers
steps.text: Fill a shallow bowl with hot water. Soak spring roll wrappers in it one at a time, 30 seconds each, until pliable. Transfer to a damp towel as they soften.

steps.title: Fill each roll
steps.text: Place 3 mint leaves in the center of each wrapper. Layer shredded carrot, cilantro leaves, julienned apple, chopped scallions, julienned cucumber, lime zest, and chopped peanuts on top. Squeeze a little lime juice over the vegetables.

steps.title: Roll and rest
steps.text: Start from the edge nearest you and roll the wrapper tightly up and over the filling. Once the filling is enclosed, fold the sides in to seal them, then complete the roll. Lay seam-side down on a damp towel and cover with another damp towel.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Cut each roll in half on the bias and serve immediately with soy sauce for dipping.

steps.title: Roast squash
steps.text: Heat your oven to 400°. Toss squash chunks with oil and season well with salt and pepper. Spread them on a foil-lined sheet and roast until the edges brown, 25–30 minutes. Let them cool.

steps.title: Make dressing
steps.text: Crush garlic with 1/2 tsp. salt into a paste. Whisk the paste with mayonnaise, buttermilk, lime juice, honey, and chipotle in a medium bowl until it breaks down smooth. Chill it while the squash cools.

steps.title: Dress and finish
steps.text: Toss the escarole with the dressing. Scatter the roasted squash and cranberries over the top. Finish with pine nuts.

steps.title: Heat oil
steps.text: Bring peanut oil to 365° in a large skillet over medium-high heat.

steps.title: Coat shallots
steps.text: Toss the shallots with flour in a bowl, breaking them into separate rings as you go.

steps.title: Fry and drain
steps.text: Working in batches, fry the floured shallots in the hot oil until they begin to crisp and brown, about 2 minutes per batch. Lift them out onto a paper-towel-lined bowl to drain.

steps.title: Season
steps.text: In a bowl, combine salt, cumin, anise seed, and pepper. Use this mixture to season the shallots to your taste.

steps.title: Process sausage
